stories.title: BJP’s special strategy for 91 SP-dominated seats:Will finalise candidates only after Akhilesh’s list; 3 formulas to counter PDA
stories.summary: BJP has started preparations for selecting candidates for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. The party is also focusing on 91 seats considered Samajwadi Party strongholds. These are constituencies with a significant number of Muslim and Yadav voters. The BJP is unlikely to rush its decisions on these seats. The party is following a 'wait and watch' strategy, which means it will decide its candidates only after the Samajwadi Party (SP) announces its nominees. According to party sources, after the SP declares its candidates, the BJP will assess their caste background, local influence and political standing in their respective constituencies. It will then try to field candidates who can challenge Akhilesh Yadav's PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) social coalition. The BJP is working on three possible formulas for this: If the SP fields a Yadav or Muslim candidate in a constituency, the BJP may nominate someone from a non-Yadav OBC community, such as Kurmi, Maurya, Shakya, Saini, Nishad or Pal. The party may also place its bet on a strong upper-caste candidate. Where the SP fields a candidate from a non-Yadav backward community, the BJP may field someone from the Yadav community. The BJP will also try to bring into its fold leaders who are denied tickets by the SP and may rebel against the party. Muslim and Yadav voters hold sway in 91 seats from western to eastern UP These 91 constituencies with a significant Muslim and Yadav population are spread mainly across western UP, Rohilkhand and central-eastern Uttar Pradesh. Muslim-influenced areas: In districts such as Moradabad, Rampur, Sambhal, Bijnor, Saharanpur, Muzaffarnagar, Amroha, Shamli, Kairana and Bareilly in western UP and Rohilkhand, Muslim voters play a decisive role. Yadav-influenced areas: Districts such as Mainpuri, Firozabad, Kannauj, Etawah, Badaun, Azamgarh, Etah and Farrukhabad have traditionally been SP strongholds. The SP is considered to have a strong grassroots organisation in more than 85 Assembly constituencies across these 17 districts. Breaking through this network is a major challenge for the BJP. BJP focuses on non-Yadav OBC communities Non-Yadav backward communities have been a key pillar of the BJP's social engineering strategy. In the 2014, 2019 and 2024 Lok Sabha elections, as well as the 2017 and 2022 Assembly elections, the party relied on this vote bank to defeat its rivals. For the 2027 elections, the BJP may once again field influential faces from the Kurmi, Maurya, Shakya, Saini, Nishad and Pal communities. It is also trying to build a broader electoral coalition by bringing together its traditional support base among Brahmins, Rajputs and Vaishyas. A senior BJP leader, speaking on condition of anonymity, said, “In the 2022 Assembly elections, the presence of the BSP made the contest triangular in several constituencies. In some seats, the votes secured by BSP candidates affected the margin between the SP and the BJP.” The BJP will therefore also keep an eye on the BSP's strategy and candidate selection in the upcoming elections. The party will try to benefit directly in constituencies where opposition votes are likely to split. However, the impact will depend on local equations and the popularity of candidates in each constituency. Survey underway to identify strong SP candidates in each region The BJP is also conducting surveys in these 91 constituencies. The findings will be sent to the state and central leadership to help them make informed decisions while finalising tickets. The surveys are being conducted on two fronts: Assessing the report cards of sitting MLAs: The party is examining the influence of sitting MLAs in their constituencies and the level of public dissatisfaction against them. It is also assessing whether fielding a new face could improve the party's chances of winning. Reports are being prepared on all these aspects. Identifying potential SP candidates: The BJP is gathering information on which SP leaders are leading the race for tickets, their strengths and weaknesses, and their acceptance among voters. Candidate selection will be the real test of the election strategy Political analyst Rajendra Kumar believes that Muslim and Yadav voters play a decisive role in these 91 constituencies. Both communities have been traditional and strong vote banks of the Samajwadi Party for decades. Creating a split in their support is a major challenge for any rival party. In these regions, local issues tend to have a greater impact than national or emotional issues. The SP is often aggressive in raising issues such as unemployment, inflation, farmers' problems and anti-incumbency against BJP MLAs. BJP spokesperson Avnish Tyagi, who has an understanding of western UP politics, said, “Every aspect is taken into account during a major election. One important factor is who the opponent is. Parties select their candidates accordingly. The BJP is preparing a similar strategy for seats where it has remained weak.” The party is also monitoring whether the SP and Congress, or Chandrashekhar and Asaduddin Owaisi, form an alliance. If an alliance takes shape, the BJP will examine which candidate is likely to contest each seat and who could be a strong choice for the party there. Decisions will be taken at the appropriate time after considering all these factors.

stories.title: Man murdered inside Ghaziabad police station:Stabbed in the chest as officers watched; he had returned home after celebrating Bhai Dooj
stories.summary: A 20-year-old man was murdered inside a police station in Ghaziabad. The attacker stabbed him in the chest, leaving him covered in blood and causing him to collapse on the floor. Police chased and caught the accused as he fled after stabbing the man. Police have registered a case based on a complaint by the man's family. The man's younger brother said the attackers had assaulted his brother on 6 November as well. At the time, police took both sides to the police station. The incident took place at 6 p.m. on Wednesday at Vijay Nagar police station. A fight broke out outside the house, police took them to the station Ayush, son of Yashpal, who lives in Sarvodaya Nagar, worked for a company in Noida. He returned home on Wednesday evening after celebrating Bhai Dooj. Outside the house, Sonu, who lives in Charan Singh Colony, surrounded him with his associates. They assaulted him. Vijay Nagar police arrived after residents of the neighbourhood complained. Sonu's associates fled when they saw the police. The police took Ayush and Sonu to the station. Ayush's family followed them to the station. As soon as they entered, Sonu stabbed Ayush in the chest. Ayush collapsed to the floor after being stabbed. The police sent him to hospital, where he died. Meanwhile, the police arrested the accused, Sonu. Brother says-They assaulted us on 6 November too Ayush's brother Aman said there had also been a fight on Dhanteras (6 November). He said, "I was going to work with my brother that day. The accused assaulted us on the way and then called the police themselves." The police arrived, put Ayush in a jeep and took him away. Aman said that the people from the other side should be arrested. The police also assaulted him. The accused were threatening to kill him Aman alleges that family members had brought Ayush home after getting him released from the police station. A complaint was also filed with the police after this. The police, acting in a one-sided manner, sent Ayush to jail instead. Meanwhile, after the altercation, Sonu was continuously threatening to kill Ayush. ACP Kotwali Upasana Pandey said that a case had been registered on the family's complaint and one accused, Sonu, had been taken into custody. Meanwhile, DCP City Dhawal Jaiswal said that two young men had fought with each other. On receiving the information, the police reached the spot and brought both men to the police station. So far, the investigation does not indicate that the death was caused by a stab wound. A small mark was found on the chest. The matter will become clear after the post-mortem report is released. Ayush's fight on Dhanteras was with other boys. The police's role is also being investigated.

stories.title: 'If not for Uttarakhand's daughter, you would be herding buffaloes':CM Yogi targets Akhilesh in Lucknow, says he calls people from Uttarakhand infiltrators
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said in Lucknow, “Someone says that people from Uttarakhand are infiltrators. I told him that if it were not for a daughter from Uttarakhand, you would have been grazing buffaloes in Saifai.” He added that the state’s first Chief Minister also belonged to Uttarakhand. Although Yogi did not name Akhilesh Yadav, his remarks were directed at the Samajwadi Party chief. Yogi said, “We have drunk the water of Uttarakhand and eaten its food grains. Accepting challenges and fighting them head-on has become part of our genes.” Speaking about the festival, the CM said its significance increases further because of its association with Lord Ram. “On one side, we have the culture of Awadh, and on the other, the pride of Devbhoomi. This festival offers a wonderful confluence of the two,” he said. CM Yogi attended the 14-day Uttarakhand Mahotsav, organised on the banks of the Gomti river in Lucknow, on Wednesday. The festival, which began on November 9, features competitions showcasing Uttarakhand’s folk culture, music, dance and traditional cuisine. Products from across the country at 150 stalls The festival will feature handicrafts, organic products from self-help groups, herbal juice, Uttarakhand sweets, Nainital savouries, Kashmiri shawls and carpets, among various other products. Around 150 stalls have been set up.

stories.title: Man troubled by in-laws jumps into Gomti in Lucknow:Sends video to family before suicide; alleges in-laws are torturing him
stories.summary: A 27-year-old man’s body was found in the Gomti river in Lucknow on Wednesday. He had been missing since Monday night. His motorcycle was found abandoned on the Gomti bridge on the route from Samta Moolak Chowk towards 1090 Chowk. The man has been identified as Mohammad Zeeshan. Before taking his own life, he recorded a video and sent it to his family. In the video, he said he was going to die by suicide and blamed his in-laws for it. He said, “My in-laws are constantly harassing me.” Following this, police launched a search operation in the river with the help of the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF). Read the full report… Motorcycle found abandoned on Gomti river bridge According to police, a motorcycle was found abandoned on the Gomti river bridge at around 3 am on the intervening night of November 10 and 11 during patrolling. A mobile phone was also found switched on and placed on the motorcycle. However, enquiries in the area did not reveal any information about its owner. Police traced the owner with the help of the e-challan app. The motorcycle belonged to Mohammad Zeeshan, a resident of Katra Khudayar Khan in Saadatganj. Police tried contacting him on the mobile number registered with the vehicle, but the phone was switched off. Sent video to family before suicide Police then informed his family through Saadatganj police station. At around 10 am on Tuesday, Zeeshan’s family members reached the police station. They told police that Zeeshan had sent a video to his brother-in-law, Saifu, at around 1 am. In the video, he spoke about taking his own life and blamed his in-laws. What Zeeshan said in the video before his death “I am Zeeshan, son of Shakeel. I am very troubled by my mother-in-law Seema, her family members and my wife Mahwar. They are harassing me a lot. They beat me up and do all sorts of things. I am going to take my own life. Mahwar, Seema, Sama, Mohsin and all the others are responsible for my death.” Body found near River Front Police then launched a search operation in the Gomti river with the help of the SDRF. At around 11 am on Wednesday, Zeeshan’s body was recovered from the river near River Front in the Gomti Nagar area. Police took possession of the body, completed the inquest proceedings in the presence of his family members and sent it for post-mortem.

stories.title: Lucknow becomes India's third cleanest city:Ranked 44th two years ago; receives award from President
stories.summary: Lucknow has become the third-cleanest city in the country. This was revealed in the Swachh Survekshan 2025-26 list. On Wednesday, President Droupadi Murmu presented the award to the Lucknow Municipal Corporation at Vigyan Bhavan in New Delhi. Urban Development Minister AK Sharma, Mayor Sushma Kharkwal, Principal Secretary P. Gurupasad and Municipal Commissioner Gaurav Kumar accepted the honour. Lucknow had earlier secured third place in 2024 and 2025 as well. This time, Visakhapatnam ranked first and Jabalpur second. Lucknow was ranked 44th two years ago The Union government conducts the Swachh Survekshan every year. Rankings are determined based on the cleanliness systems and sanitation work in cities across the country. In 2024, Lucknow made a major leap, rising directly from 44th place to third place. This time too, the municipal corporation has retained its ranking. Citizen feedback also a focus this time Citizen participation was also given importance in the survey. A field survey was conducted to assess the actual state of cleanliness in the cities. In addition, door-to-door waste collection, segregation of wet and dry waste, the condition of public toilets and the disposal of complaints were also examined. This was the tenth edition of the survey. More than 4,751 cities across the country were included. The cities were assessed across 10 key areas and 43 parameters. Municipal Corporation Rewarded for Its Hard Work Over the past one year, the municipal commissioner and the team took several major steps to improve cleanliness. From waste management and regular cleaning in the wards to public participation, awareness campaigns and digital monitoring, Lucknow's appearance was transformed. As a result, the city was included in the list of the country's top-3 cleanest cities. Public Also Participated, Bringing Success Lucknow's residents also deserve the greatest credit for this transformation. Door-to-door waste segregation, the prohibition on dumping waste in the open and increased awareness about cleanliness turned the Municipal Corporation's campaign into a people's movement. Municipal corporation officials and councillors say the goal is now to make Lucknow the country's No. 1 city in cleanliness. Several more schemes will be launched before the next survey for this purpose. Visakhapatnam first and Jabalpur second According to Municipal Corporation Additional Municipal Commissioner Dr Arvind Rao, Visakhapatnam secured first place and Jabalpur second in the Swachh Survekshan 2025-26.

stories.title: IT company executive, wife and 2 children die:Car crashes on Ganga Expressway in Hardoi; scrapes along divider for 30 metres
stories.summary: A horrific road accident on the Ganga Expressway in Hardoi left an SUV completely wrecked. The Noida-based IT company's vice-chairman, his wife and two sons, who were travelling in the vehicle, died. After hitting the divider, the out-of-control car continued travelling along it for around 30 metres. During this, a one-and-a-half-year-old child fell around 20 feet below the highway. The accident took place at around 1 p.m. on Wednesday in the Sandi police station area, 40 kilometres from the district headquarters. See two pictures... Family was travelling to Prayagraj to celebrate Bhai Dooj and Chhath Saurabh Upadhyay, 40, worked in Noida, his brother-in-law Shishir Upadhyay said. He was a resident of the EWS housing complex in Neem Sarai Mundera, Prayagraj. On Wednesday morning, he was travelling to his home in Prayagraj with his wife, Menaka Upadhyay, 35, and their two sons, Vyom, seven, and Shivom, one and a half, to celebrate Bhai Dooj and Chhath. At around 1 p.m., their car went out of control on the Ganga Expressway at kilometre 317, in the Sandi police station area of Hardoi. Near Bhatouli Mafi village, the car hit the divider and continued running along it for 30 metres. Three died at the spot According to eyewitnesses, police from the Sandi, Bilgram and Harpalpur police stations reached the scene as soon as they received information about the accident. Saurabh, Menaka and their elder son Vyom had died at the scene. Police recovered all three bodies. The injured child was taken to the nearest CHC hospital, where doctors tried to save him by administering CPR, but the medical team was unsuccessful and declared him dead. Saurabh Upadhyay was the only son Shishir Upadhyay (Saurabh's brother-in-law) said, "Saurabh was the only son. His family includes his father, Jai Govind Upadhyay, 65, and two younger sisters. Both sisters are married." Menaka, Saurabh's wife, was originally from Ghazipur. Her maternal family currently lives in Gomti Nagar, Lucknow. Menaka was her parents' only daughter. She had a younger brother. Wife left her job in 2024 Menaka and Saurabh got married in 2018. Menaka Upadhyay was also a manager at a company in Noida. She left her job in 2024, before the birth of their younger son, Shivom.

stories.title: Chauri Chaura Express derails in Kanpur:4 AC coaches go off track at Central station; train was heading to Gorakhpur
stories.summary: The Chauri Chaura Express derailed in Kanpur on Wednesday evening. The incident occurred at Kanpur Central station. The train arrived at platform number 7 and, as it began to depart, four coaches from B3 to B7 derailed. Train number 15003 was travelling from Anwarganj to Gorakhpur. Railway officials and an engineering team have reached the spot following the incident. The train is being placed back on the tracks. Passenger says- There was a sudden strong jerk, everyone rushed out A passenger said, “We were travelling home with our family for Chhath Puja. I had seat number 78 in coach B6. My child had gone to the toilet when the train started moving. There was a sudden strong jerk and my child fell inside the train. Passengers realised that something was wrong. Suddenly, everyone started rushing out. When we got outside, we learnt that several coaches of the train had derailed.” My coach suddenly started tilting to one side Sanjeev Tripathi, who was travelling from Kanpur to Deoria, said, “As soon as the train started moving, there was a loud noise. The coach I was sitting in began tilting to one side, and we could hear a rattling sound. Fearing something serious had happened, passengers got down with their belongings.” Passengers have been told that they will be sent to their destinations on a special train, which could take four to five hours to arrive. Passengers to be sent on a special train Aakanshu Goyal said around 300 passengers were travelling in the four coaches that derailed. All passengers are safe. They have been asked to wait on platform number 1, where arrangements are being made for a special train and refreshments. Passengers who do not wish to continue their journey will receive a full 100% refund at the ticket counter. Rail traffic at the station has not been disrupted due to the accident. Inquiry committee to find out cause of accident Chief Public Relations Officer Shivam Sharma said it was difficult to determine the cause of the accident at this stage. An inquiry committee will be formed after the affected coaches are put back on the tracks and arrangements are made for passengers. The committee will investigate the incident from different angles. The cause of the accident will be known only after its report is submitted. Helpline numbers issued for passengers and their families The Railways has issued helpline numbers to assist passengers and their family members. People can contact Kanpur Central on 0512-2323018, 0512-2323016 and 0512-2323015. The helpline numbers for Prayagraj Junction are 0532-2408128, 0532-2407353 and 0532-2408149. A separate helpline number, 9151833006, has been issued for Fatehpur station. stories.title: 'My daughter was beaten to death in government school':Uncle alleges she was pushed to ground and kicked repeatedly in stomach in Baghpat
stories.summary: A sixth-grade student died after being beaten at a government school in Baghpat. According to the girl's uncle, she had a quarrel with another girl from the same village. The girl knocked her to the ground and kicked her several times in the stomach. The girl had been unwell since the beating at the school ground. She died during treatment in Meerut on Wednesday. The incident took place on 28 October in the Sadar Kotwali area. The girls quarrelled while playing Misty (12), the daughter of Pawan Kumar, a resident of Hamidabad alias Nayagaon village, went to primary school on 28 October. She was a Class six student. While playing there, Misty and Arshi (14), the daughter of Shaukat from the same village, had an argument over something. The girl's paternal uncle said that Arshi knocked Misty to the ground and beat her. She kicked her five to six times in the stomach. After returning home, Misty complained of stomach pain. Her condition then began to deteriorate. We took Misty to Baraut Hospital for treatment on 4 November. On 5 November, doctors referred her to Meerut. She died at Subharti Hospital at 4 a.m. on Wednesday. Father said - daughter's health deteriorated after she was beaten at school Father Pawan Kumar said doctors at the hospital had told them that the girl had infections in her lungs and abdomen. After her death, the family took the body to the village and informed the police. The police reached the spot and sent the body for a post-mortem examination. Father Pawan Kumar accused the school administration of negligence and demanded action. He said his daughter's health began to deteriorate only after the assault at school. Principal says no fight took place at school Principal Meenakshi told the police that there had been no fight between the girls at the school. Misty's mother had visited the school several days earlier and complained that her daughter had been assaulted. Misty's aunt works as a cook at the school. The girl had not complained of being assaulted by any school employee. Around 250 children study at our school. Kotwali station in-charge Manoj Chahal said- The cause of the girl's death will become clear after the post-mortem report is received. Further action will be taken once a written complaint is received from the family.

stories.title: SGPGI to offer direct route to heart surgery after MBBS:MCh course to start for the first time; NMC approves six super-speciality courses
stories.summary: Six super-speciality courses at SGPGI Lucknow have been recognised by the National Medical Commission (NMC). This has cleared the way for the launch of the country's first DM course in Maternal and Fetal Medicine and a six-year MCh course in CVTS at the institute. Students will now have the opportunity to become heart surgeons after completing six years of study directly after MBBS. Specialist doctors will also be trained to treat diseases in unborn babies. SGPGI will be the first institute in Uttar Pradesh to launch a DM course in haematopathology. Specialists will be trained to treat unborn babies Under the DM course in Maternal and Fetal Medicine, unborn babies will also be treated as patients, and trainees will be taught how to provide them with medical care. The course will cover prenatal examinations, the diagnosis of fetal diseases and fetal therapy. This will help in detecting congenital diseases and complex conditions affecting unborn babies in time. According to the institute, it may also help reduce maternal mortality, stillbirths and neonatal mortality. Six years of study directly after MBBS for heart surgery Under the six-year MCh course in CVTS, students will be able to train in heart surgery immediately after completing their MBBS. They will not need to first complete a three-year MS in General Surgery. According to the institute, this is the first time such a six-year course is being launched in the country. It will produce specialist surgeons for heart surgery. Specialists to be trained to treat thalassaemia and haemophilia Under the DM course in haematopathology, specialists will be trained to diagnose and treat blood-related diseases. This will strengthen treatment facilities for serious conditions such as thalassaemia and haemophilia. SGPGI's Department of Haematology has been running the DM Clinical Haematology course since 2011. Specialists to treat long-term pain Under the DM course in Pain Medicine, specialists will be trained to treat patients suffering from long-term pain. According to the institute's press release, around 30% of adults in the country suffer from chronic pain. Nearly 80% of those experiencing severe pain do not receive appropriate treatment. The new course will provide training in modern pain-relief procedures along with medication. Specialisation in cancer and paediatric treatment will also increase The six-year course in Radiation Therapy and Oncology will provide training in cancer detection, staging, and treatment through radiation and chemotherapy. Meanwhile, the six-year MCh course in Paediatric Urology will train specialists to treat complex urinary and urological conditions in children. It may be noted that the institute's director, Prof. RK Dhiman, is also a member of the committee of the NMC's Postgraduate Medical Education Board that grants recognition to new courses.

stories.title: Car crashes into railing at 100 kmph:Metal sheet pierces child’s body; siblings killed; family was travelling from Gujarat to UP
stories.summary: In Ratlam, a speeding car went out of control and crashed into a roadside railing on the Delhi-Mumbai eight-lane Expressway on Wednesday morning. The impact was so severe that the car was completely wrecked. The railing pierced the car through the front seat, tore through the body of a child inside and emerged from the other side. The couple's 13-year-old son and six-year-old daughter died in the accident. Their parents were injured. The car had a Gujarat registration number. The family travelling in it was going from Baroda in Gujarat to Unnao in Uttar Pradesh. The accident occurred near Badayla crossroads in Jaora. The car was travelling at around 100 kmph at the time. As soon as the police received the information, they reached the spot and took the injured to Jaora Hospital. After initial treatment, they were referred to Ratlam Medical College for better treatment. Here are some pictures taken after the accident... Family is from Uttar Pradesh; father is a deputy manager at a pharma company in Gujarat The deceased children were identified as six-year-old daughter Vidhi Verma and 13-year-old son Sagar Verma. Their father, Rajababu Verma, is a deputy manager at a pharma company in Harol, Gujarat. They are originally from Unnao in Uttar Pradesh. His wife, Rishu Verma (42), was also seriously injured in the accident. The railing pierced the car before the airbags deployed Father Rajababu Verma said that they lived in Harol, Gujarat. They had left at 4:30 a.m. on Wednesday with the family to travel to their village. He was driving the car himself, which was travelling at around 100 km per hour. His son Sagar was sitting in the front seat, while his wife and daughter were seated in the back. He said the car was also fitted with airbags, but the impact was so forceful that a section of the iron railing along the roadside pierced the car. One part tore through his son Sagar's body and came out the other side, while another struck his daughter's head. Both children died in the accident. Father says daughter might have survived if she had received timely treatment Rajababu expressed anger over the lack of timely medical treatment on the highway. He said there was no hospital or healthcare facility around the eight-lane highway. His daughter might have survived if she had received treatment in time. At present, his son's body is being kept in Jaora, while his injured wife has been admitted to the medical college.

stories.title: Akhilesh says he will visit Vrindavan after Ayodhya:Asks, 'Why is BJP so worried?'; saints call meeting against SP chief in Ayodhya
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav said on Wednesday, "I will visit not only Ayodhya but also Kedareshwar. I will also visit Vrindavan." This is the first time Akhilesh has himself spoken of visiting the Ram temple. Earlier, SP leader Pawan Pandey had said that the former chief minister would visit Ram Lalla on 12 December. Akhilesh gave a new meaning to PDA: "First darshan, then blessings." He said that both Shiva and Ram were in their home. "Uncle Shivpal and Ram Gopal Yadav are both with us. Awadhesh and Pawan are also with us. Why is the BJP so worried?" Meanwhile, the saints and mahants of Ayodhya have prepared to oppose Akhilesh. The saints will hold a meeting at Maniram Das Chhauni today to chalk out a strategy to oppose him. The meeting will be chaired by Mahant Kamal Nayan Das Shastri. Key points from Akhilesh's press conference: 1. Khajanchi turns 10 today At the Samajwadi Party headquarters in Lucknow, Akhilesh described demonetisation as an 'ocean of corruption'. Referring to 'Khajanchi', the child born in a bank queue during demonetisation, he said that Khajanchi had turned 10 today. The BJP had not celebrated his birthday to date. The BJP should now adopt him. However, it should not do so in the way its leaders have adopted villages. The Samajwadi family continues to take care of Khajanchi's education and overall welfare. 2. What happened to the ₹2,000 friend? Akhilesh quipped that the ₹2,000 note was born at the same time as Khazanchi. He said, "Sometimes Khazanchi asks tearfully, 'What happened to my ₹2,000 friend who was born with me? Why was he taken away?'" 3. Akhilesh says: It is no longer an 80-20 battle, but a 95-5 fight Akhilesh said that the fight was no longer between 80 and 20; it was a fight between 95 and 5. The 95% who are oppressed, distressed and humiliated are on one side, while the 5% exploiters are on the other. When there is a 95-5 fight, people from the Bharatiya Janata Party will not even realise where they have ended up. That is why their language and behaviour have changed. 4. Offered two suggestions on the CM's claim that 1.27 crore votes had been deleted The SP chief took a dig, saying that newspapers had reported the seizure of cannabis worth 1 crore 27 lakh. Meanwhile, there is talk of 1.27 crore votes being deleted. What a strange coincidence. For a transparent election system, do two things: provide voters with strong metal cards that cannot be duplicated or copied, and link the voter list to Aadhaar. 5. Government could not advance the metro by even 10 centimetres in 10 years Akhilesh said the Lucknow, Kanpur and Agra metro projects were the SP government's contribution. The BJP government could not advance the metro by even 10 centimetres in 10 years. The riding quality of roads and expressways has become extremely poor due to corruption in the tendering process, leading to an increase in accidents. 6. ‘Collected 200 litres of cow urine, but the DM refused to accept it’ Akhilesh said, "The government is unable to provide farmers even with fertiliser and DAP. They had said they would buy cow dung and cow urine. We collected 200 litres of cow urine in a bucket in a single day, but the Lucknow District Magistrate refused to accept it! Now tell us, what is a farmer supposed to do?" 7. SP MPs and senior leaders are not being provided security The former chief minister said, “Despite requesting it, SP MPs and senior leaders (RK Chaudhary, Anand Bhadauria and Inderjit Saroj) are not being provided security, while the government's favourites are being given NSG (NSG) cover and heavy security by the Centre.”

stories.title: Man arrested over bomb threat to Diljit Dosanjh's Indore concert:UP ATS detains suspect who sent email to Gwalior High Court
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) arrested a suspect on Tuesday night in connection with a bomb threat targeting Punjabi singer Diljit Dosanjh's concert scheduled for November 15 in Indore. Investigators found several threatening messages linked to the suspect's email account. During questioning, he claimed that he had sold the account to another person. The ATS is now searching for the alleged buyer to establish who sent the threats. The threatening email was sent to the official email address of the Gwalior Bench of the Madhya Pradesh High Court. It warned that the concert stage would be blown up using an improvised explosive device (IED). The email also threatened to bomb Bollywood actor Amitabh Bachchan's residence, Jalsa, in Mumbai. ATS traces IP address to identify suspect While investigating the threatening emails, the ATS traced their IP address. This led investigators to two cities in Uttar Pradesh, where they detained a suspect on Tuesday night. During questioning, the man claimed that he had sold his email account. However, it is yet to be established whether he sent the threats himself or someone who purchased the account used it for the purpose. The ATS is investigating the account's sale and purchase, as well as the motive behind the threats. Gwalior police are in the process of registering an FIR based on a complaint by the High Court's security in-charge. Investigating agencies are working to identify the person who sent the threatening messages. Following the incident, police in Indore and Bhopal have also been placed on alert. Similar threats reported in Delhi and Mumbai This is not the first time that threats have been issued in connection with Diljit Dosanjh's concerts. Similar threatening messages were received in Delhi and Mumbai earlier. In October, the singer's proposed concert in Delhi was initially denied permission due to security concerns. However, approval was granted after a review of the security arrangements, and the show was held on October 30. On October 23, the office of former Mumbai mayor Ritu Tawde also received a threatening email. The message reportedly warned of an attack on Diljit's concert. In view of the repeated threats, police are maintaining heightened security arrangements for the singer's November 15 concert in Indore.

stories.title: 12-year-old boy kidnapped and murdered in Mirzapur:₹30 lakh ransom demanded after land sold for ₹60 lakh; accused arrested in encounter
stories.summary: Police arrested in an encounter the accused who kidnapped and murdered a 12-year-old boy in Mirzapur. The accused strangled the child to death for a ransom of ₹30 lakh. He had taken him on a motorcycle on the evening of 9 November on the pretext of taking him for a ride. The incident took place in Semri village in the Vindhyachal police station area. The child has been identified as 12-year-old Prince Bind of Semri village. Police arrested the accused after shooting him in both legs early on Wednesday. The child's body was also recovered from Kushiyara forest based on information provided by the accused. Villagers blocked the road to protest the child's murder. They said the child died because of police negligence. They said the child's life could have been saved if the police had taken action in time. Read the full story... Keshav Bind, son of Ramdas Bind and a resident of Semari village, runs a tea and paan shop on the Mirzapur-Prayagraj road near Mahashakti Inter College. Pintu alias Shailendra of Parsia Kamapur used to visit the shop. By visiting the shop, he had become acquainted with the family. At around 4 p.m. on Monday, 9 November, Keshav Bind's 12-year-old only son, Prince, was at the shop. He was a Class 6 student at ISS Public School in Bihsada Kala village. During this time, Pintu came to their shop. He lured the child and took him along for a ride on his motorcycle. When Prince did not return home for a long time, the family became worried. They were still searching for the child when the young man called the child's father's mobile phone at around 10 p.m. on Monday. During the call, the young man demanded ₹30 lakh in exchange for abducting the child and returning him. The family became distressed after hearing the ransom demand. SP deploys three teams to arrest accused The father went to the police station on Tuesday (10 Nov). He explained the entire matter and submitted a named complaint. The police registered an FIR and began an investigation. Based on surveillance, call details and manual inputs, the police established the involvement of the accused, Pintu alias Shailendra. SP Aparna Rajat Kaushik formed three teams to recover the child and arrest the accused. All three teams conducted raids at several locations. Opened fire at police during checking Police received information in the early hours of Wednesday that the accused was coming from the Lalganj side. Following this, teams from the Gaipura and Ashtabhuja police outposts, led by Vindhyachal Station House Officer Inspector Ajit Singh, began checking on the road from Gaipura-Vijaypur to Lalganj. During the checking, a motorcyclist was spotted approaching from the Lalganj side. When police tried to stop him, he turned the motorcycle towards Kushiyara forest, abandoned it some distance ahead and fled into the forest. He opened fire at the police team in the forest. In retaliatory firing by the police, he was shot in both legs. He was subsequently arrested. The injured accused was sent to the district hospital for treatment. Body hidden in forest after murder During police questioning, accused Pintu said that around two and a half hours after taking the child with him, he strangled him to death in Kushiyara forest at 6:30 p.m. He then hid the body in the forest. According to the police, he kidnapped the child out of greed for money. He said that the child's father had sold his land for ₹60 lakh. He had learnt about this. The police recovered the child's body based on information provided by him. 17 cases, including murder and robbery, registered Accused Pintu alias Shailendra has a criminal history. A total of 17 cases, including theft, murder, attempted murder, robbery, offences under the Arms Act, the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act and the Gangsters Act, have been registered against him at various police stations in Mirzapur and Raebareli. These include a 2014 case registered at Vindhyachal police station for murder, concealing evidence and criminal conspiracy, as well as a 2020 case at Handia police station in Prayagraj concerning murder, kidnapping and destruction of evidence. Villagers accuse police of negligence, block road Anger spread among the family members and villagers after they were informed on Wednesday morning that the child's body had been found. They blocked the Mirzapur-Prayagraj road in front of Semri village. Villagers allege that the child's life could not be saved because of police negligence. They say the police were unable to trace Prince despite searching for around 36 hours. The aggrieved family members remained adamant that the SP be called to the spot and that the accused be given strict punishment.

stories.title: Gorakhpur players meet CM Yogi after Asian triumph:India's Asian champion tennis ball cricket team presents him winning jersey after 6 consecutive victories
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath met and congratulated players from Gorakhpur who helped India win the Asian Tennis Ball Cricket Championship 2026 in Chennai on Wednesday. Indian team captain Aman Raj, along with his teammates, paid a courtesy visit to the Chief Minister and presented him with the winning jersey of the Asian champions. Yogi praised the team's historic achievement and encouraged the players to continue bringing glory to the country and Uttar Pradesh. Captain Aman Raj was accompanied by Prateek Tripathi, Avinash Sahani, Rohit Sharma and Naman Singh during the meeting. India wins Asian title after six consecutive victories The Asian Tennis Ball Cricket Championship 2026 was held in Chennai from October 26 to 29. The Indian senior men's team won the gold medal after an impressive campaign under the captaincy of international player Aman Raj from Gorakhpur. Competing against teams from 12 countries, India won all six matches to lift the title. In the final, India defeated Bahrain by 25 runs to become Asian champions. India defeats five teams to reach final India began its campaign with victories over Nepal, Uzbekistan, the Maldives and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) in the group stage to qualify for the semi-finals. The team then defeated Sri Lanka by 16 runs in the semi-final to book its place in the title clash. Batting first in the final, India set Bahrain a target of 64 runs. However, the Indian bowlers restricted Bahrain to just 39 runs, securing a 25-run victory and the championship title. Gorakhpur players bring pride to the city Players from Gorakhpur made a significant contribution to India's historic success. Captain Aman Raj led the team with his leadership and strategy, while Prateek Tripathi and Avinash Sahani delivered impressive all-round performances with both bat and ball. Gaurav Singh also strengthened the team's batting line-up. A total of six players from Gorakhpur represented India across the youth and senior categories of the championship. They were Aman Raj, Prateek Tripathi, Avinash Sahani, Gaurav Singh, Rohit Sharma and Faiz. Their performances on the international stage have brought pride to the city's sporting community. Players present winning jersey to Chief Minister The players described their meeting with Yogi Adityanath after winning the Asian title as a special moment. Captain Aman Raj said the Chief Minister's blessings and encouragement were a source of inspiration for the entire team. He added that the victory was not just an achievement for the Indian team but also a matter of pride for Uttar Pradesh and Gorakhpur. The players presented the winning jersey to the Chief Minister as a memento of their championship victory. Hard work and teamwork behind India's success Tennis Ball Cricket Federation of India secretary Imran Ahmed Lari congratulated the Indian team, saying the achievement was the result of the players' hard work, discipline and team spirit. He said that under Aman Raj's experienced leadership, the team had demonstrated its talent and potential at the Asian level. He also noted that Gorakhpur players' consistent performances in international competitions were a matter of pride for the entire city. According to Lari, tennis ball cricket has been recognised by the Government of India since 1999, and the sport's popularity continues to grow.

stories.title: Yogi says one took exam, another got the job:'Munna Bhais' were sitting in the system; 1,146 candidates receive joining letters
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said on Wednesday that before 2017, young people could not get government jobs fairly in the state. He said there was discrimination in the recruitment process and that appointment boards and commissions were under the control of the Saifai syndicate. Yogi said that people known as 'Munna Bhais' had even taken control of government positions. He said, "Before 2017, one person would take the examination, while someone else would get the appointment letter." Earlier, the Chief Minister distributed appointment letters to 1,146 candidates selected for junior assistant posts in the Revenue Department in Lucknow. He also provided financial assistance worth ₹215 crore to 4,300 beneficiaries under the Chief Minister's Farmer Accident Welfare Scheme. Key points from Yogi's speech 1. Yogi asks candidates if they had to pay money or seek recommendations After handing over the appointment letters, Yogi asked the candidates whether they had to seek recommendations from anyone during the recruitment process. He also asked if anyone had asked them for money, called them to influence the process or created problems during document verification. All the candidates replied that they had faced no such problems. Yogi said this showed the progress made by Uttar Pradesh. 2. Those in the government were behind the unfair practices earlier Yogi said it was unfair when a person who did not even take an examination got an appointment letter, while deserving candidates who worked hard were left without jobs. He said candidates naturally felt hurt when they did not get the results of their hard work. They would complain to the government or approach the court, but the same government was responsible for these unfair practices. This often led to court cases and stay orders. 3. SP government had also disbanded 34 PAC companies The Chief Minister said that when his government came to power in 2017, he held a meeting with the police and Home Department officials. He asked how many posts were vacant in the police force. Officials told him that around 1.5 lakh posts were vacant at the time. Yogi also said that the Samajwadi Party government had disbanded 34 companies of the Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC), which was known for taking action against rioters. He claimed that around 1,500 riots took place during the SP government's rule. News being updated…

stories.title: Man shoots himself at girlfriend's house:Family refused to let them meet; her marriage fixed with someone else
stories.summary: A 30-year-old man died by suicide after shooting himself outside his girlfriend's house in Basti on Wednesday morning. The girl's family had initially agreed to their relationship but later refused to go ahead with the marriage and fixed her marriage with someone else. At around 7:30 am, Shiv arrived at the girl's house to meet her, but her family stopped him outside. He said that he would kill himself if they did not let him meet her. When the family refused, he took out a country-made pistol and shot himself in the chest. The incident took place in Basewa Rai village in Harraiya, around 30 km from the district headquarters. After receiving information, the police and forensic team reached the spot and collected evidence. Police questioned the family, took custody of the body and sent it for a post-mortem examination. He created a scene in the village before shooting himself According to the police, Shivkumar, a resident of Thakurpur, had come to Basewa Rai village to visit his relative, Lalu Prasad. He was in a relationship with a girl from the family and was insisting on meeting her. When he could not meet her, he threatened to die by suicide. Shivkumar was shouting loudly, hearing which people from nearby houses gathered at the spot and tried to calm him down. However, he did not listen to anyone and shot himself in front of the villagers. Amid the chaos, Harraiya Station House Officer Sanjay Kumar reached the spot with police personnel and a forensic team. The officer said that the marriage of the two had been fixed earlier but was called off for some reason. He said this led Shivkumar to die by suicide. However, Circle Officer Swarnima Singh gave a different account. She said Shivkumar wanted to marry his cousin, his paternal aunt's daughter, but the girl was not willing to marry him. This had led to tension between the two families. On Wednesday, Shivkumar threatened people before shooting himself. Here is the full sequence of events According to Parshurampur police station in-charge Pradeep Singh, Shivkumar was a resident of Thakurpur village and had been in a relationship with a young woman from Basewa village. The two had been in contact for the past 10 years. Shivkumar wanted to marry the woman at any cost. However, after her family fixed her marriage elsewhere, he allegedly sent them objectionable photos and videos of her and threatened to make them public. After receiving a complaint, Parshurampur police called both of them to the police station on Tuesday, a day before the incident. They reached an agreement and decided to stop talking to each other and change their mobile numbers. Shivkumar also agreed to delete the photos and videos from his phone. However, the very next day, he reached the woman's house and insisted on meeting her. He started shouting loudly and later shot himself.

stories.title: House wall collapses, killing 2 children:Trapped under debris while sleeping with parents, bodies recovered after 7 hours
stories.summary: Two young sisters died after a wall of their house collapsed in Varanasi, while their parents were injured. The family was sleeping in the verandah of their house, which was built beside a pond, when the accident occurred. The wall suddenly collapsed at around 12.30 am on Tuesday night, trapping the entire family under the debris. Water from the pond also flooded the house following the collapse. The parents somehow managed to get out, but the two girls remained trapped under the debris and water. Hearing their cries, neighbours woke up and rushed to the spot. Police and State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) teams arrived and launched a rescue operation. After seven hours, at around 7.30 am, the bodies of Afiya (7) and Palak (4) were recovered from the debris. Their mother, Tabassum, and father, Ajuddin, were inconsolable after seeing their daughters' bodies. Police said moisture and dampness in the house, due to its location beside the pond, may have contributed to the collapse. The incident took place in the Bachchhaw Pashchim Pura area under the Rohania police station limits. Grandfather recounts how the accident happened The girls' grandfather, Sirajuddin, said the family had gone to sleep at night. His son, daughter-in-law and four children were inside the house, while he was sleeping outside. "I woke up when the wall suddenly collapsed. I heard my son and daughter-in-law shouting, 'The children have drowned, the children have drowned!'" He said he immediately jumped into the pond. Other villagers soon reached the spot, and his brother also jumped into the water to search for the children. However, they could not find them. The police arrived later and began the search operation. Sirajuddin said two children died in the accident, while the family's elder daughter, Roshni, and a younger son survived. The boy has not yet been named. He added that the family owns the land and has the property registration documents. The house was built in 2010. Family lived in a four-room house Sirajuddin's house has four rooms and a tin shed at the front. He has three sons. His eldest son, Ajuddin alias Kallu, is married, while his two younger sons are unmarried. Ajuddin lived in one of the rooms with his wife and their four children, making a family of six. Rohania ACP Awadhesh Vishwakarma said two girls died after the wall collapsed. Police reached the spot during the night after receiving information and called in rescue teams. Both bodies were recovered from the debris. Further action is being taken in the case.

stories.title: Muslim Christian groups accused of religious conversions in Lucknow:Hindu woman doctor targeted; former DGP claims bid to establish 'Ghazwa-e-Hind'
stories.summary: Several cases of alleged religious conversion have come to light in Lucknow over the past few months. A preliminary investigation is said to have pointed to the involvement of some Christian missionaries and Muslim organisations. Hindu organisations have alleged that some Muslim men target Hindu girls and women by trapping them in relationships under the name of 'love jihad'. They then pressure them to change their religion. Christian missionaries are also accused of using prayer meetings to attract poor Hindu families by offering financial help and claiming to cure illnesses. They allegedly persuade people to convert gradually. Former DGP links 'love jihad' to attempts to create terrorists Former Director General of Police Brij Lal said attempts were being made to create terrorists through 'love jihad' to carry out 'Ghazwa-e-Hind', which he described as a religious war against India. He also said that those questioning the Special Task Force (STF) investigation should themselves be investigated. He called for strict action against them so that it sets an example. Meanwhile, Hindu Mahasabha national spokesperson Shishir Chaturvedi said that King George's Medical University (KGMU) no longer appeared to be just a hospital. He alleged that it had become a place where Hindu girls were being targeted. He also demanded an investigation into the role of KGMU officials in the matter. Check out the pictures below : First, understand Muslim love jihad Hindu girls targeted, rate cards prepared The STF established during its investigation into KGMU doctor Rameez and those linked to him that Hindu girls were targeted and converted by forming a gang. Rate cards were also prepared to target girls from different castes. Doctors with good physiques were also provided facilities to influence the girls. Maulanas trained them to appear secular and to make the girls feel safe before luring them. Nursing staff at KGMU lured and converted The STF has stated in connection with the case that came to light in the conversion racket operating at KGMU that some doctors and employees posted in the pathology and other departments used to lure Hindu women doctors, students and nursing staff into romantic relationships and subject them to physical and mental exploitation. They later pressured them to convert. Prof. Suresh Babu, head of the pathology department, Dr Sumaira Qayoom and others used to suppress such cases, side with the accused and discriminate against Hindu employees and doctors. Parents of accused Dr Rameez also used to brainwash people The charge sheet filed by the police in the case involving Dr Ramizuddin, alias Ramiz, states that the main accused in the KGMU conversion case, Dr Ramizuddin alias Ramiz, and his parents used to brainwash and trap non-Muslim women doctors. They would initially pretend to be secular. They would then pose as hardline Muslims, make obscene videos and photographs to carry out religious conversions, and subsequently torture the victims. His parents allegedly drugged a woman doctor and had their son, Dr Ramiz, rape her. Two women doctors were allegedly forced to undergo abortions. Now, understand Christian conversion in the name of healing meetings... Contacting people through religious gatherings Although the allegation of religious conversion linked to the prayer meeting held inside a house in Rajajipuram has not been substantiated in the police's preliminary investigation, the method of inviting people to the meeting and assuring them that their personal problems would be resolved is similar to that seen in earlier cases. Investigations into religious conversion cases in Nigohan and Mohanlalganj had also found that problems such as illness, poverty and childlessness were being used to establish contact with people. A case of religious conversion in the name of a healing meeting came to light in September 2025 in Baktaurikheda village of Nigohan. Police arrested Malkhan alias Mathews. He was accused of inviting people to the meeting by assuring them that their illnesses would be cured and financial problems resolved. The investigation also found that contact with people was being expanded through religious meetings. Claim of financial assistance and treatment for illnesses Similarly, a religious conversion case came to light in July 2026 in Bharsawan village in Mohanlalganj. Police have filed a charge sheet against seven accused in the case. The police investigation found that people were being offered various inducements, including treatment for illnesses, the prospect of having children, financial assistance and education for their children. The gang lured people with money. After this, meetings were held at night, after which people were misled into becoming crypto-Christians, or secret Christians. The investigation also found that the gang did not ask people to change their names. After one generation, the next-or the third generation-became completely Christian, and their names were then changed. Healing meeting being held at a house on 1 November Information has emerged that prayer meetings were held every Sunday at a house in D-3, Rajajipuram, with the meeting on 1 November also taking place there. Women, men and children from various areas, including Dubagga, Kakori and Mohan, used to attend. Police sources said that during questioning, those who attended the meeting told them that they were promised relief from illness and poverty and the blessing of having children, among other things. Vishwa Hindu Parishad vice-president Saroj Singh said that more than 100 women, men and children were seated at the prayer meeting. The women said they had been called there to accept Christianity and that this would rid them of their sorrow and problems. That was why they had come there. However, Talकटora police said that the preliminary investigation had found no evidence of religious conversion. Bajrang Dal and Vishva Hindu Parishad members said that, as in earlier cases, a conversion racket was being run here by offering inducements. The police should investigate the matter seriously.

stories.title: Former GST Commissioner Anupama likes Sitapur:Says Akhilesh-Dimple are her favourite couple; has also written songs for Rahat Fateh Ali Khan
stories.summary: Anupama Saroj Singh, a Provincial Civil Services (PCS) officer who served as Deputy Commissioner (GST) in the Uttar Pradesh government, has taken voluntary retirement from service. She has since sought a Samajwadi Party ticket to contest the Assembly election from the Sidhauli seat in Sitapur. Anupama says she has entered politics to challenge the barriers in society that prevent people from bringing about change. She also said she admires the partnership between Akhilesh Yadav and Dimple Yadav, as they complement each other. This is one of the reasons she is drawn to the Samajwadi Party. Asked where she plans to contest the election, she said she has a deep emotional connection with Sitapur. Anupama is the wife of Samajwadi Party national spokesperson Anurag Bhadauria and the daughter of former MP Sushila Saroj. Her mother has served as a Lok Sabha MP and was also a minister in the Mulayam Singh Yadav government. Her husband has contested the Lucknow East Assembly seat and served as a minister in the Akhilesh Yadav government. Anupama is also a singer and composer. Anupama talks about her musical journey and favourite singers In an exclusive conversation with a Dainik Bhaskar reporter, Anupama spoke about her interest in music. She said Rahat Fateh Ali Khan is her favourite singer and that she has composed several songs for him, which he has also sung. She also enjoys Sonu Nigam's music. Among contemporary singers, she likes Arijit Singh's songs, although she has not yet had the opportunity to work with him. Read the full conversation with Anupama - Question: How are you feeling after leaving your job? Answer: I am feeling quite free from stress. I am spending time with my family during the festival. The word retirement itself means being free from work. However, I still have a great deal of responsibility and many challenges ahead of me. I am now quite excited about this new journey, as I have a lot to do there. I have an open sky before me. Question: You have taken VRS, and since then, speculation about you entering politics has intensified? Answer: Politics is a very broad term. It can be a means of connecting with society, but that is not my primary objective. My main aim is to break the barriers that make people feel uncomfortable about connecting with society. I have some ideas of my own and want to work on them. I want to improve the things around me. I now feel free from constraints; it feels as though there is a canvas in front of me that I have to fill with colour. In our family, my mother and maternal grandfather were involved in politics and served society through it. I simply want to take that work forward. Question: You come from a political background and resigned just before the election. Will you contest the 2027 election? Answer: I am not in a position right now to reveal anything or say whether I will contest an election or enter politics in the future. I have many thoughts and feel deeply for the people. When I feel the time is right to use my administrative experience and energy to help improve society, a decision will be taken. Question: Recently, IAS officer Divya Mittal left her job and entered politics. Has politics gained the upper hand over the bureaucracy? Answer: I would not say that politics has gained the upper hand over the bureaucracy. Everyone has their own priorities and perspective. People leave their jobs for personal reasons. There is no political pressure. Yes, politics is certainly connected to all our lives. People have moved from the bureaucracy to the corporate sector or other sectors; not everyone enters politics. Question: Do you have a preferred constituency from which you would like to contest the election? Answer: (Laughing) I like the whole of India. I am a daughter of India, and I will contest from wherever fate decides. We will see what happens from there. My mother contested from Mohanlalganj, and we campaigned for her during our childhood. We also have a deep connection with Sitapur. We have observed politics closely since childhood. However, no decision of this kind has been taken yet. I also like music very much. We have composed songs for Rahat Fateh Ali Khan and Mika Singh. They have sung our songs. Music is my soul. You may hear my songs on social issues in the future. Question: Who is your favourite singer? Answer: Rahat Fateh Ali Khan. I have written songs for him. Apart from him, I also like Sonu Nigam very much. Among young artists, I particularly like Arijit Singh. It has been my misfortune that I have not yet been able to work with him. Question: Which political personality do you like the most? Answer: Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Mulayam Singh are among my favourite leaders. We have had a close family relationship with Mulayam Singh. I particularly like Atal ji's thinking and the way he spoke, especially his poetry. Among women, I like Dimple Yadav very much; her way of speaking and simplicity have deeply impressed me. It is her simplicity that takes her family forward. Question: We are living in the Gen Z era. How do you view it? Answer: The Gen Z movement that has emerged is a symbol that our country needs change. We were looking at the countries around us and sensing that this movement would now reach India. We saw that the issues affecting the countries around us were the same issues affecting our country. We saw that change was needed. Gen Z is the largest population group in our country, and its members will make sure they achieve what they want. At a time like this, the new generation should come forward, and whatever change takes place will be brought about by Gen Z. Question: There is a lot of talk about couples in politics. Who is your favourite couple? Answer: We see only one couple in politics: Akhilesh Yadav and Dimple Yadav. They complement each other very well. The values they uphold are also reflected in the party. They consider their party workers members of their family, and all the workers address them as Bhaiya and Bhabhi.

stories.title: Former MP Rajesh Mishra eyes PM Modi's Varanasi seat:Puts up posters signalling 2029 Lok Sabha bid after joining BJP from Congress
stories.summary: A poster featuring former MP Rajesh Mishra has triggered political discussions in Varanasi ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. The former Congress leader, who joined the BJP, has signalled his intention to contest the 2029 Lok Sabha elections from Varanasi. Mishra has staked his claim to the seat represented by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who has won it three consecutive times. He has released a poster featuring the BJP's lotus symbol and shared it on his social media accounts. His move to stake a claim to the Varanasi seat has sparked discussions within the BJP. His supporters have also posted comments expressing their support, while BJP leaders have largely avoided commenting on the development. On Tuesday night, former MP Rajesh Mishra changed his display picture and cover photo on Facebook and X, triggering discussions in Varanasi and national political circles. The poster projects him as a strong contender for the BJP ticket from Varanasi in 2029. This is the first time a BJP leader has publicly staked a claim to the seat represented by the Prime Minister, drawing attention in both BJP and opposition circles. The party may also view Mishra's social media post as a matter of indiscipline. Rajesh Mishra joined BJP three years ago Former Varanasi MP Dr Rajesh Mishra joined the BJP three years ago. At the party's central office in Delhi, former Union Minister Ravi Shankar Prasad inducted him as a primary member of the BJP. Mishra had said that opposition parties would not even find polling agents for their candidates in the Varanasi constituency. He had also described it as a matter of pride that Narendra Modi represented Varanasi and had brought recognition to the city and the country worldwide. Rajesh Mishra represented Varanasi in 2004 Rajesh Mishra is known as a soft-spoken politician in Varanasi. He began his political journey through student politics at Banaras Hindu University (BHU). In the 1980s, he was elected president of the BHU Students' Union. From 1996 to 2004, he served two terms as a member of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council (MLC). In the 1999 Lok Sabha elections, the Congress fielded him against BJP candidate Shankar Prasad Jaiswal from Varanasi. Mishra lost that election but defeated Jaiswal in 2004 to win the Varanasi Lok Sabha seat. Lost to Murli Manohar Joshi in 2009 The Congress fielded Mishra for the third consecutive time in 2009. The BJP nominated Dr Murli Manohar Joshi, while Mukhtar Ansari contested on a BSP ticket. After falling out with the BJP, Ajay Rai contested the election on a Samajwadi Party ticket. Vote polarisation is believed to have pushed Mishra down to fourth place. Joshi secured 2,03,122 votes, Mukhtar Ansari received 1,85,911, Ajay Rai got 1,23,874, while Mishra secured 66,386 votes. Expressed displeasure after being denied ticket in 2014 In 2014, the Congress dropped Mishra and fielded Ajay Rai against Narendra Modi, then the BJP's prime ministerial candidate. Three years later, the Varanasi South Assembly constituency became a major political talking point during the 2017 Assembly elections. The BJP's decision to deny a ticket to seven-time MLA Shyamdev Roy Chowdhury, popularly known as Dada, had created difficulties for the party. The BJP fielded Neelkanth Tiwari, while the Congress nominated Rajesh Mishra against him. Prime Minister Narendra Modi stayed in Varanasi and campaigned during the election. Tiwari defeated Mishra. In the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, the Congress again gave Mishra a ticket, this time from Salempur in his home district of Deoria. However, he secured only 27,288 votes and lost his security deposit. Poster creates buzz amid Assembly election discussions Rajesh Mishra represented Varanasi in the Lok Sabha from 2004 to 2009. There had been discussions about fielding him from Bhadohi or another constituency in the Assembly elections when his poster staking a claim to the 2029 Varanasi Lok Sabha ticket surfaced. Mishra's decision to join the BJP had been a major setback for the Congress. He was reportedly unhappy with Ajay Rai's appointment as the state Congress president. However, following Rai's removal, speculation has also emerged about Mishra potentially returning to the Congress. There is also speculation over whether PM Modi will contest the next Lok Sabha election from Varanasi or retire from electoral politics there. Political observers are interpreting Mishra's poster as a possible calculated political move. Mishra yet to get a significant position in BJP Despite joining the BJP from the Congress, Mishra has not received a prominent organisational position in the party, according to the report. His political influence is also said to have declined over the past three years. Several of his former associates have reportedly distanced themselves from him, while his role within the BJP has remained limited. During the Prime Minister's visits, Mishra has reportedly been seen among those welcoming him from behind barricades.

stories.title: Air quality worsens in Noida-Ghaziabad, AQI crosses 300:Fog covers western UP districts; temperatures to drop in 2 days
stories.summary: Fog and haze have increased across Uttar Pradesh after Diwali. The Meteorological Department has issued an alert for dense fog in the state on Wednesday. Temperatures are also expected to drop, with severe cold likely to begin after two days. Visibility dropped to zero in Varanasi on Tuesday morning due to dense fog. In Bareilly, visibility was limited to 100 metres, while it was 300 metres in the state capital, Lucknow. Dense fog also covered 15 cities, including Sambhal, Hapur, Bijnor and Shamli. Hardoi and Bareilly were the coldest places, with minimum temperatures of 13.5°C and 14.2°C, respectively. BHU meteorologist Prof. Manoj Srivastava said, "Minimum temperatures will fall further as dry north-westerly winds become stronger. This will make the cold more intense." Weather in four major districts - Lucknow: Cold conditions have increased in the city. Light fog was seen in the morning, while the air quality remained poor. The AQI was recorded at 200. - Kanpur: Cold winds have been blowing since morning, and light mist was seen on the roads. Weather expert Dr S.N. Sunil Pandey said sunshine would cause temperatures to rise during the day, but it would remain cold at night. - Varanasi: The weather remained clear in the city, but haze was visible after Diwali fireworks. Humidity in the air also made the weather feel cold. - Prayagraj: The weather remained clear, but strong winds made it feel cold. Dense fog continued in rural areas, while mist was seen in the city. Know the temperatures recorded over the past 24 hours What is the Air Quality Index (AQI)? It is a score that indicates the quality of the air and helps us understand whether the air around us is clean or polluted. The AQI measures the levels of pollutants present in the air. The higher the AQI, the more dangerous the air is considered to be, and the greater the health risk. Understand it through the graphic below- How does poor AQI affect our health? When the AQI is poor, pollutants such as PM2.5, PM10, nitrogen dioxide, sulphur dioxide and ozone present in the air reach deep into our lungs. These particles spread throughout the body through the bloodstream. They can cause various health problems, ranging from immediate effects to long-term conditions. stories.title: 3 more special trains to run via Gorakhpur for Chhath:Travel to Delhi, Bihar, Mumbai to become easier; check dates timings
stories.summary: Railways has announced three additional special train services to manage the rush of passengers travelling home for Chhath after Diwali and returning to work. These trains will run between Muzaffarpur and Delhi, Ramnagar and Patliputra, and Mumbai and Gorakhpur. A festival special train will make one trip between Muzaffarpur and Anand Vihar Terminal via Gorakhpur. The running period of the Ramnagar-Patliputra weekly special train has also been extended, with one additional trip planned. Meanwhile, a 20-coach special train will run between Mumbai's Lokmanya Tilak Terminus and Gorakhpur from November 10. These services will make travel easier for passengers travelling to and from Bihar, eastern Uttar Pradesh, Lucknow, Delhi and Mumbai. Special train from Muzaffarpur to Delhi on November 18 Train number 05281, the Muzaffarpur-Anand Vihar Terminal Festival Special, will leave Muzaffarpur at 6:30 am on November 18. stories.title: Shopkeeper shot dead in Ghazipur market:Chased attacker before collapsing, struggled for life on road for 5 minutes, cried for help
stories.summary: A young man was shot dead in the middle of a market in Ghazipur on Tuesday evening (November 10). He ran a footwear shop and was returning home when a man in a car rammed into his motorbike, causing him to fall. The attacker then fired three rounds at him. One bullet struck the victim on the left side of his neck, while another hit his abdomen. Despite being injured, he ran about 20 metres behind the attacker's car before collapsing on the road. Victim names Shubham as shooter before collapsing As he lay injured, the young man repeatedly took Shubham's name and shouted, "Shubham has shot me, save me." Local residents immediately rushed him to hospital, where he died during treatment. DIG of the Varanasi zone Vaibhav Krishna also reached the spot and sought details of the incident from officials. Police suspect old enmity behind the murder According to the police, Shubham and the footwear shop owner had an old dispute. Two days before the shooting, Shubham had lodged a complaint with the police, alleging that the shopkeeper had thrown a bomb at him and attempted to kill him. The deceased was his parents' only son. See 2 pictures... Read the full story... Mohammad Daud lives in the Muftipura neighbourhood with his only son, 28-year-old Mohammad Kausen. Kausen ran a footwear shop in the Rauza area. The family of Anil Chaubey, who has since died, lives near the Niyazi Ganga Temple, around 3 km away. His son, Shubham Chaubey, lives at the house. On November 8, Shubham lodged a police complaint alleging that Kausen had thrown a bomb at him and attempted to kill him. On Tuesday, Kausen had gone to Mishra Bazaar to eat samosas. Shortly after leaving the area on his motorcycle, he was near the State Bank when Shubham allegedly rammed his vehicle into the bike. He collided with an e-rickshaw and fell on the road. Shubham then opened fire, hitting him with two bullets and leaving him critically injured. Local residents alerted an ambulance and rushed Kausen to hospital. Despite receiving treatment, he died. Following Kausen's death, his father, Mohammad Daud, accused Shubham Chaubey of murdering his son. Case was registered against Kausen in 2025 Vaibhav Krishna, DIG of the Varanasi Range, who reached the scene, said that Shubham and Kausen had an old rivalry. A case was registered in 2025 involving Kausen and Shubham's father, Anil Chaubey. Kausen was accused of firing a shot in the case. The police also filed a charge sheet. The DIG said that a case had been registered against Shubham.
