IAS Anjaneya transfers government land to businessman's name:Land worth ₹40 crore, Rampur officials baffled; seek guidance from Revenue Council on what to do
stories.summary: IAS officer Anjaneya Kumar Singh, who had sent Azam Khan to jail, is once again in the headlines. This time, the reason is not Azam Khan but a land scam. Government land worth ₹40 crore in Rampur was transferred in the name of a businessman. The order was issued by the Moradabad Commissioner’s Court. IAS officer Anjaneya Singh was the commissioner at the time. When the businessman reached the Rampur Collectorate with a copy of the order to get his name entered on the Bhulekh portal, officials were taken aback. The land that the businessman had got transferred in his name through the Moradabad Commissioner’s Court in 2024 was actually government land. This means it could only be used for public purposes such as ponds, roads, burial grounds or cremation grounds. It could not be sold to anyone. However, the Moradabad Commissioner’s Court had declared the land ‘Sankramaniya Bhumidhar’. This meant that the government would no longer be the owner of the land; instead, the businessman would have ownership rights. He could then sell the land or use it for any other purpose. After examining the documents at the Rampur Collectorate, officials suspected irregularities and immediately stopped the process. The Rampur administration has written to the ‘Commissioner and Secretary, Board of Revenue’ seeking clarity on the next course of action. Read the sequence of events to understand how the irregularity began… The land is located near Sarai Darwaza in the Sadar tehsil area of Rampur. Measuring 4,355.72 square metres, it is recorded in the revenue records under Khata No. 11 and Gata No. 34/1. The tehsil records classify it as ‘Shikmi Kashtkar’ under Category 15 of the Non-ZA land category. Non-ZA land refers to land to which the Zamindari Abolition Act (ZA Act) does not apply and which is owned by the government. Temporary permission may be granted to cultivate such land, but it cannot be sold to any individual. SDM court had to say: It has no jurisdiction to hear the case According to businessman Dr Mahmood Ali Khan, he purchased the land from Wajahat Ali Rizvi on 6 April 2019. When he attempted to carry out construction on the land, the administration stopped him. Following this, Dr Mahmood Ali Khan filed a petition in the court of the SDM, Rampur. He sought to be declared a ‘Sankramaniya Bhumidhar’ of the land, which would give him ownership rights and the authority to sell it. After hearing the matter, the SDM court rejected his claim on 16 January 2024. The court clearly stated in its order that the land was entirely owned by the state government. The court said the SDM court did not have the jurisdiction to hear cases involving such land. No provision of the UP Revenue Code, 2006, or the Uttar Pradesh Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950, granted it such authority. The petition was therefore dismissed. Moradabad court overturned the SDM court's order Following this, Dr Mahmood Ali Khan filed a petition in the Moradabad Commissioner’s Court. He argued that he had this right under Section 207 of the Uttar Pradesh Revenue Code, 2006. This section states that if an SDM or tehsildar passes an order against a person in a revenue matter and the person is dissatisfied with it, they can appeal to the commissioner or the Board of Revenue. During the hearing, the Moradabad Commissioner’s Court overturned the order passed by the Sadar SDM court and ruled in favour of Dr Mahmood Ali Khan. It declared him a ‘Sankramaniya Bhumidhar’, thereby granting him the right to sell the land. The court stated in its order that the provisions of the UP Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act were also applicable to Non-ZA land located within the limits of Rampur Municipality. While issuing this order, the Moradabad Commissioner’s Court also cited earlier cases. However, questions are now being raised over the legal basis of the earlier cases used to justify the new order. It is being argued that those very precedents were incorrect. - In its verdict, the Commissioner’s Court referred to the case of Uttar Pradesh Government vs Akhilesh Kumar, decided by Dr Sudheeran Mahadev Bobde, a member of the Board of Revenue in Lucknow. However, that order concerned Category 5 Non-ZA land in Rampur itself. Category 5 land is agricultural land, whereas the disputed property falls under Category 15, which is public land. Applying rules meant for agricultural land to public land is now being considered legally inappropriate. - While delivering its verdict, the Moradabad Commissioner’s Court ignored an order dated 5 June 2023, passed by DS Upadhyay, a member of the Board of Revenue in Prayagraj, in the case of Uttar Pradesh Government vs Jameel Khan. That order also concerned Non-ZA land in Rampur. In it, the Board of Revenue had clearly rejected the claim made by a private individual. Earlier, the Additional Commissioner’s Court in Moradabad had taken the view that the provisions of the Zamindari Abolition Act automatically applied to all land in Uttar Pradesh. The Board of Revenue in Prayagraj completely rejected this interpretation. It clarified that the Supreme Court had held that applying the ZA Act to all land was incorrect. According to a government order issued on 15 June 2012, zamindari cannot be abolished in urban areas, nor can any urban Non-ZA land (government/public land) be converted into ZA land (private land).

stories.title: Shivpal says, ‘Don't threaten officials’:Why he had to issue a warning; Akhilesh to remove ‘outspoken’ leaders, BJP came to power in 2022 by building ‘red cap, hooliganism’ narrative
stories.summary: If any party worker threatens people by saying, ‘We will deal with you once our government comes to power’, the district president should immediately expel them from the party. Shivpal Yadav, Saifai, 8 November The Samajwadi Party’s national general secretary issued a stern warning. A month ago, Akhilesh Yadav had also cautioned party leaders against making aggressive statements. With the 2027 Assembly elections just three months away, the SP fears that the BJP could deliberately provoke its leaders into making inflammatory remarks and then use them to corner and discredit the party. This fear has not emerged suddenly. Before the 2022 Assembly elections, the BJP had already built a narrative against the SP by highlighting statements made by its MPs and MLAs and linking the party’s red caps with hooliganism. As a result, the SP failed to form the government. Although it gained 64 Assembly seats and increased its vote share by more than 10 percentage points, the BJP managed to form the government with 273 seats. After its defeat in 2022, Akhilesh Yadav moved away from the party’s MY (Muslim-Yadav) equation and formed the PDA alliance, introducing a new formula based on backward classes, Dalits and minorities. The SP also demonstrated the effectiveness of this formula in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections by giving greater representation to non-Yadav and non-Muslim communities. As a result, the party gained a total of 32 seats. 2019 Lok Sabha elections: The SP contested in an alliance with the BSP and won only five seats. 2024 Lok Sabha elections: The SP contested in an alliance with the Congress and won 37 seats. Both Akhilesh and Shivpal know that the PDA formula will remain strong only if the party is seen as ‘decent’ and ‘disciplined’ among the public. If the SP continues to carry its old image of ‘strong-arm tactics’, it will struggle to win the trust of Dalits and the most backward communities. Warned leaders by showing old clips from TV debates Akhilesh has also been strict about discipline within the party for some time. In October, he called a meeting of party spokespersons at the SP headquarters and asked them to improve their language. He also played old video clips of Rajkumar Bhati, Anurag Bhadauria, Ameek Jamei, Manoj Kaka and Manoj Yadav. Akhilesh pointed out their shortcomings and instructed them to avoid aggressive and abusive language during TV debates. He asked them to go fully prepared so that the party’s ideology and development agenda could be presented effectively. All these efforts are being made because the BJP has consistently been reminding people of the period before 2017. It alleges that an atmosphere of security was established under the BJP government. Now, if the SP wants to corner the BJP over unemployment, inflation and farmers’ issues, it will have to shed its old image. Statements by SP leaders in 2022 that derailed the party’s campaign Before voting in the first phase of the 2022 Assembly elections, aggressive statements by SP leaders had started emerging in Meerut. BJP linked these statements to law and order and the ‘return of anarchy’. As a result, floating voters who were moving closer to the SP became apprehensive and backed away. Floating voters are those who are not committed to any particular political party or ideology and make their voting decisions independently. SP uncomfortable with statements by these leaders in 2026 Sanatan Pandey defended Mulayam’s order to open fire On 8 November, SP MP from Ballia, Sanatan Pandey, defended Mulayam Singh Yadav’s decision to order firing on kar sevaks in Ayodhya. He said: “If the then Chief Minister, Netaji, ordered firing to protect the Constitution of India, it was absolutely the right step. Had this not been done, the structure or the temple could have been damaged. This could have created a situation similar to a civil war in the country. Therefore, the order to open fire was given only to protect the Constitution.” As soon as his statement came to light, the BJP began targeting the SP. Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak hit back, saying that although his name was ‘Sanatan’, his thinking was completely anti-Sanatan, anti-Ram and anti-Hindu. As the controversy grew, Pandey backtracked the very next day, on 9 November. He held a press conference in Ballia to clarify his remarks. He said: “I never said that we had ordered the firing. I was only saying that Netaji had unwavering faith in the Constitution.” Sharafat Ali made a controversial remark about the district panchayat chairperson On 30 September, the SP organised a ‘PDA conference’ in Gopamau town of Hardoi. During the event, former party district president Sharafat Ali made a controversial remark about Premavati PK Verma, the BJP-backed district panchayat chairperson. He said: “If Mulayam Singh Yadav had not strengthened the reservation system, Premavati would have been washing clothes at a dhobi ghat today.” His statement went viral on social media. Following this, district panchayat chairperson Premavati Verma became emotional. She said: “I am proud of my Dhobi caste. Do I look like someone who washes clothes? My parents educated me. I became a teacher and later entered politics.” Premavati Verma also lodged an FIR against Sharafat Ali under the SC/ST Act. Rajkumar Bhati made a remark about the Brahmin community and later apologised On 5 May 2026, SP national spokesperson Rajkumar Bhati made a controversial remark about the Brahmin community during a book launch event in Delhi. Speaking from the stage, he said: “A Brahmin is no better than a prostitute, and no one is worse than a Brahmin! Some prostitutes may be decent, but no Brahmin is.” BJP leaders called the statement an insult to the Brahmin community. An FIR was subsequently registered against him at Kavi Nagar police station in Ghaziabad. As the controversy grew, Rajkumar Bhati issued an unconditional apology. What does the SP spokesperson say? Speaking about the SP’s strategy, the party’s national spokesperson, Dr Ashutosh Verma, said the BJP was always looking for opportunities to damage the SP’s image. That is why the party’s top leadership had asked its leaders to be careful while speaking. He added that even during the MLC elections, when SP candidates were winning, Akhilesh Yadav had issued strict instructions. He had told party workers not to indulge in any kind of disorder or lose their composure in the heat of the moment.

stories.title: Municipal Corporation lifts 37 lakh kg waste in 9 days:Gorakhpur stays clean during Diwali; sanitation drive covers markets and streets
stories.summary: Gorakhpur Municipal Corporation launched a special campaign to maintain cleanliness in the city during Diwali. Over the nine-day festival, the municipal corporation disposed of 3,719.23 tonnes of waste. The waste was collected through GTS (Garbage Transfer Station) centres and other means between 1 and 9 November. The total quantity of waste was 37,19,227 kilograms. Lifting and disposing of such a large quantity of waste during the festival was a major challenge for the municipal corporation. On Diwali, the city's markets, commercial areas and main roads saw heavier crowds than usual. Shopping also led to an increase in waste at shops and markets. In addition, large quantities of waste were generated from house cleaning and festival preparations. In view of this, the municipal corporation launched a special cleanliness campaign from 1 November. Under the campaign, special attention was paid to cleanliness in the city's main markets, religious sites, public places, ghats and residential areas. Additional sanitation workers assigned for duty Additional sanitation workers were deployed in all the city's wards during the campaign. The door-to-door waste collection system was made more effective so that household waste did not spill onto the streets. Additional vehicles were arranged to collect waste from markets and crowded areas. This helped ensure that the waste was collected on time and transported to designated locations. Cleaning was also carried out at night, including drains As markets and major roads were more crowded during the day during the festival, cleaning was also carried out at night. A night-sweeping arrangement was made for this purpose. Along with cleaning the roads, attention was also paid to cleaning drains and ensuring proper water drainage. Lime and insecticides were sprayed in public places. In addition, repairing street lights was also undertaken as a priority so that people would not face difficulty travelling at night. Officials were assigned responsibility for monitoring Senior municipal corporation officials, zonal officers and sanitation inspectors were assigned duties to ensure the cleanliness drive was conducted in an organised manner. They were instructed to continuously monitor sanitation arrangements in their respective areas and ensure there was no negligence in waste collection. The municipal corporation claims that the 3,719.23 tonnes of waste collected during the campaign was disposed of scientifically and in an environmentally friendly manner. The municipal corporation said special arrangements had been made to keep the city clean during the festival. The campaign sought to maintain cleanliness in markets, public places and residential areas.

stories.title: Man convicted in Rampur CRPF camp attack shot dead:Released from jail exactly a year ago
stories.summary: Mohammad Sharif (53), a convict in the CRPF camp attack in Rampur, Uttar Pradesh, was shot dead. The incident took place around 50 km from the district headquarters and just 400 metres from Khajuria police station. On Tuesday evening, Mohammad Sharif had gone to the police station with his son to mark his attendance. At around 7 pm, Sharif was returning home on a motorcycle, with his son riding it. Two unidentified assailants on a motorcycle approached from behind, shot Sharif in the temple and fled. On seeing his father being shot, his son was left in shock and collapsed on the ground. Sharif was taken to hospital, where he died during treatment. Police are searching for the attackers. In the 2007 CRPF camp attack in Rampur, seven personnel and a rickshaw puller were killed. The Rampur court had sentenced Mohammad Sharif to death in the case. Later, the Allahabad High Court acquitted him in the terror case, except for the Arms Act charges. He was released from jail exactly a year ago, on 10 November. See two pictures related to the incident… Read the 18-year-and-10-month-old FIR… Terrorists opened fire on police before entering the CRPF centre The FIR related to the attack on the CRPF Group Centre in Rampur on the night of 31 December 2007 was registered at Civil Lines police station on 1 January 2008. It was filed by Sub-Inspector Om Prakash Sharma. According to the FIR, he was on patrol with Constables Indrapal Singh and Jitendra Singh, Home Guard Aftab Khan and driver Jaswant Singh. Gunshots heard at 12.25 am The police team reached the CRPF toll barrier at around 12.25 am. They heard gunshots coming from the direction of Gate No. 1 of the Group Centre. At around 2.30 am, the policemen spotted four to five armed men in the light of an electric bulb. They were carrying automatic weapons and firing at CRPF personnel. Policemen also returned fire According to the FIR, Constable Indrapal Singh fired eight rounds, Jitendra Singh fired seven, Virendra Rana fired five and Home Guard Aftab Khan fired five rounds. The terrorists also retaliated. Indrapal Singh and Aftab Khan were injured in the exchange of fire. Indrapal's rifle was also damaged. Terrorists entered CRPF centre and opened indiscriminate fire After overpowering the police team, the attackers entered the CRPF centre and opened indiscriminate fire. Seven CRPF personnel were killed in the attack. They were Constable Devendra, Vikas Kumar, Head Constables Rishikesh Rai, Afzal Ahmed and Ramjeet Saran Mishra, and Constables Anand Kumar and Manveer Singh. An unidentified rickshaw puller was also killed. FIR registered under these sections A case was registered at Civil Lines police station in Rampur under Sections 147, 148, 149, 307, 302 and 332 of the IPC, Sections 3/5 of the PDPP Act and Section 3 of the Explosives Act. Rampur court sentenced him to death in 2019 On 9 January 2008, Ashok Kumar Raghav, the then Additional SP, arrested three accused — Baba alias Jung Bahadur, Mohammad Sharif alias Sohel and Faheem alias Arshad with weapons in connection with the CRPF camp attack in Rampur. The next day, on 10 January, Imran Shehzad, Mohammad Farooq and Sabauddin were also arrested. The police filed a chargesheet and several supplementary chargesheets in the case. The prosecution presented a total of 38 witnesses before the court. On 2 November 2019, the Rampur court found Mohammad Sharif, Sabauddin, Imran Shehzad and Mohammad Farooq guilty of murder and sentenced them to death. Jung Bahadur Khan was sentenced to life imprisonment. Two of the accused challenged the verdict in the Allahabad High Court. The Jamiat Ulama-i-Hind represented them in the High Court. High Court acquitted Mohammad Sharif in 2025 On 29 October 2025, the Allahabad High Court acquitted Mohammad Sharif and the other accused of the major charges related to murder and terrorism after finding serious lapses in the investigation. The court also raised questions about the recovery of weapons, gaps in the chain of custody of evidence and identification procedures. However, the court upheld their conviction under the Arms Act and sentenced them to 10 years in prison. After adjusting the period already spent in jail, Mohammad Sharif was released in November 2025. High Court verdict challenged in Supreme Court The Uttar Pradesh government challenged the Allahabad High Court's verdict in the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court issued a notice in the matter.

stories.title: Yadav community upset over Dhirendra Shastri's remark in Varanasi:Says he insulted Sanatan Dharma; calls Shri Krishna their clan deity
stories.summary: Opposition continues in Varanasi to a statement made by Dhirendra Krishna Shastri, peethadhishwar of Bageshwar Dham, about Lord Krishna. Members of the Yadav community expressed their displeasure over the issue during the Govardhan Yatra. Some called it an insult to Sanatan Dharma, while others said that Lord Krishna was their clan guru and that such comments about him were unacceptable. People demanded that the state government bar such storytellers from entering Uttar Pradesh. Some also called for strict action against Dhirendra Shastri. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to members of the Yadav community. Read the report... First, learn about the controversy- On 29 October, during a Ram Katha in Karera, Madhya Pradesh's Shivpuri district, Bageshwar Dham Peethadhishwar Dhirendra Krishna Shastri commented while comparing Lord Ram and Lord Krishna. Comparing Lord Shri Ram with Shri Krishna, he said- "Just look at even one photograph of your Thakurji. Even when he stands, he is bent at three places. One foot over the other, sometimes he sways his waist and plays the flute with his neck tilted. "Our one even stands upright-perfectly straight. Our one's name is straight too. Our one's walk is straight, and our one looks straight as well. Your ones' name is crooked, they walk crookedly and even stand crookedly." "Lifting a mountain is no great feat. A disciple of our Lord flew off with an entire mountain. Our ones' holy place is straight too-Ayodhya, while your one's is Vrindavan!" However, as the controversy grew, Dhirendra Shastri released a video clarifying his remarks. He said, "Many people have misunderstood what I said. We ourselves are devotees of Thakurji and Braj. Whenever we pray to Thakurji, we ask to be granted residence in Braj." "We also recite the Shrimad Bhagwat Katha and sing the praises of Thakurji. We had no intention of differentiating between Lord Ram and Lord Krishna." Several political leaders, including Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, had also raised objections in the matter. Read what people said- One should not make such remarks about God Rakesh Kumar Yadav said that Dhirendra Shastri should neither be allowed to enter Kashi nor to come anywhere in Uttar Pradesh. Ramnarayan Yadav said that making such remarks about Lord Krishna was wrong. One should not say such things about Lord Krishna to show one's influence. This has hurt the sentiments of devotees. Ram Babu said: Such people have no right to live in the country Eleven-year-old Shivani Yadav said that what Dhirendra Shastri had said was wrong. Ram Babu Yadav expressed his displeasure, saying that Dhirendra Shastri should not make such remarks. Such people should be expelled from the country. Aarti said: One should think before speaking Aarti Yadav said that no one should make such comments about any god. People should think about their words before speaking. Ankita Yadav said that Dhirendra Shastri had questioned Lord Krishna, even though he was their family guru. He should not have made such a comment.

stories.title: Voters can add names to electoral rolls till December 16:Draft voter list to be released on November 17; one month for claims and objections
stories.summary: The schedule for the Special Summary Revision (SSR) of the electoral roll has been changed amid preparations for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. The draft electoral roll for all 403 Assembly constituencies in the state will now be published on 17 November. It was earlier scheduled to be published on 12 November. Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa said on Tuesday that the Election Commission of India had issued a revised schedule for the Special Summary Revision-2027 being conducted with 1 January 2027 as the qualifying date. Under the revised schedule, claims and objections for adding or deleting names from the electoral roll and correcting registered details will be accepted from 17 November to 16 December. Claims and objections to be resolved by 28 December According to the revised schedule, after the draft electoral roll is published, citizens will have the opportunity to check their names and those of their family members on the electoral roll. During this period, people whose names are not included in the roll can apply to have them added. Applications can also be submitted under the prescribed procedure to correct incorrect entries and remove ineligible names. The Election Commission will have to dispose of the claims and objections received by 16 December by 28 December 2026. The final electoral roll will be published on 4 January 2027. There has been no change to the date of the final publication. Political parties will also be informed The Chief Electoral Officer has directed all District Election Officers to widely publicise the revised schedule through newspapers, electronic media and other communication channels. They have also been asked to inform recognised national and state-level political parties about the new timetable. All Electoral Registration Officers and Assistant Electoral Registration Officers have been instructed to complete the revision-related process within the stipulated timeframe. Appeal to Check Voter Lists Before the Election The Chief Electoral Officer has appealed to the citizens of the state to check their own entries and those of their family members after the draft electoral roll is published. Eligible citizens whose names are not on the list can apply within the stipulated period. The aim is to ensure that no eligible citizen is left out of having their name registered on the electoral roll.

stories.title: Dogs, cats bite 107 people in Varanasi in 2 days:Long queues at hospital for anti-rabies vaccines
stories.summary: Cases of dog, cat and monkey bites have increased in Varanasi after Diwali. A total of 107 people reached hospitals for treatment after being bitten by animals over two days, on 9 and 10 November. Of these, 43 cases were reported on 9 November and 64 on 10 November. People continued to queue at Kabirchaura Divisional Hospital to receive anti-rabies vaccine (ARV) shots. According to experts, animals become frightened by the loud noise, bright lights and smoke from firecrackers. This causes changes in their behaviour, and they may become aggressive. Animals become frightened and stressed by the noise of firecrackers Dr Vimlesh Kumar said that changes in animals' behaviour can be observed around Diwali. This season is also the breeding season for many animals, which can increase their agitation and aggression. In addition, the loud noise of firecrackers and sudden bursts of fireworks frighten animals. Fear and stress can cause them to attack people. Study also highlights the impact of firecrackers The impact of firecrackers on animals has also emerged in scientific studies. Keep pets in a safe and quiet place Dr Vilesh Kumar said preparations should be made before Diwali to protect pets from loud noises. Keep them in a safe and quiet place indoors. Do not leave animals loose while bursting firecrackers, as they may run away or become aggressive out of fear. He said that some medicines are also available to reduce stress in animals, but they should be used only on the advice of a veterinary doctor. Ayurvedic or homoeopathic medicines should also not be given without expert advice.

stories.title: AI to monitor pollution in smart cities:Experts at IIT-BHU say rivers, lakes and green spaces must be protected before urban development begins
stories.summary: Building smart cities will require more than just high-rise buildings and wide roads. It will also be necessary to protect rivers, lakes, greenery and the environment. Sustainable cities can be developed only by integrating the Indian knowledge tradition with modern science and artificial intelligence (AI). With the help of AI, sensors and data systems, pollution sources can be identified and climate-related risks assessed in advance. IIT Kanpur Kotak School of Sustainability Dean Prof. Sachchidanand Tripathi made these remarks at a seminar held at the institute on Tuesday. Experts discussed environmental challenges and their technological solutions at the seminar on 'Emerging Environmental Challenges, Technology and Sustainable Development Goals'. Prof. Tripathi said the concept of dharma in Indian philosophy teaches people to live in balance with nature. He said there was a need to integrate this approach with modern technology today. Rivers and lakes must be protected as cities expand Prof. Tripathi said that cities are expanding rapidly, but natural resources must not be harmed in the name of development. Floodplains along rivers must be protected, old lakes revived and water conservation made part of urban planning. Along with constructing environmentally friendly buildings, the natural habitats of elephants, sparrows and other wildlife must also be preserved. Waste management explained using the example of Maha Kumbh Giving the waste management system at Maha Kumbh 2025 as an example, he said waste should be viewed as a resource rather than a burden. With proper processing, refuse-derived fuel (RDF), or alternative fuel, can be produced from waste. This will not only ensure waste disposal but also provide an energy option. AI will identify where and why pollution is rising Prof. Tripathi said that pollution in cities can be monitored more effectively through AI, sensors, cameras and data systems. This will help identify which areas are experiencing rising pollution and which sources are responsible. Referring to technologies such as SAAQMS-ML, nRTSA and DHSA, he said they can help identify pollution hotspots and the actual sources. This will make it easier to take action as needed in affected areas. Digital technology and climate change also discussed In the first technical session of the seminar, Prof. Tripathi delivered a lecture on the topic, "Wisdom Augmented by Algorithms: The Future of Indian Cities". Prof. Anurag Singh of the Institute of Management Studies at BHU shared his views on digital technology and sustainable consumption. In the second session, Prof. Sarfaraz Alam of BHU discussed future challenges amid global ecological and political changes. Dr Prashant K. Srivastava outlined the prospects for sustainable development in an era of changing climate. Both sessions also featured question-and-answer sessions between experts and participants.

stories.title: History-sheeter killed with bricks in Lucknow:Party with friends turns deadly; body found on rooftop next morning
stories.summary: A history-sheeter was beaten to death with a brick in Lucknow. His blood-soaked body was found on the roof of his house on Tuesday morning. He had been drinking with friends on the roof at night. The sound of loud shouting and bricks being used continued for a long time. The family assumed that the men were creating a ruckus while drunk. The family members began screaming after seeing the body on the roof in the morning. Several cases had been registered against Ramashankar, alias Chhotu Kalia, 55. The incident took place in the Manak Nagar area. See two pictures... Read the full incident... The party began at 10 p.m. Ramashankar was a resident of Manak Nagar. The family comprises two sons, Ashu and Vivek, and a married daughter, Khushi. His elder son, Ashu, lives in Ashiana. In a complaint filed with the police, his son stated that between around 10 and 11 p.m. on 9 November, his father, Ramashankar alias Chhotu Kalia, was holding a party on the roof of the house with his friend Veeresh Bahadur Singh alias Kinky and four or five other people. Sounds of shouting and bricks being hurled were heard During this time, loud shouting and sounds of bricks being hurled could be heard from the roof. When family members went up to the roof at around 10 a.m. on Tuesday, they found the father lying dead in a pool of blood. The police control room was then informed. The Manak Nagar police and a forensic team reached the spot and collected evidence from the scene. The body has been sent for a post-mortem examination. Ten cases of robbery, snatching and murder are registered against Rameshankar at different police stations in Lucknow. There is a murder case against him in Krishnanagar. All the cases date back to before 1998; no case has been registered recently. Son files complaint against one named accused and 5 unidentified people His son Ashu filed a complaint in the matter against the named accused, Veeresh Bahadur Singh, and 4-5 unidentified people. The police are investigating the case. The reason behind the murder and the roles of those involved in the incident are being ascertained.

stories.title: 10,000 foreign devotees join Govardhan Parikrama:US woman prepares 250kg halwa, says she finds peace here
stories.summary: A huge crowd of devotees has gathered in Mathura today for Govardhan Puja. In Govardhan, devotees are performing the 21-km-long circumambulation of Govardhan Hill by repeatedly lying down on the ground. They are offering 56 bhog dishes, while more than 10,000 foreigners from 40 countries have also arrived. They are singing devotional songs and dancing to the beat of drums and traditional percussion instruments. A 3-km-long queue has formed outside the Banke Bihari Temple in Vrindavan. At ISKCON's cowshed, Giriraj Ji has been made from 2,000 kg of semolina halwa. Gaura Mani Devi Dasi, who came from the United States, prepared 250 kg of halwa. She sang a devotional song and said that coming here brings peace to the mind. According to tradition, during the Dwapar Yuga, Lord Krishna lifted Govardhan Hill on his little finger. After holding it aloft for seven days and seven nights, he humbled Indra's pride and protected the people of Braj. The tradition of Govardhan Puja has continued ever since. stories.title: Jhansi woman TTE tells passenger, 'Are you illiterate?':Says she hates the sight of him; Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw suspends her
stories.summary: A woman TTE who misbehaved with a passenger in Jhansi was suspended on Tuesday. The Railways has also ordered an inquiry against her. The incident took place at Veerangana Lakshmibai Railway Station. The TTE became angry with the passenger after he took time to show his ticket. She allegedly took him to her office when he was unable to show the ticket and reprimanded him harshly. During the incident, she told the passenger: "You are illiterate. Get out of the room immediately. I hate the sight of your face. Get out of here. If we were not busy right now, we would have shown you what we are capable of." The passenger recorded a video of the incident. On 8 November, he posted the video on X and complained to the Railway Minister and railway officials. Taking cognisance of the matter, the officials took action against the TTE. Read the full story... Passenger said: The counter ticket had gone missing from his bag Shravan Kumar (32) said he is from Lakhimpur and works for a motor company in Andhra Pradesh. On 6 November, he was travelling with two colleagues from Penukonda in Andhra Pradesh to Jhansi in the sleeper coach of the Karnataka Express (12627). Shravan had to travel from Jhansi to Lucknow. For this, he had bought a counter ticket from Penukonda to Jhansi and an online ticket from Jhansi to Lucknow. On the ticket from Penukonda to Jhansi, the three passengers had waiting-list numbers 2, 3 and 4. After the chart was prepared, two passengers were allotted RAC on seat number 39 in coach S-2, while the third was allotted RAC on seat number 47. At around 3 a.m. on 8 November, the train reached Jhansi. At the time, TTE Anita Verma was checking tickets at the station. She stopped the three passengers and asked for the counter ticket from Penukonda to Jhansi. According to Shravan, the ticket had gone missing somewhere in his bag. He told the TTE that they had travelled from Andhra Pradesh on the Karnataka Express and had a ticket, but it could not be found in the bag. The TTE then took all three to her office. TTE refused to accept the ticket According to Shravan, TTE Anita Verma asked him about the counter ticket. He told her that the ticket was in his bag but he could not find it at the time. He also asked the TTE to check the PNR. It is alleged that the TTE then began reprimanding him and immediately told him to leave the station. Shravan said he had to travel from Jhansi to Lucknow and had booked an online ticket for the journey. The TTE said that if the online ticket was not confirmed, he would not be allowed to board the train. She also insulted him by calling him "illiterate". Shravan alleges that the TTE said, "I hate the look of your face. If I were not busy, I would tell you what I am capable of." Shravan then searched the bag again and found the counter ticket from Penukonda to Jhansi. Showing the ticket to the TTE, he said that it had been in the bag but he had been unable to find it. He had told her the same thing earlier, yet she still abused him. According to Shravan, the TTE refused to accept the ticket and said that he had brought someone else's ticket from outside. He then said that he would take the Aadhaar cards of all three passengers and verify them, but the TTE was not willing to admit her mistake. TTE suspended after complaint to Railway Minister Shravan recorded a video of the incident and posted it on X on 8 November. He tagged Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and officials of the Jhansi railway division in his complaint. Taking cognisance of the matter, the railway suspended the accused TTE, Anita Verma, on Tuesday. It also ordered an inquiry against her. PRO says, ‘Action taken against TTE after investigation’ Manoj Kumar Singh, public relations officer (PRO) of the Jhansi railway division, said that a passenger had complained about the TTE to the media and on X. The complaint was found to be valid during the investigation. The accused TTE, Anita Verma, was subsequently suspended.

stories.title: Government schoolteacher beaten to death in Basti:Congress women's wing chief accused of murder; sticks and knives used in attack
stories.summary: A government schoolteacher was beaten to death in Basti, Uttar Pradesh. Neighbours attacked Sudha Yadav with sticks and knives at around 8 am on Tuesday. Her family members rushed her to the district hospital with severe injuries. She died during treatment at around 1 pm. The incident took place in Tahir village under the jurisdiction of Kalwari police station. Complaint filed alleging she got the job using fake documents Sudha Yadav worked at a government school in Gonda. Her neighbour, Lakshmi Yadav, who is also from the same village, had complained that Sudha had secured the job using fake certificates. The two families had a long-standing dispute over this issue. Son says attackers used sticks and knives Her son, Akhilesh Yadav, said, "Lakshmi came in the morning. My mother and father were working at home when she started abusing them as she approached. "After some time, Alok Yadav, Premchand Yadav and three or four others from Lakshmi's house arrived, along with three or four unidentified people. They were carrying sticks and knives and attacked our family members." CO says Lakshmi had come to her maternal home Kalwari Circle Officer (CO) Brijesh Singh said, "Lakshmi Devi was coming to her maternal home in Tahirpur from her in-laws' house in Baijalpur. An idol was being installed at her maternal home. As soon as she reached near Sudha's house, an argument broke out between the two sides. “Lakshmi called her family members over the phone. A fight broke out between the two sides. Sudha, her husband and other family members were injured in the incident. They are all undergoing treatment. Police have taken the accused into custody for questioning.” This report is being continuously updated...

stories.title: Woman tied up and kicked in Lucknow:Hung upside down, beaten on private parts with sticks; inspector calls it a minor assault case
stories.summary: A mentally ill woman was tied up with a rope and brutally beaten on suspicion of theft in a slum settlement in Sugamau, located in Lucknow's Indiranagar. The accused knocked her to the ground and kicked her in the chest and private parts. She screamed and cried out for help, but no one took pity on her. A video of the incident has surfaced. It shows more than 40 people surrounding and beating the woman. Indiranagar Inspector Ajay Narayan Singh said, "This is a case of minor assault." See 5 pictures- Blood was also coming from her mouth, but no one tried to save her The video shows a rope tied around the woman's leg. Some people can be seen knocking her to the ground and beating her with sticks from behind. Blood can also be seen coming from the woman's mouth during the assault. A large number of people were present at the scene, but no one tried to save her. Inspector said: A person from the other side was also injured What is surprising is that despite such a major incident taking place in the area, the local police had no knowledge of it. The matter came to light after the video went viral. Indiranagar Inspector Ajay Narayan Singh said the case involved a minor assault. A person from the other side was also injured. Meanwhile, East ADCP Amol Murkut said, “The video is five days old. The woman is a resident of Jarhara village and is mentally challenged. The accused suspected that she had come to steal a child and beat her because of this. Two people have been detained.”

stories.title: Man kills married lover in Ghaziabad:She had come to meet him at his room; the two had connected on Facebook
stories.summary: A man killed his 28-year-old married girlfriend by repeatedly hitting her on the head with a brick in Ghaziabad. The woman had gone to his room with her sister on Monday night, where the two got into an argument. During the quarrel, the accused picked up a brick lying nearby and repeatedly struck her on the head. She collapsed on the floor, bleeding heavily. Hearing her screams, her sister, who was waiting outside the room, rushed in and found blood scattered across the floor. When the sister raised an alarm, local residents rushed to the spot. They caught the accused and his friend while they were trying to flee and handed them over to the police. The incident took place in Naipura Colony, under the jurisdiction of Loni Border police station. The deceased was identified as Pinky, 28, wife of Pramod and a resident of Bulandshahr. She had met the accused on Facebook around five months ago. They met on Facebook, then grew closer Pinky was a resident of Malkapur in Bulandshahr. The accused, Pintu (33), is a resident of Sheikhpur Garhwa village in Bulandshahr. The two met on Facebook five months ago. Initially, they chatted on Facebook. They then exchanged mobile numbers and began speaking on the phone. Their friendship gradually grew, and they started meeting. Pintu lived in a rented room in Naipura Colony. On Monday evening, Pinky went to meet him with her sister. Her sister stayed outside the room while Pinky went inside. The two had an argument over something in the room. Pintu allegedly killed Pinky after this. Accused was fleeing with a bag when people caught him Tenant Prateek Tyagi said, "Pintu had come to rent and live in the room with his friend Aryan Gupta alias Bunty (22) just five days earlier. After the crime, Pintu began fleeing the room with a bag. Pinky's sister, who was standing outside, became suspicious of his actions. When she entered the room, she found Pinky lying there covered in blood. She raised the alarm, prompting people from the surrounding area to gather. They caught Pintu and his friend Aryan and handed them over to the police." ACP Indrapuri Amardeep Maurya said, “We received information about a woman being murdered at the Indrapuri police outpost. The police reached the spot and conducted an investigation. Pintu and his friend are being questioned.”

stories.title: Pradhan shoots 2 men after losing ₹25,000 bet:One killed in Ghazipur; wife demands encounter
stories.summary: A village head allegedly shot two young men with a country-made pistol after losing Rs 25,000 in a gambling game in Uttar Pradesh's Ghazipur district. One of the victims died, while the other sustained serious injuries. The village head was gambling with four or five young men and had staked Rs 25,000. When he began losing, the men playing with him made a joking remark, which angered him. He then opened fire on two of them. The incident took place late on Monday (9 Nov) night in the Sadar Kotwali area, around 7 km from the district headquarters. The deceased has been identified as 28-year-old Ajay Pasi. The accused, 35-year-old village head Sanjay Bind, surrendered at around 11 am on Tuesday. Ajay's wife said, "The accused should be killed in the same way as my husband was killed. He should be killed in an encounter." See 3 Photos... Opened fire after losing Rs 25,000 gambling bet Many people gather to gamble in Maharajganj Mohanw village, under the jurisdiction of Kotwali police station, on the day after Diwali. At around 10.30 pm on Monday, eight to 10 people were gambling near a pond in Pasipurwa, close to the village. Sanjay Bind, the head of neighbouring Bakrabad village, arrived with two or three companions and joined the game. According to eyewitnesses, Rs 25,000 was at stake. As Sanjay was on the verge of losing the amount, the other players made jokes about him. This angered the village head and led to a minor altercation. He then pulled out a country-made pistol and opened fire on two young men. One victim shot in abdomen, another in right hand City Circle Officer Anil Kumar said Ajay Pasi, a resident of Mohanw village, was shot in the abdomen, while his companion, 35-year-old Surendra Ram, a resident of Islamabad, sustained a bullet injury to his right hand. Both were rushed to the district hospital. As their condition was serious, doctors referred them to Varanasi for further treatment. Ajay Pasi died during treatment, while Surendra Ram remains under medical care. Village head surrenders at police station holding placard The village head fled after the incident. Following a complaint lodged by Ajay's elder paternal uncle, Shriram, the police registered a case against him and formed teams to track him down. However, at around 11 am on Tuesday, Sanjay Bind surrendered at the police station. He arrived carrying a cardboard placard that read: "I, Sanjay Bind, am surrendering." Ajay was the only brother among three sisters The injured Surendra is a mason. Ajay worked as a labourer with him. Both their homes are 800 metres from the scene, while the village head's home is two kilometres away. Ajay was the only brother among three sisters. He is survived by his wife, Aparna Paswan (26), and their three-year-old daughter, Lado. Aparna said, "My husband left home saying he would return in five minutes. He had no dispute with anyone." Won the village head elections in 2015 and 2021 Sanjay Bind was elected village head of Bakrabad village for two consecutive terms. He won the panchayat elections held in 2015 and 2021. Villagers said he was friends with several people in Mohांव village. He often visited the village. City CO Anil Kumar said two cases had already been registered against the village head. His other activities are also being investigated.

stories.title: Gorakhpur Zoo prepares for winter:Tigers and lions to get a new diet; bears to be fed honey and jaggery
stories.summary: With temperatures beginning to drop in Gorakhpur, the Shaheed Ashfaqullah Khan Zoological Park has started preparations to protect its animals from the winter cold. Like humans, wild animals also need special care as the weather changes. Keeping this in mind, the zoo administration will make necessary changes to their enclosures, food and water arrangements. Additional measures will be taken when temperatures fall sharply and cold waves set in. Tarpaulin sheets, screens and green nets will be installed around enclosures to prevent cold winds from entering. Heaters and blowers will also be used wherever necessary during severe cold. Tarpaulin sheets and green nets to protect enclosures Chief Veterinary Officer Dr Yogesh Pratap Singh said the zoo makes seasonal changes to animal care arrangements, just as people change their clothing and use heaters and blowers during winter. The first priority during colder weather is to make the enclosures safe and comfortable. Tarpaulin sheets, screens and green nets will be installed to block cold winds. Heaters and blowers will be arranged in areas where temperatures fall significantly. These measures aim to protect the animals from cold winds and the effects of extremely low temperatures. Tigers and lions to receive changes in their diet The diets of animals will also be adjusted according to their seasonal requirements. The quantity of meat given to carnivores, particularly tigers and lions, will be modified as needed. Dr Singh said their feeding arrangements are managed according to the weather and individual requirements. Herbivorous animals will be given energy-rich food during winter. Their diets will be adjusted according to the needs of each species to ensure that the cold weather does not adversely affect their health. Bears to be fed honey, jaggery and gram Special attention will also be given to the diet of bears during winter. Honey, jaggery and gram will be included in their food. Some herbivorous animals will also be given sweet potatoes, sugarcane and oilseed cake, wherever required. The zoo administration will provide different food items according to the nature and nutritional requirements of each animal. Officials said all animals are not given the same diet, as their food is determined by their physical needs and prevailing weather conditions. Bonfires to be arranged safely during cold waves As temperatures drop further and cold waves intensify, additional arrangements will be made to keep the animals warm. Bonfires will also be arranged at safe locations wherever necessary. Enclosures exposed to cold winds will be covered with tarpaulin sheets and other protective materials. Heaters and blowers will also be used as required. Necessary seasonal changes will also be made to the upkeep of deer and other animals. Pond water to be refreshed for aquatic animals Special arrangements will also be made for aquatic animals living at the zoo. Particular attention will be paid to water management in the ponds housing hippopotamuses, crocodiles, gharials and turtles. Dr Singh said a drop in water temperature can cause discomfort to these animals. To manage the water conditions, fresh water is continuously added to the ponds from one side, while old water is drained from the other. This process ensures regular water replacement and helps maintain a suitable environment for aquatic animals. Care arrangements to vary according to each animal Dr Singh said the zoo focuses on two key aspects of animal care: food and enclosure management. Both are adjusted according to changing weather conditions and the requirements of individual species. Animals that need additional warmth will receive suitable arrangements in their enclosures, while energy-rich food will be added to the diets of those that require it. Aquatic animals will receive separate water-management arrangements. The zoo administration aims to ensure that all animals remain healthy and safe, without discomfort, as temperatures fall and cold waves affect the region.

stories.title: Siberian birds arrive in Varanasi from Russia:Migratory visitors attract tourists; Ganga ghats buzz with selfie and reel enthusiasts
stories.summary: Varanasi, the city of Baba Vishwanath, takes on a special charm during winter. Morning fog over the Ganga ghats, cold winds, cups of hot tea and thousands of white birds floating on the river create a picturesque scene. It almost looks as if Siberia has arrived at the ghats of Kashi. As every year, thousands of migratory birds have travelled thousands of kilometres to reach the banks of the Ganga. They began arriving in the first week of November and are expected to stay until February, attracting tourists and visitors who are keen to take selfies and make reels. Birds escape temperatures as low as -60°C These beautiful white birds, seen swimming in the Ganga and flying in large flocks across the sky, are commonly known as Siberian birds. Their white bodies, orange beaks and orange feet make them a major attraction for tourists. During winter, temperatures in Siberia can drop to between -50°C and -60°C. To escape the extreme cold, these birds fly thousands of kilometres to reach relatively warmer parts of India. Migratory birds reach Kashi via Pakistan According to Professor Chandana Haldar, the distance between India and Siberia is approximately 4,400 kilometres. The migratory birds follow different routes to reach India, travelling through several European countries as well as Afghanistan, Mongolia, China and Bhutan. Another group travels through Pakistan and Rajasthan before reaching Prayagraj and then Varanasi. During this long journey, the birds face several challenges, including changing weather conditions, food availability and natural obstacles. What does the scientist say? These migratory birds stay in Kashi for around four months. During their stay, they swim in the Ganga and also breed in the sandy areas across the river, where they lay their eggs. In March, as the winter chill begins to fade, they return to their natural habitats along with their young ones. According to Chandana Haldar, the natural environment of Kashi is suitable for their breeding, and the birds also find sufficient food here. However, their numbers are considerably lower this November compared with previous years. Climate change is believed to be one of the reasons why many migratory birds have not yet arrived in Kashi. Bread and savoury snacks offered by tourists can harm birds After reaching Kashi, the migratory birds face another challenge. Tourists visiting the ghats often feed them bread, savoury snacks and puffed rice out of affection. However, these food items can be harmful to the birds' health. Increasing pollution in the Ganga is also a threat to their survival. As a result, several birds die during their stay in Kashi, while others lose their lives during the return journey.

stories.summary: In view of the rising number of passengers travelling after Diwali for Chhath Puja, the Railways has announced two important measures. A special train festival will run from Gorakhpur to Hadapsar in Pune on November 10 and 17. In another move, the Gorakhpur-Yeshvantpur Express will make a trial halt at Pukhrayan station. The decisions are expected to benefit passengers travelling to Pune and southern India. The special train will make two trips in each direction. Train to depart from Gorakhpur at 9.55 pm According to the timetable released by the Railways, train number 05093, Gorakhpur-Hadapsar Festival Special, will depart from Gorakhpur at 9.55 pm on November 10 and 17. It will reach Basti at 11.12 pm, Mankapur at 12.04 am the following day and Gonda at 12.30 am. It will then halt at Lucknow at 2.45 am and Kanpur Central at 4.35 am. The train will depart from Orai at 6 am, Virangana Lakshmibai Jhansi at 8.15 am and Bina at 12.05 pm. It will reach Bhopal at 2.15 pm, Itarsi at 4.20 pm, Khandwa at 7.08 pm and Bhusaval at 9.05 pm. On the third day, it will travel via Manmad, Kopargaon, Belapur, Ahilyanagar and the Daund chord line before reaching Hadapsar at 7.30 am. Return train to leave Hadapsar at 10.05 am Train number 05094, Hadapsar-Gorakhpur Festival Special, will depart from Hadapsar at 10.05 am on November 12 and 19. It will reach the Daund chord line at 11.12 am, Ahilyanagar at 12.32 pm, Belapur at 2.30 pm and Kopargaon at 3.24 pm. The train will then depart from Manmad at 4.15 pm, Bhusaval at 7 pm and Khandwa at 9.50 pm. The following day, it will halt at Itarsi at 12.20 am, Bhopal at 2.25 am and Bina at 4.30 am. It will travel via Virangana Lakshmibai Jhansi, Orai, Kanpur Central, Lucknow, Gonda, Mankapur and Basti before reaching Gorakhpur at 7 pm. Special train to have 20 coaches According to the Railways, the special train will have 20 coaches, including: Yeshvantpur Express to stop at Pukhrayan The Railways has also decided to introduce a trial halt for the Gorakhpur-Yeshvantpur Express at Pukhrayan station under the North Central Railway. Train number 15023, Gorakhpur-Yeshvantpur Express, will arrive at Pukhrayan at 6.58 pm from November 10 and depart at 7 pm. Similarly, train number 15024, Yeshvantpur-Gorakhpur Express, will arrive at Pukhrayan at 9.47 am from November 12 and depart at 9.49 am. The additional halt is expected to make travel between Gorakhpur and southern India more convenient for passengers from Pukhrayan and nearby areas.

stories.title: Businessman kills wife in Shahjahanpur:Tries to strangle one daughter; second daughter locks herself in a room to save her life
stories.summary: A businessman allegedly strangled his wife to death in Uttar Pradesh's Shahjahanpur district. He also tried to strangle their 11-year-old daughter. Terrified by her father's actions, their 16-year-old daughter locked herself inside a room and saved her life. The incident took place at around 1 am on Monday night (9 Nov). The elder daughter called her uncle from inside the locked room, following which he alerted the police. The mother and the younger daughter were rushed to a medical college, where the mother died during treatment. The 11-year-old girl is in critical condition and has been admitted to the ICU. Accused arrested from house, police say he did not flee The accused, identified as Kamlesh, did not flee after the incident and was still at home when the police arrived. He was arrested at the scene. The incident took place in Adarsh Nagar Colony, under the jurisdiction of Roza police station, around 10 km from the district headquarters. See two pictures Now understand the full case Kamlesh is reportedly living with his wife Seema (40) and daughters Komal, also known as Ananya (16), and Anjali (11). Kamlesh lived on the upper floor, while his family members lived downstairs. He has an electronics shop nearby. Kamlesh is reportedly under stress over his business these days. He also has a debt of lakhs of rupees. The husband and wife quarrelled over this at around 12:30 a.m. Kamlesh then began assaulting his wife and children. He knocked his wife to the floor and then strangled her to death. During this, he also strangled and tried to kill his younger daughter Anjali, who had come to save her mother. He then tried to attack his elder daughter Komal as well. However, she fled and locked herself in a room, saving her life. People living downstairs arrived after hearing the elder daughter's screams. Father says he never saw his son and daughter-in-law quarrel Accused Kamlesh's father, Ramesh Chandra Gupta, said, "We live downstairs in the house, while my son Kamlesh lives on the terrace with his family. There was no dispute between my son and daughter-in-law. If there had been any problem, he would have told me. I do not know what happened between them that Kamlesh took such a step." Brother says sister did not mention the quarrel Deceased Seema's brother Ashok said he had spoken to his sister on the phone on Monday evening, but she had not mentioned anything resembling a dispute. He said it did not seem from their conversation that she was troubled. This morning, he received a call telling him to come to the hospital quickly. He then spoke to his elder niece, who told him that her father had killed her mother. SP City Devendra Singh said, “Preliminary investigation has revealed that the accused committed the crime while under the influence of alcohol. He strangled his wife to death and also tried to kill his daughter by strangling her. The accused has been arrested and is being questioned.”

stories.title: Model Shraddha offers prayers morning and evening in jail:Has started interacting with other inmates; no family member has visited her so far
stories.summary: Model Shraddha Dubey, an accused in the murder case of Lucknow chicken trader Shiva Sharma, is spending her time in jail through yoga and spiritual activities. Prayers and yoga sessions in the morning and evening have become part of her daily routine. During the rest of the day, she talks to her sister Rashmi and other women inmates in the barrack. The change in her behaviour has been observed since her judicial custody was extended. Her custody was extended by 14 days on October 31 and is due to end on November 13. So far, no family member or acquaintance has visited her in jail. She has met her lawyer only twice. After businessman Shiva died on October 9, Shraddha allegedly fled with her sister Rashmi and driver Danish. After remaining on the run for 12 days across Nepal, Rae Bareli, Lucknow and Agra, she was arrested in Nagpur on October 22. See 3 pictures... Shraddha stays with her sister in jail According to jail sources, Shraddha has settled into a regular routine. She spends her mornings and evenings doing yoga, praying and engaging in spiritual activities. During the day, she talks to other women inmates in the barrack. Her sister Rashmi stays with her. Acting Senior Superintendent of Jail Rithvik Priyadarshi said Shraddha, Rashmi and their driver Tanveer were being treated like other inmates. All three are following the jail's prescribed routine. Both sisters initially appeared restless in jail For the first 24 hours after entering jail, Shraddha and Rashmi did not speak to anyone. However, they repeatedly asked questions of the deputy jailer assigned to monitor them. The sisters were lodged in a barrack housing 40-45 women inmates. According to jail sources, both were distressed by the sudden loss of their luxurious lifestyle. They reportedly kept walking around the barrack. However, their behaviour gradually changed. After losing hope of getting out of jail soon, they began spending time with and talking to other inmates. Shraddha's Instagram followers increase, following decreases After Shraddha's name surfaced in the Shiva Sharma murder case, her Instagram account became a major talking point. She maintained a public profile and regularly shared updates. Her follower count has also attracted attention. Following the incident, her followers increased from 1.41 lakh to 1.44 lakh. At the same time, the number of accounts she follows decreased from 421 to 404. It is being claimed that some VIP profiles were either blocked from her account or unfollowed by Shraddha after the incident. However, this claim has not been independently established. What is the Shiva Sharma murder case? On October 9, Shiva Sharma died after falling from the fourth floor of Awadh Green Apartment in Lucknow's Hazratganj area. He had reportedly been living with Shraddha in a live-in relationship for the previous four months. At the time, Shiva's body was reportedly found wearing only underwear. Lipstick marks were found on his face, while several cigarette-burn marks were also noticed on his body. Shiva's mother, Ranjana Sharma, filed a murder case against five people, including Shraddha, her sister Rashmi and driver Adil, in connection with his death. She alleged that Shraddha pushed Shiva from the fourth floor. The three accused are currently lodged in Lucknow jail.

stories.title: Lawyers hold dance and poetry session inside Prayagraj police station:Stage sit-in with beds, chairs, tables and loudspeakers; demand accused person's arrest
stories.summary: Eight lawyers have been staging a sit-in protest at the Civil Lines police station in Prayagraj for the past four days, demanding the arrest of an agent accused of cheating a lawyer of ₹70,000 on the pretext of arranging vehicle finance. The lawyers have adopted an unusual style of protest. They dance to songs such as 'Naka Bandi' and 'Hum Pagal Nahi Hain Bhaiya, Hamara Dimaag Kharab Hai'. They have now started reciting ghazals and poetry over a microphone. Before reciting a verse, they announce, "Station House Officer, this one is for you." The lawyers have set up camp outside the police station, spreading mats, mattresses, bedsheets and mosquito nets. They have also arranged chairs, tables, a microphone and loudspeakers. They continued their protest at the police station even during Diwali and the following day, known as Parewa, without returning home. See 3 pictures... How did the dispute begin? Lawyer Brijesh Tiwari was allegedly cheated on the pretext of arranging vehicle finance. According to the complaint, an agent took ₹70,000 from him but fled without depositing the money with the finance company. An FIR was registered at the Civil Lines police station in connection with the incident. The lawyers allege that the police took no action against the accused despite registering the case. Angered by the alleged inaction, Brijesh Tiwari arrived at the police station with fellow lawyers on November 7, carrying mats and bedding, and began a sit-in protest. They later arranged chairs, tables, a microphone and loudspeakers. Lawyers refuse to end protest until agent is arrested The police have repeatedly tried to persuade the lawyers to call off their protest, but they have refused to budge. They say the sit-in will continue until the agent is arrested.

stories.title: Thar runs over 4 friends, including 2 teachers:3 killed; they were riding one bike in Kannauj, bodies scattered across road
stories.summary: A speeding Thar ran over four friends in Kannauj late on Monday night, killing three on the spot. One is in critical condition. All four were travelling on the same motorcycle. The man riding the bike was not wearing a helmet. Eyewitnesses said the Thar was travelling at an estimated speed of 100–120 kmph. It hit the motorcycle head-on with such force that all four men were thrown 15–20 metres away. Their bodies were scattered across the road, and the motorcycle was completely wrecked. Even after the collision, the Thar driver did not stop. Instead, he sped away from the spot. Police reached the scene after receiving information and sent the bodies for post-mortem in plastic bags. The injured man has been referred to Kanpur. The accident took place in the Indergarh police station area, 35 km from the district headquarters. The deceased have been identified as Manish Savita (28), Vedram Pal (40) and Vijay Kushwaha (35). Ashish (25) is in critical condition. Vijay, also known as Ramji, was an instructor at a primary school, while Ved Prakash was a private schoolteacher. Thar driver hit the bike from the wrong side According to information, Vijay, also known as Ramji, a resident of Agaus village, was constructing a new house near Patel Nagar Tiraha in Indergarh. On Monday night, he was taking his three friends, Manish, Vedram and Ashish, to his new house. Villagers said the four were close friends. They were often seen together and usually travelled on the same motorcycle. At around 11:20 pm on Monday, they left their homes for Patel Nagar Tiraha in Indergarh town. They said that as soon as their motorcycle reached near Sardar Patel Inter College in Kachhatipur village, a speeding car coming from the wrong side hit them. The driver fled with the car after the accident. Police search for the Thar using CCTV footage Passers-by spotted the four men lying on the road and informed the police. They also called local residents for help, who moved the four men to the roadside. Meanwhile, the police arrived with an ambulance and took all four to the medical college. Doctors declared three of them dead. As the condition of the fourth man was critical, he was referred to a higher medical centre in Kanpur. His condition is said to be serious. CCTV footage of the incident emerges; police intensify search Police have also obtained CCTV footage of the incident. It shows a speeding car running over the four friends. When police examined footage from cameras near the accident site, they found that the car stopped outside Makrandapur village, about one kilometre ahead. A man got out of the car and walked towards Indergarh. Police are now trying to identify the Thar and the people travelling in it. Family blocks road with Vijay's body Vijay was the first among the three deceased to undergo a post-mortem. As soon as his body reached the village, his family members came out onto the road at around 3:45 pm. They alleged that even 18 hours after the accident, the police had failed to catch the Thar driver. They said they would not perform the last rites until the vehicle and its driver were caught. During the protest, the family members also got into an argument with Indergarh police station in-charge Vinod Kumar Kashyap. Know about the three men who lost their lives 1. Vedram: He was a farmer and owned 15 bighas of ancestral farmland. His family includes three sons, Praveendra, Pushpendra and Ashish, and a daughter, Priyanka. Ashish is in the final year of his BSc course, while Pushpendra works outside the village. Praveendra helps his father with farming. Priyanka is married. 2. Manish: His family includes his father, Shashikant, mother, brother Ashish and two sisters, Pooja and Anju. He worked in a private company in Pune. Two months ago, he returned home after his father's health deteriorated so he could arrange his treatment. Both his sisters are married. There was a wedding in the family, and he was busy with its preparations. 3. Vijay: He worked as an instructor at Junior High School in Agaus. His family includes his father, Subhash Chandra, wife Neelam and three-year-old son Raunak. His death has left the family devastated.

stories.title: Fog covers 15 UP cities, air quality worsens in Noida-Ghaziabad:AQI crosses 300; dense fog tomorrow, colder weather in 2 days
stories.summary: Fog and haze have increased across Uttar Pradesh after Diwali. Dense fog covered 15 cities, including Sambhal, Hapur, Bijnor and Shamli, on Tuesday morning. Visibility dropped to just 10-20 metres in some areas, making it difficult to see even a short distance ahead. Air pollution has also increased due to Diwali firecrackers. On Monday evening, Noida recorded an AQI of 332, followed by Bulandshahr at 331, Ghaziabad at 324 and Baghpat at 305. Meanwhile, temperatures in the state have dropped below 15°C. Hardoi recorded a minimum temperature of 14.5°C, while Kanpur recorded 14.6°C, making them the coldest places in the state. The Meteorological Department has issued an alert for dense fog across Uttar Pradesh on Wednesday. Severe cold is likely to increase in the state after two days. Prof. Manoj Srivastava, a weather scientist at BHU in Varanasi, said, "As dry north-westerly winds become stronger, minimum temperatures will fall further. This will make the cold more intense." It is a score that indicates the quality of the air and helps us understand whether the air around us is clean or polluted. The AQI measures the level of pollutants present in the air. As the AQI rises, the air is considered increasingly dangerous and the health risk also increases. Understand it from the graphic below: How does poor AQI affect our health? When the AQI is poor, pollutants such as PM2.5, PM10, nitrogen dioxide, sulphur dioxide and ozone present in the air reach deep into our lungs. These particles spread throughout the body through the bloodstream. They can cause various health problems, ranging from immediate issues to long-term conditions. stories.title: Former SP leader opens fire:Celebrates family's acquittal in Gonda; claims it was a gun used to scare away monkeys
stories.summary: Former Samajwadi Party leader Abhishek Tiwari and his family members opened fire during Diwali celebrations in Gonda. He recorded a video of the firing and posted it on his Facebook account. The video surfaced at around 3:30 pm on Monday. It shows eight people, including Tiwari, taking turns to fire a gun. Around 15 days ago, Tiwari's family members were acquitted in an old case. The firing was reportedly carried out to celebrate their acquittal. The incident took place in the Nawabganj police station area, around 40 km from the district headquarters. Check out visuals below : Read the full story below : Abhishek Tiwari (28), who lives in Lauwwa Veerpur village, is active in student politics. His parents are also part of his family. Abhishek joined the Samajwadi Party on 9 November 2024. He was later appointed district general secretary of the Samajwadi Party's Lohia Vahini. However, he was removed from the post on 25 February 2025 for making objectionable remarks against SP chief Akhilesh Yadav and engaging in anti-party activities. He was also expelled from the party. Eight people, including a girl, opened rapid fire In the viral video, six young men are seen firing guns one after another. The seventh person, a middle-aged man, and the eighth, a girl aged around 19, are also seen firing guns. He shared the video with a post on Facebook Abhishek Tiwari shared the video on Facebook and wrote, "After a long 25-year struggle and wait, justice has finally prevailed. This is the first Diwali after my family members were honourably acquitted, when all the members of the family are together." This time, lamps are being lit not only in homes but also in the hearts of those who faced darkness and suffering for many years. It is a celebration of the victory of justice, patience and the family. However, after the video went viral, Abhishek Tiwari removed the post from Facebook. Dainik Bhaskar does not verify this viral video. Former Samajwadi Party leader Abhishek Tiwari said that he has a crow gun, which is used to drive away monkeys. There are a large number of monkeys in his area. For this reason, members of the family had fired the gun. He claimed that it was not a real gun. Former Samajwadi Party leader says-fired crow gun to drive away monkeys Former Samajwadi Party leader Abhishek Tiwari said, "I have a crow gun. It is used to drive away monkeys." "There are a large number of monkeys in my area. For this reason, members of the family had fired the gun. It is not a real gun." Nawabganj Station House Officer Mrityunjay Singh said: “The matter is being investigated seriously. Strict legal action will be taken against the accused based on the findings of the investigation.”

stories.title: 'Ayodhya will become the global capital of Sanatan tourism':Akhilesh says temple theft row has reduced devotees affected business
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party national president Akhilesh Yadav has targeted the BJP government over the situation in Ayodhya. He claimed that the number of devotees visiting the city was falling after the controversy over the alleged theft at the Ram temple. He said this was also affecting local businesses. Akhilesh said that if the Samajwadi Party forms the government, it will restore Ayodhya's honour and bring transparency to temple management. He promised to develop world-class facilities and make Ayodhya the "global capital of Sanatan pilgrimage". Akhilesh shared his vision for Ayodhya in a detailed social media post. He raised issues related to temple management, tourism, local businesses, employment for boatmen, ration supplies for the poor and alleged land scams. He said the city's religious identity and the interests of local people would be given priority. Ram temple management to be made transparent Akhilesh said the controversy over the alleged theft at the Ram temple had hurt the feelings of devotees. He claimed that the fall in the number of pilgrims was affecting the local economy. He said an open and transparent system would be introduced for temple management to restore people's trust. He also promised world-class facilities for pilgrims visiting Ayodhya from across the country and abroad. He said the city would be developed as a major centre for religious tourism. Boatmen to get employment, Nishadraj's bond with Lord Ram to be highlighted Akhilesh promised to promote traditional boating in Ayodhya to provide employment to local boatmen. He said this would also help bring back the close bond between Lord Ram and Nishadraj. He accused the BJP of weakening this historic relationship. Akhilesh said the BJP's politics of dominance did not want people to remember the story of Lord Ram embracing members of the PDA community. Ayodhya to be freed from outside contractors The SP president also raised questions about the role of outsiders in land deals and construction work in Ayodhya. He said the land would be investigated and the city would be freed from outside contractors. Referring to an alleged scam involving circle rates, Akhilesh said BJP leaders and officials involved in corruption would not be spared. He alleged that outsiders had taken advantage of Ayodhya while ignoring the interests of local people. Oil and ghee to be included in ration for poor families Akhilesh also promised to include oil and ghee in ration supplies if the SP forms the government. He said this would help meet the nutritional needs of poor families. He spoke of building an Ayodhya where no poor woman or child would face humiliation or harassment. He also referred to an alleged incident in which a poor woman and her children were mistreated while collecting oil. AI video explains PDA government's ration plan Akhilesh also shared an AI-generated video along with his post. In the video, a child is shown collecting oil from lamps. When a woman asks him why he is doing so, the child says that his father is no longer alive and he is collecting oil for the family's ration. The woman tells him not to worry, saying that the PDA government will provide mustard oil free of cost along with ration supplies when it comes to power. She also says that his mother will receive ₹40,000 every year. Through the video, Akhilesh highlighted his proposed welfare plans for poor families, women and children. Action promised against those who hurt religious feelings Akhilesh also spoke about religious harmony and disputes related to places of worship. He said strict action would be taken against anyone who insults Lord Ram, Lord Krishna or respected figures of any other religion. He added that those who protect people involved in such acts would also face action if they were found to be part of a plan to disturb social harmony. Akhilesh targets BJP over Ayodhya issues Through his post, Akhilesh brought together issues related to religious faith, local business, employment, corruption and social justice. He tried to link the Ram temple theft controversy with the alleged fall in the number of devotees and its impact on local businesses. He presented Ayodhya not just as a religious tourism destination but also as a political issue focused on local jobs, transparent temple management, welfare of poor families and respect for local people.
