stories.title: 'Dhirendra Shastri should not be invited to Kunda':Pratapgarh MP says they will oppose the event despite having faith
stories.summary: Political tensions have intensified in Kunda, Pratapgarh, over a religious discourse by Dhirendra Krishna Shastri, head of Bageshwar Dham, which is scheduled to be held there. After Samajwadi Party national president Akhilesh Yadav opposed it, the party's leaders and workers have also launched a campaign against the event. Pratapgarh SP MP Prof. SP Singh said, "Such a controversial person should not be invited to deliver a religious discourse at all. Dhirendra Shastri conducts business in the name of religion and hurts the faith of Hindus through his statements." The MP made it clear that the Samajwadi Party would oppose the event, but that the opposition would be conducted entirely through democratic means. The workers would not disrupt law and order. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to MP Prof. SP Singh about the entire controversy and the SP's position. Read the key excerpts... Question: The Samajwadi Party has suddenly come out against the religious discourse by the head of Bageshwar Dham in Kunda. What is the party's stand? Answer: The Samajwadi Party will openly oppose it. If you claim to be well-wishers of Hindus and call yourselves protectors of Hinduism, why then do you make statements that hurt Hinduism and the sentiments of its followers? The head of Bageshwar Dham is known for his controversial statements. Sometimes he claims to speak to Lord Hanuman over the telephone. At other times, he makes statements that hurt religious sentiments. He had said that those who died in the stampede during the Kumbh had attained salvation. Such statements insult Hinduism. Question: Which of his conduct or statements do you object to the most? Answer: Hypocrisy and commercialisation are being carried out in the name of religion. People are being fooled by drawing slips, and this has been turned into a means of making money. At times, claims are made of speaking directly to God. Such people are known by their actions and conduct. Questions have repeatedly been raised about the activities of people such as Radhe Maa and the presiding head of Bageshwar Dham. Religion is a matter of faith and should not be turned into a business. Question: What would you say about the BJP's stand on this matter? Answer: The BJP should take action against such people. If someone else made such a statement, BJP members would create a huge uproar. But when such events are held among their own supporters, no action is taken. BJP members oppose Muslims, but it seems they are also opposed to Hinduism. These people are merely peddling hypocrisy. Question: Your national president, Akhilesh Yadav, has also made statements about Lord Krishna and Lord Ram. How do you view his statements? Answer: Our national president has made an absolutely correct statement. There are different beliefs regarding the form of Lord Krishna. We also have faith in Lord Ram. However, BJP leaders make statements suggesting that discrimination is being made between God and the gods and goddesses. It is beyond comprehension why the BJP does this. Our national president has raised the issue of the insult to Sanatan Dharma. Question: A religious discourse is going to be held in your district. Is the Samajwadi Party preparing to oppose it at the grassroots level? Will you also ask the main organiser, Raja Bhaiya, to cancel it? Answer: The Samajwadi Party will oppose it. The national president has also made his position clear. We are against such events and against inviting such controversial individuals. The sentiments of those who have faith in religion are hurt by such statements. Such a person should not be invited to deliver a religious discourse at all. My point is that Raja Bhaiya should not have invited such a controversial person. He should reconsider this event. Although Kunda does not fall in my Lok Sabha constituency, Pratapgarh district is ours. That is why I am opposing this event. Question: Is there a possibility of workers turning aggressive during the protest or the law and order situation deteriorating? Answer: No, we will not disrupt law and order. The protest will be held democratically. The workers will maintain law and order. We are Hindus too. We also feel hurt when someone insults our gods and goddesses. Protest does not mean violence or any kind of anarchy. The Chief Minister once also described Lord Hanuman as a Shudra. When senior party leaders themselves start making such statements, it amounts to playing with people's faith. This should not happen. Question: The event has already been proposed. Does opposing it serve any purpose now? Answer: The fact that the event was proposed earlier does not mean questions cannot be raised about it. We will continue our opposition. The decision to invite such a controversial person to deliver the religious discourse is not right.

stories.title: Lucknow's sky comes alive on Jamghat:Modi-Yogi picture kites in demand; people boycott Chinese manjha
stories.summary: On the second day of Diwali, people flew kites enthusiastically during Jamghat in Lucknow. The kites were special this year. Some featured pictures of Modi and Yogi, while others carried slogans. One kite read, "Fly kites, not your life." Kite traders completely boycotted Chinese manjha this year. Some kites also carried slogans related to the issue, such as, "Say No to Chinese manjha, use only cotton string." The biggest Jamghat for kite-flying was held in Chowk. Kite-flyer Wसी Haider said, "We wait throughout the year for this day. Hindus, Muslims and people of all faiths fly kites together. In Lucknow, kite-flying conveys the message of Ganga-Jamuni culture." A tradition that began in 1775 Kite flying in Lucknow is not a recent practice but a 250-year-old tradition. It flourished in Lucknow during the reign of Nawab Asif-ud-Daula in 1775. Kites were used not only for entertainment but also to protest against the British. Lovers would write messages on kites and send them to their beloveds' rooftops. Kites made in Lucknow now reach foreign countries. Kites priced from ₹5 to ₹500 There are more than a dozen varieties of kites, priced from ₹5 to ₹500. Rockets, Manjoli, Addhi, Pauna, Chand-Tara, Baaz, Kalidaar and plastic kites are in high demand. Traders and kite flyers are both opposing Chinese manjha. Lucknow kites reach Saudi Arabia Mohammad Salman, who runs a kite business in the Hussain Ganj area, said the shop is 35 years old. He learnt to make and fly kites from his grandfather. Whenever a kite-flying competition is held anywhere in Uttar Pradesh, the Tourism Department sends him to participate in it. Kites have now undergone this change. They have become smaller in size, as has the thread used to fly them. Kites made in Lucknow are considered the finest in India. Kites made by Salman reach Saudi Arabia and Dubai. He said that accidents were taking place regularly because of Chinese manjha. All traders are also opposed to Chinese manjha, so this time they are conveying the message "No Chinese manjha" from their shop, and kites are being flown on the same theme. He said that because of this Chinese manjha, Lucknow's 250-year-old kite-flying culture and passion are also being defamed. 'A kite is like a second wife' Meraj Ahmad Faridi, 52, says he is a kite lover. He has been flying kites continuously for the past 30 years. He says he cannot sleep on the night of Jamghat and simply waits for morning. It is a festival celebrated by people of every faith in Lucknow. As a child, his father would be very angry with them for flying kites. His father beat him, but he never lost his passion for kite flying Once, they beat him so badly over a kite that his head split open, but he still did not give up his passion for kite flying. He says a kite is like a second wife. Miraj said kite flying is not just a hobby but also exercise. He is completely fit at the age of 52, and he credits kite flying for this. He said flying a kite gives the hands plenty of exercise. It also exercises the eyes and the body.

stories.title: Shivpal meets Azam Khan in jail after Akhilesh:Says he will share details after meeting; over 400 SP workers gather outside
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party national general secretary Shivpal Yadav reached Ghaziabad on Wednesday. He arrived at Dasna Jail around 10:30 am to meet party leader Azam Khan, who is lodged there. More than 400 Samajwadi Party workers gathered outside the jail. Party leaders welcomed Shivpal and raised slogans of "Shivpal Yadav zindabad" and "Azam Khan zindabad". Shivpal asked the workers to remain calm and spoke to the media. He said, "I will meet him now and ask about his well-being. After that, I will come out and speak to the media." After speaking to reporters, Shivpal went inside the jail. Shivpal completed formalities before meeting Azam Shivpal first met jail officials and completed the required formalities. He was then allowed to meet Azam Khan. The two leaders are currently talking inside the jail. According to sources, they may also discuss the Assembly elections. ED arrested Azam Khan in money-laundering case The Enforcement Directorate (ED) arrested Azam Khan on October 31 in a money-laundering case. He was arrested at the gate after coming out of Rampur Jail. On November 1, a special PMLA court sent him to 14 days of judicial custody. He has been lodged in Dasna Jail for the past 12 days. Earlier, SP national president Akhilesh Yadav met Azam Khan in jail on October 22. His wife, Tazeen Fatima, also met him on November 6. Wife Tanjeen Fatima reached Dasna Jail to meet him on 6 November On 6 November, Tanjeen Fatima reached Dasna Jail with her elder son, Adeeb Azam, and her adopted daughter, Ekta Kaushik. She met her husband, Azam Khan. After this, Tanjeen said, "Azam Khan, who has served as an MLA 10 times and as a Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha MP, is being kept amid filth in jail. He is being kept as if he might escape. A killer roams freely, but this is how Azam sahib is being treated." She said, "The court has been informed that Azam is not keeping well. He has suffered a stroke. All his medical reports have also been submitted to the court, yet he is being kept in such conditions in jail." What case has the ED arrested Azam in? Read what happened after Azam was released from jail On 29 October, the High Court suspended the 10-year sentences handed to Azam and his son Abdullah in the two PAN card cases and granted bail to both of them. They were released from Rampur jail at around 7:15 p.m. on the evening of 31 October, after 11 months. Fifteen minutes before he came out, a team from the ED entered the jail. A heated argument broke out at the jail's main gate between the officers, who arrived in a white car, and Azam's lawyers. During this, Azam also answered the officers' questions, but the matter was not resolved. The officers then took him away in their car. During this, Azam raised his hand towards the sky and said, "Allah is watching everything. What is there to say now? This is the punishment for being Muslim. The mistake is that a Muslim built a university. This is our sin." Outside Ghaziabad court, Azam had said: "What is left to say?" On 1 November, ED officers produced Azam before the special PMLA court in Ghaziabad. A total of 100 CRPF and police personnel were also deployed during the proceedings. Azam appeared quite calm when he arrived at the court premises. He only kept looking towards the people. As soon as he rolled down the car window, the media asked, "Won't you say anything?" He replied, "What is left to say?" The Supreme Court had refused to hear the bail plea The Supreme Court refused to hear Azam Khan's bail plea on 5 November. It also transferred his petition to the Allahabad High Court. The court told the Chief Justice of the High Court to list the case for hearing before a division bench before 16 November. The bench must pass an interim order on Azam's petition on 16 November itself. Azam had said: "They want to keep me in jail during the election" Azam told the court, "I will face every case, but I need bail. I am 80 years old. I was arrested in 28 other cases besides the ED case. At this rate, I will die in jail. They want to keep me in jail until the election." Azam did not appear before the Supreme Court himself. He made these submissions through his lawyer, Kapil Sibal.

stories.title: "I don't look beautiful, I should die":Gorakhpur Class 12 pass-out attempts suicide 3 times, parents worried
stories.summary: “I am 19 years old. Everyone says I am beautiful, but I find my face ugly when I look in the mirror. I have attempted suicide three times. Each time, I survived by luck.” A 19-year-old NEET aspirant from Basti told a psychologist in Gorakhpur this during a counselling session. Her parents remain deeply distressed by her repeated suicide attempts and are unable to sleep peacefully at night. One family member or another stays with her at all times. Family turns to psychologist after several treatments fail Her family had taken her to several doctors, but her condition did not improve. They eventually approached a psychologist. During counselling, it emerged that the student was suffering from body dysmorphic disorder. NEET preparation after scoring well in Class 12 Nitika (name changed), a resident of Basti, studied at a school in Gorakhpur until Class 12. After securing good marks in the Intermediate examination, she began preparing for NEET. Her mother is a teacher, while her father works as an administrative officer in a district of the state. ‘I have been struggling with my reflection for two years’ The student told the psychologist, "People wonder what is wrong with me. I do well in my studies, have friends at college and receive a lot of love from my family. But the truth is that I have been struggling with my reflection in the mirror every day for the past two years. "As soon as I wake up, the first thing I do is look in the mirror. I feel that my nose is crooked, my face looks terrible and my stomach sticks out. I also feel that my hair looks bad. I can spend an hour standing in front of the mirror, constantly trying to fix my appearance." She avoids showing her face in group photographs She said, "Sometimes I apply make-up, sometimes I use filters and at other times I keep adjusting my hair. When I go to college, I feel that everyone is looking at me and laughing at the flaws in my face. I sit at the back of the classroom so that no one can see me. "I am afraid of having my photograph taken. I even hide my face in group photographs. All this has made me feel that I no longer want to live." ‘She has even cut a vein in her hand’ Dr Aakriti Pandey said the student had been troubling her family for the past two years. She had attempted suicide three times. On one occasion, she had even cut a vein in her hand. She was treated at several places in Kanpur and Gorakhpur, but there was no significant improvement. In April 2026, her parents brought her to me. Counselling revealed that she was suffering from body dysmorphic disorder. She needed regular counselling. With the help of cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT), her condition improved significantly over seven months. Now, learn about two more such cases... 1. Attempted suicide because of facial pimples Rahul (name changed), an 18-year-old living in Gorakhpur's Gulriha area, has topped his school in Class 12. His father works in government service, while his mother is a housewife. Rahul has severe pimples on his face. Because of this, he hides his face from people. He once tried to commit suicide by jumping from the roof. His parents then consulted doctors and took him to a psychologist. Tests and counselling revealed that he was suffering from body dysmorphic disorder. He underwent treatment for around 12 months. His behaviour has improved considerably with psychotherapy. He is currently undergoing Ayurvedic treatment for the pimples. 2. "I look like a girl; I should die" Rohit, 19, who lives in Gorakhpur city, has attempted suicide twice. He feels that his body looks like a girl's. His father is a railway employee, while his mother is a homemaker. Rohit has suffered from obesity since childhood. He has a considerable amount of fat around his stomach and chest. Other students at school used to tease him because of this. At home, too, he spends the entire day looking at himself in the mirror. He also goes to the gym. He was recently admitted to a BTech course at a college in Kanpur. He attempted suicide there as well. Since then, his parents have been keeping him with them. He has been receiving psychotherapy for the past year, which has improved his behaviour. Now learn about the main symptoms of body dysmorphic disorder... What could be the causes? stories.title: Mother kills son, dies by suicide:Six-month-old girl was strangled in Siddharthnagar left after being believed dead
stories.summary: A woman allegedly strangled her one-and-a-half-year-old son to death in Siddharthnagar, Uttar Pradesh, before attempting to kill her six-month-old daughter in the same way. When the baby lost consciousness, the woman reportedly assumed she was dead and left her behind. She then died by suicide by hanging herself. The boy died, while the baby girl was found unconscious and was subsequently attended to. The woman was identified as Kajal (25), a native of Mehra village in Madhya Pradesh's Bhind district. She lived with her husband, Ramnaresh (27), their son Tiger and six-month-old daughter Khushi in a rented house in Ward No. 11 of Raghunath Nagar, under the Shohratgarh police station area in Siddharthnagar. Ramnaresh, originally from Talgaon village in Madhya Pradesh's Datia district, has been living in Siddharthnagar for the past five years. He supports the family by selling phulki, a local snack. Mother allegedly strangled son before attacking daughter According to the police, Kajal first strangled her one-and-a-half-year-old son, Tiger. She then allegedly strangled her six-month-old daughter, Khushi. The baby lost consciousness, following which Kajal reportedly assumed she had died. The woman then hanged herself. Police begin investigation into deaths After receiving information about the incident, police reached the spot and took the bodies of the woman and her son into custody for further proceedings. The six-month-old girl was found unconscious. Police are also gathering information about her condition. The reason behind the incident remains unclear. Police are questioning family members and local residents as part of the investigation. Post-mortem report to establish cause of deaths Circle Officer Mayank Dwivedi said police were investigating both deaths. The exact circumstances would become clear after the post-mortem reports are received. Police are examining all possible aspects to establish the reason behind the incident.

stories.title: Bride weeps all night as groom skips wedding:Groom refuses to marry over ₹2 lakh dowry; she keeps gazing at her Henna
stories.summary: A bride in Sambhal spent the night crying in her wedding attire after the groom refused to arrive with his wedding procession over a dowry demand on Wednesday. She kept looking at the mehendi on her hands and feet as she waited for the wedding that never took place. The bride's family had agreed to give the groom ₹5 lakh as dowry but had paid only ₹3 lakh. Four hours before the wedding, the groom called and refused to bring the wedding procession, demanding the remaining ₹2 lakh. He also returned the ₹3 lakh already received. The bride's family tried to persuade the groom's relatives over the phone for six hours, but their efforts failed. They subsequently filed a police complaint against the groom and his father. The incident took place in a village under the jurisdiction of a police station around 11 km from the district headquarters. See 2 pictures- Groom works in the scrap business; bride's father died three years ago The bride, Shania, is from Mohammadpur Tanda village. Her father, Babu Rihan, died three years ago. The groom, Aqib, is from Fitkari village in Meerut and works in the scrap business in Delhi. Shania's brother, Shuaib, also works as a labourer at a scrap warehouse in Delhi. The two families had met at a funeral in Mohammadpur Tanda village some time ago. During the meeting, the groom's family noticed Shania, and discussions about the marriage began. Food arranged for 1,000 guests; 400-500 had already eaten Shan Mohammad, the bride's uncle, said the wedding was scheduled for the night of November 11. The family had made arrangements for food for around 1,000 guests. Around 400-500 guests had already eaten, but the wedding procession never arrived. Groom's father demanded ₹2 lakh over the phone The bride's uncle said the groom's father, Salim, called at around 4 pm and informed the family that the wedding procession would not arrive. The family continued requesting him to reconsider until 10 pm, but he remained firm on his decision. He insisted that the procession would arrive only if the remaining ₹2 lakh in dowry was paid. The bride's family said it could not afford the additional amount and refused to pay. As a result, the wedding was called off and the food prepared for the guests went to waste. Bride says groom had refused three days before wedding too Shania Malik, also known as Sannu, said she had been in regular contact with the groom, who had initially agreed to marry her. She alleged that he had also refused to bring the wedding procession three days before the nikah. However, discussions between the two families followed, and the matter was resolved, with the groom agreeing to proceed with the marriage. On the day of the nikah, however, he again demanded the remaining ₹2 lakh and refused to arrive with the wedding procession.

stories.title: Premanand Maharaj rides Bullet:Visits Yamuna bank for spiritual practice; meets devotees after 34 days
stories.summary: Vrindavan religious leader Premanand Maharaj was seen riding a Bullet motorcycle on Wednesday, on the occasion of Bhai Dooj. He travelled to the banks of the Yamuna, where he meditated at a secluded spot. The location was inaccessible by car. As soon as devotees spotted the saint, they ran towards him, chanting 'Radhe-Radhe' and greeting him with folded hands. Premanand Maharaj raised both hands to bless them. After completing his meditation, he returned to the Yamuna Bihar Kunj Ashram. Devotees got to see him after 34 days. The Bullet motorcycle was being ridden by his disciple and former wrestler Rinku Singh. Other disciples accompanied them. See 3 pictures- Premanand Maharaj has been living in seclusion for months Saint Premanand Maharaj has been living in seclusion for the past few months. He is currently staying at the Yamuna Bihar Kunj Ashram, located near Belvan, across the Yamuna in Vrindavan. The ashram is spread over approximately 9.5 bighas. Most of the premises are covered with greenery, while construction occupies around 25% of the area. Premanand Maharaj also undergoes dialysis at the ashram. He was last seen on October 8 Premanand Maharaj was last seen on October 8, when he visited the Keli Kunj Ashram at 5 am. He stayed there for around 10 minutes before walking to meet his guru, Shri Hit Govind Sharan Maharaj, whose residence is around 150 metres away. After meeting his guru, he returned to his new Yamuna Bihar Kunj Ashram. Disciple died by jumping from the Keli Kunj Trust building On September 25, Premanand Maharaj's disciple Rasik Dulari Sharan died by jumping from the fourth floor of the Keli Kunj Trust building. His last rites were performed on the banks of the Yamuna on September 26. During the incident, his mother alleged that her son was not allowed to meet her. Rasik Dulari Sharan was originally from Jabalpur in Madhya Pradesh. He moved to Vrindavan two years ago and took initiation from Premanand Maharaj. Following this, he changed his name from Deepak Lodhi to Rasik Dulari Sharan.

stories.title: Kashi's air turns toxic as AQI reaches 315:Construction dust adds to pollution, DM warns agencies of action
stories.summary: Although the weather in Varanasi remains dry, the city's air is steadily deteriorating. Kashi's Air Quality Index (AQI) was recorded at 315 on Thursday morning, placing it in the very poor category. Rising pollution poses a risk to people's health. People, particularly those suffering from asthma and respiratory illnesses, need to remain alert. The city's temperature was recorded at 22 degrees Celsius on Thursday morning. Wind speed was 5 kilometres per hour and humidity stood at 70 per cent. According to BHU meteorologist Prof. Manoj Srivastava, the weather is likely to remain dry for the next one week. Therefore, there is currently little hope that rain will reduce pollution. Dust from construction work is also increasing pollution, along with firecrackers Firecrackers are not the only reason for the rise in air pollution in the city. Ongoing construction work and unplanned excavation at various locations are also polluting the air. Dust blowing from construction sites is adding to people's problems. District Magistrate Satyendra Kumar has fixed the accountability of the executing organisations and construction agencies in this regard. He has strictly instructed all agencies to comply with pollution-control standards during construction work. Fine to be imposed for negligence, DM warns The DM has made it clear that adequate arrangements must be made to control dust at all construction sites. Compliance with the prescribed standards will be mandatory during construction work. If negligence by any agency comes to light, strict action, including a fine, will be taken against it. Fine dust particles pose a risk of reaching the lungs According to environmentalists, dust generated by construction and excavation contains extremely fine particles of silica and various geochemical minerals. These particles can mix with the air and reach the lungs through breathing. This can cause problems such as asthma, breathing difficulties, and irritation in the eyes and throat. Therefore, children, the elderly and people with respiratory illnesses need to take special precautions.

stories.title: Dense fog engulfs 15 UP cities, disrupts flights:5 flights delayed and one cancelled as visibility drops to 50 metres; Noida schools switch to hybrid mode
stories.summary: Winter is gradually setting in across Uttar Pradesh. Dense fog covered 15 cities, including Lucknow, Unnao, Deoria, Shamli, Kushinagar and Ballia, on Thursday morning. Visibility in rural areas dropped to just 50 metres, making it difficult to see beyond that distance. Fog disrupted flight operations at Noida Airport, delaying five flights by 30 to 50 minutes. Another flight from Jaipur to Noida was cancelled. Air quality also remained poor in Noida and Ghaziabad, with the Air Quality Index (AQI) crossing 300. Residents have been advised to wear masks and take special care of children and elderly people. Due to pollution, schools up to Class 5 in Noida and Greater Noida will switch to hybrid mode from Thursday. Students will have the option of attending classes either physically or online. Lakhimpur Kheri recorded the lowest temperature in the state at 19.2°C over the past 24 hours. Daytime temperatures have also dropped below 32°C. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), temperatures could fall by 5-6°C over the next week, bringing further relief from the heat but increasing the chill. Lucknow-based meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said, Fog will persist during the morning for the next five days, while light haze is expected during the day. There is no possibility of rain over the next seven days. What is the Air Quality Index (AQI)? The Air Quality Index (AQI) is a measure of air quality that indicates how clean or polluted the surrounding air is. It measures the levels of various pollutants in the air. A higher AQI indicates more polluted air and greater health risks. How does poor AQI affect health? When AQI levels are poor, pollutants such as PM2.5, PM10, nitrogen dioxide, sulphur dioxide and ozone can enter deep into the lungs. Some of these pollutants can also enter the bloodstream and spread throughout the body. Exposure to polluted air can cause several health problems, both immediately and over the long term. stories.title: Railways to run 214 special trains until Chhath:Security to be increased at 4 stations including Gorakhpur; surveillance through CCTV
stories.summary: With a large number of passengers travelling home for the Chhath festival, the Northeast Frontier Railway has made special arrangements to manage the rush. It has notified 214 special trains, which will operate a total of 2,044 trips. Of these, 43 trains will originate from different stations under the Northeast Frontier Railway. The remaining trains will run as passing specials, connecting various metropolitan centres and major cities. The railway said the additional services would provide passengers with convenient connections to key destinations. North-Eastern Railway introduces crowd-control measures at four major stations North-Eastern Railway CPRO Sumit Kumar said passenger numbers rise significantly during festivals compared with normal days. To manage the additional rush, the railway has implemented a special crowd-control plan at major stations and increased the number of trains. Four stations have been identified for these measures: Gorakhpur Junction, Chhapra, Banaras and Lucknow Junction. Additional passenger holding areas are being set up at these stations to prevent overcrowding on platforms while passengers wait for their trains. Four holding areas at Gorakhpur station to accommodate 3,000 passengers In view of the heavy passenger movement during Chhath, four passenger holding areas have been prepared at Gorakhpur Junction. Three are located near Platform 1, while the fourth has been set up towards Platform 9. Together, these facilities can accommodate around 3,000 passengers. Holding areas equipped with passenger amenities The four holding areas at Gorakhpur Junction can accommodate around 2,500 to 3,000 passengers at a time. Several facilities have been provided to make their wait more comfortable, including drinking water, mobile phone charging sockets and coolers. First-aid facilities are also available, along with a help desk where passengers can get essential information and assistance with ticket-related services. Large LED screens to display train timings and platform details Large LED screens have been installed in the holding areas to display train arrival and departure information. This will help passengers check their train timings and platform details. The railway aims to ensure that passengers wait in an orderly manner in these designated areas before being moved to the platforms as required. Additional CCTV cameras and RPF personnel for security Along with crowd management, security arrangements are also being strengthened at the four stations. The number of Railway Protection Force (RPF) personnel is being increased at major stations. Additional CCTV cameras are being installed to monitor activities across station premises and passenger holding areas. Railway staff will also be deployed to ensure the smooth and orderly movement of passengers. Railways warns passengers against carrying firecrackers on trains North-Eastern Railway CPRO Sumit Kumar has appealed to passengers not to carry firecrackers while travelling by train during Diwali and Chhath. He said firecrackers are inflammable and could cause accidents, including fires, if carried on trains. Passengers found carrying firecrackers during inspections will face strict action. The railway has urged everyone to follow safety rules and travel responsibly.

stories.title: Chandrashekhar and Owaisi’s parties form alliance in UP:To contest all seats with Chandrashekhar as CM face; eye 40% Dalit-Muslim votes
stories.summary: A new political alliance has taken shape in Uttar Pradesh ahead of the Assembly elections. AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi and Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram) president Chandrashekhar Azad have joined hands for the first time and announced the formation of the ‘Samajik Parivartan Morcha’. Chandrashekhar Azad to be the alliance's chief ministerial face Owaisi said Chandrashekhar Azad would be the alliance's chief ministerial face in Uttar Pradesh. He described the front as a strong alternative to the BJP and said, “So far, our people have only been used as voters. We will work to strengthen this front.” He also announced that the alliance would contest all 403 Assembly seats in the state. “Abdul will now get equal status,” Owaisi said. Chandrashekhar says the alliance will be a strong political force Chandrashekhar Azad said the alliance would not be a third front but the first strong front. He said they had tried to join larger alliances but were treated as weak partners. “We will no longer tolerate disrespect,” he said. Muslims account for 19% and Dalits 21% of UP's population Muslims make up 19% of Uttar Pradesh's population, while Dalits account for 21%. Together, the two communities represent around 40% of the state's population, making their support an important factor for the new alliance. The alliance could directly affect the vote bases of the Samajwadi Party (SP) and the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP). The SP's support base largely comprises Muslims and Yadavs, while the BSP draws much of its support from Dalit voters. The Owaisi-Chandrashekhar alliance could make inroads into both vote bases. This could further divide opposition votes and potentially benefit the BJP.

BJP maintains silence over Dhirendra Shastri's remarks:Akhilesh steps up his attack; what lies behind the change in political behaviour?
stories.summary: Baba Bageshwar Dham head priest Dhirendra Shastri’s controversial remarks on Lord Ram and Lord Krishna have triggered an aggressive response from Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav. Saints and religious leaders are also protesting. Meanwhile, the BJP has maintained complete silence on the issue. This is unprecedented. The BJP has always been highly aggressive in responding to controversial remarks about Hinduism and Sanatan Dharma. Akhilesh Yadav and the Samajwadi Party (SP), on the other hand, would usually avoid speaking at length about such statements. This time, the roles have been reversed. We will decode the reasons behind this ‘change in political behaviour’ of both parties in this UP Explainer… The BJP usually launches nationwide protests against any remarks targeting Sanatan Dharma, Hindu deities or religious symbols. However, the party's traditional aggression and sharp criticism are completely ‘missing’ in the controversy triggered by Dhirendra Shastri’s remarks. There are 4 key strategic and ideological reasons behind the silence of the BJP’s top leadership and spokespersons in this matter. 1. Ideological affinity with Dhirendra Shastri The BJP’s aggressive response is usually seen when religious remarks come from the opposition camp or someone associated with left-wing ideology. In such cases, it becomes easier for the BJP to fight a political battle. Senior journalist and political analyst Siddharth Kalhans says Dhirendra Shastri’s closeness to PM Narendra Modi, CM Yogi Adityanath and the entire BJP ecosystem is no secret. He openly acknowledges and publicises this association and, in a way, also appears to work in support of the BJP. This is why the party is silent. Senior journalist Rajendra Shukla says Dhirendra Shastri is a Kathavachak whose image is that of a supporter of Hindu Rashtra and unity among followers of Sanatan Dharma. Ideologically, he is considered part of the same right-wing and nationalist narrative represented by the BJP. In such a situation, the BJP cannot launch the kind of aggressive political campaign or police action against someone from its own ideological camp or a religious storyteller who identifies as a follower of Sanatan Dharma that it would against its political opponents. 2. Dhirendra Shastri has publicly apologised In cases involving opposition leaders and others, it has been observed that they stand by their controversial remarks or turn them into an ideological debate. This gives the BJP an opportunity to prolong its protests and turn the issue into an election campaign. However, when Dhirendra Shastri realised that saints from Mathura and Braj, along with devotees of Lord Krishna, were deeply upset by his remarks, he immediately apologised with folded hands in a video message on 2 November. He clarified that he had no intention of insulting Lord Krishna. After this, the BJP was left with no strong moral grounds to attack him over the issue. Former state BJP president Bhupendra Chaudhary has also said that the matter should be considered closed. UP Cabinet Minister and former BJP state president Bhupendra Chaudhary said on Thursday that the matter should end after the Maharaj expressed regret. He added that it was not a political issue. 3. Maintaining silence in matters involving religious figures Rajendra says the BJP’s entire politics is built around respect for saints, religious heads and spiritual leaders. The party has always accused the opposition of insulting saints. Earlier, the BJP had also refrained from reacting to Swami Rambhadracharya’s remark calling someone a ‘lowly Brahmin’. This is why, if the BJP takes an aggressive stand against Dhirendra Shastri or cancels his programmes, it could get caught in its own trap. Therefore, instead of treating the controversy as a political offence or blasphemy, the BJP is viewing it as a mistake or lapse made on a religious platform. However, Jyotirmath Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand appears to be an exception. Following a controversy during the Magh Mela in Prayagraj in January 2026, some BJP leaders questioned the Shankaracharya’s conduct, while others called for a softer and more respectful approach towards saints. 4. Staying away from a political trap In the context of Uttar Pradesh politics, the BJP’s silence is part of a strategy. Akhilesh Yadav is being highly aggressive on the issue to corner the BJP among the Yadav community and the wider Hindu society. The BJP understands that if it jumps into the controversy and starts making statements against Dhirendra Shastri, the narrative created by Akhilesh will only grow stronger. The BJP’s aggression would have kept the issue alive in the media for several more days, potentially harming the unity of the Hindu majority. By treating the matter as ‘resolved at a personal and religious level’ and maintaining silence, the BJP is protecting itself from Akhilesh’s political trap. SP leaders are putting up posters against Dhirendra Shastri at various places. They are also asserting that the SP will form the government in the 2027 elections. Now, let us understand why Akhilesh Yadav is being so aggressive. Political experts point to 4 major reasons… 1. Cornering the BJP on its own turf In this entire episode, Akhilesh has spotted a strategic and political opportunity to weaken the BJP’s strongest electoral weapon — its ‘religious narrative’. He is trying to build a narrative that the BJP and religious storytellers considered its supporters use Hindu traditions and deities for political convenience. Akhilesh wants to convey to the public that the BJP’s Hindutva is driven only by electoral gains, while he himself stands for popular faith and genuine respect for saints. By demanding a ban on Dhirendra Shastri’s programmes, Akhilesh is questioning the BJP government. Akhilesh is asking why a government that orders immediate bulldozer action in other cases remains silent on Dhirendra Shastri’s remarks. He has also targeted Madhya Pradesh CM Mohan Yadav, who is himself a prominent Yadav face in the BJP, thereby creating an ideological and political conflict within the party. 2. Building an image of ‘soft Hindutva’ and a ‘true Sanatani’ The BJP often accuses Akhilesh and the Samajwadi Party of being anti-Hindu. Akhilesh has seen this controversy as an opportunity to completely change that perception. Rajendra Shukla says that instead of merely condemning Dhirendra Shastri’s remarks, Akhilesh has made strong demands, including cancelling his programmes and sealing the Uttar Pradesh border against him. Through this, he wants to show the public that he is extremely serious about any insult to Hindu beliefs. Akhilesh wants to establish himself and his party as true followers of Sanatan Dharma, who respect the traditions associated with deities and saints. He has clearly stated that every true Sanatani should boycott those who insult Hindu gods. Through this strategy, he wants to weaken the BJP’s image as a ‘pro-Hindu’ party. Dhirendra Shastri had called Lord Krishna ‘crooked’ during an event in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh, on 29 October. As the controversy escalated, he apologised with folded hands on 2 November. 3. Mobilising the core vote bank (Yadav community) Siddharth Kalhans says both Lord Ram and Lord Krishna are worshipped. However, Krishna’s geographical reach is somewhat wider. Several communities consider him their deity in one form or another. He is worshipped as Vitthal, Khatu Shyam and Shrinathji, among other forms. Siddharth says Shastri’s remarks had a negative impact on people. Akhilesh Yadav is being aggressive to capitalise on this sentiment. Akhilesh sees this as an opportunity to ‘expose the BJP’s true face’. Rajendra Shukla says Lord Krishna is considered the deity and ancestor of the Yaduvansh. Akhilesh Yadav has presented Dhirendra Shastri’s remarks on Lord Krishna not merely as religious comments, but as an attack on the identity and pride of the entire Yaduvanshi (Yadav) community. Social and caste identities are highly sensitive in Uttar Pradesh politics. Through this controversy, Akhilesh is sending a message to his core vote bank that any insult to their revered deity will not be tolerated at any cost. He is attempting to turn this religious debate into a social movement to ensure that his traditional voters remain firmly united behind him. 4. Expanding the vote bank (Raghuvanshi + Yaduvanshi) Akhilesh does not want to restrict this controversy to the Yadav community or Lord Krishna alone, thereby limiting his political appeal. This is why he has deliberately and strategically brought Lord Ram into the discussion. Akhilesh Yadav referred to both Braj (the land of Lord Krishna) and Awadh (the land of Lord Ram). He said the sentiments of both Yaduvanshis and ‘Raghuvanshis’ (descendants of Lord Ram, primarily Kshatriyas/Rajputs and the wider Hindu community) had been hurt. By raising the issue of respect for both Lord Ram and Lord Krishna, Akhilesh wants to move beyond the Yadav vote bank and expand his acceptance among the wider Hindu community. By bringing Raghuvanshis and Yaduvanshis together on the same platform, he is trying to build a broader social and political alliance (upper castes + backward castes) to further expand the party’s support base.

stories.title: US influencer loses 1 lakh followers after mocking Shivani Kumari:UP woman says he travelled at her expense, then defamed her
stories.summary: An American influencer, Marvin Achi, who picked a fight with Auraiya-based influencer Shivani Kumari, has lost 100,000 followers. Shivani had drawn a moustache on his face using soot during the traditional Bundelkhand festival of ‘Tesu-Jhanjhi’. Marvin called it an insult and posted several videos mocking Shivani. Shivani later told Dainik Bhaskar: “I spent thousands of rupees to show Marvin around India, but he left no stone unturned in tarnishing my image.” Read what she revealed about the incident… Shivani says tearfully: “If Marvin had a problem, he should have told us. We could have protected him. Why was there a need to defame me like this?” Shivani says Marvin Achi is a fitness model who wanted to visit India. He had messaged her himself last year, saying he loved rural life and Indian culture and wanted to experience and understand them closely. We welcomed him. Marvin first came to India in July 2025. He stayed in our village, Ariyari, for two days. During his stay, we hosted him warmly, served him traditional food cooked on a wood-fired stove and showed him around the entire village. He then returned to his home in Texas, US. We remained connected on social media. He then came to India for the second time in September 2026. Marvin thoroughly enjoyed rural life in Uttar Pradesh. He also tasted traditional chutney ground on a stone grinder. Shivani says Marvin came to India ahead of schedule Shivani says Marvin had promised during his first visit to their village that he would return only after reaching 10 million followers. However, he came to India ahead of schedule. His visit this time brought him significant social media gains. When Marvin arrived in India, he had 5 million followers. By the time he left, his following had crossed 6 million. Several videos featuring me went viral. One of them showed me feeding him with my own hands and received 87 million views. Perhaps this was why he had promised to return after reaching 10 million followers, but he came to India in September itself. This time, a woman named Fernanda also accompanied him. Marvin received a grand welcome on his arrival in India. Shivani took him around the entire village in a bullock cart. Took him to Jaisalmer and Rishikesh at our own expense Shivani says: “When Marvin arrived, we planned a trip to Jaisalmer. We covered all the expenses from Kanpur to Jaisalmer. Several reels were shot there, featuring camel rides and cooking, which garnered millions of views. After Jaisalmer, the entire team went to Rishikesh. I took care of all the arrangements and expenses there as well. Until then, it never occurred to us that there could be any controversy.” We asked Shivani what happened during the ‘Tesu-Jhanjhi’ festival that made Marvin angry. Shivani replied: “After visiting Rishikesh and Delhi, we returned to our village on 21 October. In Bundelkhand, there is a tradition of celebrating ‘Tesu-Jhanjhi’ for six days after Dussehra. A doll is called Tesu, while an earthen pot with a lamp is called Jhanjhi. A symbolic wedding is performed between the two, followed by their immersion in a procession with music and celebrations.” Marvin played the groom at the ‘Tesu-Jhanjhi’ event. A moustache was drawn on his face using soot. ‘I covered Marvin with a dupatta so he would not feel insulted’ Marvin himself had said: “I also want to celebrate this festival and see how people observe it.” On 26 October, a tent was decorated, and food was arranged for around 200 people. Marvin was then dressed up as Tesu. In our tradition, Tesu’s moustache is considered a symbol of pride. So, we drew a black moustache on his face and applied a tilak on his forehead. During the celebrations, villagers also throw mud and dust. That is why we covered Marvin’s head with a dupatta to ensure that his dignity was not hurt. You can watch the videos from that time. Marvin can be seen enjoying himself. The event videos were posted on social media. Marvin himself uploaded these videos on his Instagram account, saying he had become an Indian groom. Changed his tune after reaching Guwahati, claimed he was insulted On the morning of 27 October, we dropped Marvin at Kanpur airport, from where he left for Guwahati. However, at 11 pm, Marvin messaged us saying people were posting abusive comments on his video and that he had been insulted. Shivani’s team tried to explain the situation to him, saying it was a Bundelkhand tradition and not an insult. But Marvin did not respond. The next day, he uploaded a video on Instagram, alleging that he had been deliberately insulted in the name of culture. He then posted several mocking videos targeting Shivani, including one in which she appeared to cry. Marvin posted a video showing a moustache drawn on Shivani’s face. The background song was: ‘Chhachhundar ke sir par na bhaaye chameli.’ Shivani unfollowed him, Marvin started losing followers Shivani says she had begun considering Marvin a true friend. He was like a brother to her. But his behaviour deeply hurt her. She unfollowed Marvin on Instagram and posted a video explaining her side of the story. She says she had no idea that her decision would trigger such a reaction. Soon after she unfollowed him, Indian fans started trolling Marvin, and many also unfollowed him. The drop in Marvin’s Instagram followers was tracked through the Social Blade website. According to the figures: 1 November: Around 20,000 followers lost. 2 November: Around 25,000 more followers lost. So far: Marvin has lost nearly 100,000 followers. It also emerged that Marvin’s followers had been declining rapidly before his India visit. stories.title: Yogi pauses for a little girl carrying snacks:Takes a selfie with her and invites her on stage
stories.summary: In Lucknow, a young girl stopped CM Yogi at the 'One District, One Product' (ODOP) programme. Handing him a packet of moong dal savoury snacks, she said, "My mother made this." The Chief Minister smiled at her enthusiasm, accepted the packet and then took a selfie with her. Later, when the Chief Minister arrived on stage to address the gathering, he mentioned the girl. Yogi said that she had been calling out to him as he arrived at the programme. While handing him the packet of savoury snacks, she told him that her mother made and sold them. CM Yogi tours 'Taste of Uttar Pradesh' exhibition On Thursday, Yogi visited the 'Taste of Uttar Pradesh' food exhibition at the Indira Gandhi Pratishthan in Lucknow. During the visit, he honoured artisans and addressed the organisers and artisans. The exhibition showcased Uttar Pradesh's art, culture and traditional cuisine on a single platform. A video was recorded instead of a selfie, Yogi said, "No problem, do it" The chief minister took selfies with the children of artists associated with ODOP. During this, the children accidentally recorded a video instead of taking a photo. Someone then said from behind, "It went to video instead of photo." Smiling, Chief Minister Yogi said, "Oh, do it. What will happen? No problem, no problem." The people present there began laughing. Yogi says-With packaging, it could become a brand The Chief Minister said he was very happy to see the girl's enthusiasm. He said, "I will also tell the department that if we include her with a little packaging, could her product become a brand?" Yogi said the girl was not talking about profit; rather, she was enthusiastically saying, "You give us chocolates, so please take this savoury snack from us." He also took a selfie with the girl and later called her on stage with another girl. Such products can be prepared in every household The CM said that such products could be prepared in every household in the state. Local products and dishes are found in different districts. With this in mind, the government is promoting 'One District, One Cuisine' (one district, one dish).

stories.title: Ambulance stuck in rally traffic, injured cop dies:Father says he kept pleading before traffic police in Kanpur; 12 km took 3 hours
stories.summary: An injured constable died in an ambulance stuck in a traffic jam in Kanpur at around 1.30 p.m. on Wednesday. A traffic jam stretching for around 3 kilometres formed at Tatmil crossing because of a BJP rally. As a result, the ambulance remained stuck at the crossing for one and a half hours. Pramod Sachan, the father of the deceased constable, Pranshu Sachan, said, "I kept pleading with the traffic police to clear the way for the ambulance, but no help came." Even after crossing the junction, the ambulance encountered traffic jams at several points along the route. It took three hours to cover the 12-kilometre distance. When it reached Hallett Hospital at 4.30 p.m., doctors declared Pranshu dead. Pranshu was travelling by motorcycle with his father. A speeding dumper then collided with their motorcycle. Both fell onto the road, and Pranshu came under the dumper's wheel. He suffered serious injuries, while his father sustained minor injuries. Now read the full incident... Constable Pranshu was a resident of Motipur village in Ghatampur. He belonged to the 2025 batch of constables. He was currently posted at Tanda police station in Ambedkar Nagar. He was to serve summons in Kanpur Dehat, Kanpur, Fatehpur and Rae Bareli. For this, he had travelled from Ambedkar Nagar to Kanpur Dehat on Tuesday. After serving the first summons in Rasulabad, he went home. They reached Bidhnu in Kanpur Nagar by bus on Wednesday morning. After serving the second summons there, they left for Fatehpur. On the way, they met Pramod Sachan, Pranshu's father, who offered to drop Pranshu in Fatehpur on his motorbike. Pranshu then rode on his father's motorbike. According to Pramod Sachan, at around 12 p.m., a speeding dumper truck coming from behind collided with the motorbike near Buxar Mod in the Kalyanpur area of Fatehpur. Both of them fell on the road in the collision. Pranshu came under the dumper's wheel and suffered serious injuries. His father also sustained minor injuries. After the accident, the dumper driver fled the scene. Ambulance crawled from Tatmil Crossing to Hallet The villagers reported the accident on Dial 112. Kalyanpur police reached the spot and took the father and son to the CHC. Seeing Pranshu's critical condition, the doctors referred him to Kanpur's Hallett Hospital. His father also boarded the ambulance with him. According to Pramod Sachan, the ambulance left Kalyanpur CHC at around 12:30 p.m. and reached Tatmil Crossing at 1:30 p.m. A traffic jam had formed there because of the BJP's "Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy" rally. The ambulance was also caught in it. It took the ambulance around one and a half hours to clear the crossing. Even after that, it encountered traffic jams at several points on the way to the hospital. As a result, the ambulance continued towards the hospital at a slow speed. Father said-He kept pleading for a way through Pramod Sachan said, "He repeatedly got out of the ambulance and pleaded with traffic police personnel and people to give way. He kept saying, 'My son has met with an accident; let the ambulance through.'" The traffic police personnel also tried to get the ambulance through, but no way could be found. While stuck in the traffic jam, Pranshu writhed in pain. He was bleeding from his body. His father kept trying to stop the bleeding with his hands and a gamchha, but the ambulance could not move forward. Doctors said, "Sorry, Dada, you were late bringing him" The ambulance reached Hallet Hospital at around 4:30 p.m. After examining Pranshu, the doctors declared him dead. According to his father, Pramod, the doctors told him, "Sorry, Dada, you were late bringing him." Pranshu was the only son in the family. His father is a farmer. His mother, Vibha, and sister, Chandni, are inconsolable.

stories.title: Yogi promises 1 lakh jobs in next 6 months:Interview ends, results follow; joining letters handed to 28 forensic officers
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath handed joining letters to 28 newly appointed scientific officers on Thursday. The UPPSC selected these officers. The Chief Minister said, "We will provide 1 lakh jobs over the next six months. Uttar Pradesh has changed today. Young people are now getting jobs here without any recommendation or discrimination, and with complete honesty." Yogi said- "Merit is now the only criterion for selection in Uttar Pradesh. If anyone tries to jeopardise the future of young people, they will be sent behind bars." 'Nepotism used to prevail in government jobs' Yogi said, "There was a time when nepotism and corruption prevailed in Uttar Pradesh in the name of government jobs. Qualified young people were forced to wander from door to door. But today, our government has completely transformed the system." The recruitment of these 28 scientific officers is the biggest example of this. The results were declared without any delay on the same evening that the candidates' interviews concluded. 'Forensic science plays a crucial role in crime control' The Chief Minister explained the importance of their work to the newly appointed officers. He said that in today's times, it is essential to use technology and science to stay two steps ahead of criminals. Forensic experts play the most important role in ensuring that criminals receive the strictest possible punishment and that the innocent receive justice. Unless our forensic reports are strong and accurate, it will be difficult to secure the conviction of criminals in court. Therefore, all of you have a very great responsibility on your shoulders. 'The Scope of Forensic Laboratories Is Expanding in Uttar Pradesh' The Chief Minister referred to the steps being taken to strengthen forensic infrastructure in Uttar Pradesh. He also presented some figures- • Laboratories operational in 12 districts: Forensic Science Laboratories (FSLs) are currently operating at full capacity in 12 major districts of the state. • Work underway in six new districts: Work on setting up new forensic laboratories in six more districts of Uttar Pradesh is progressing rapidly and will be completed soon. • Facility to be available at every range level: The government's objective is to provide forensic laboratory facilities at every police range level, so that time is not wasted sending samples from districts and awaiting reports. The CM also mentioned the 'Uttar Pradesh Institute of Forensic Sciences' (UPIFS) in Lucknow. He said the institute had been established to produce some of the finest forensic experts in the country and the world, and that young people were receiving world-class training there. Suresh Khanna said-Major investors from India and around the world are coming to Uttar Pradesh Finance and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Suresh Kumar Khanna, who was present at the event, also praised the state government's policies. He said that under Chief Minister Yogi's leadership, Uttar Pradesh had set new development records in every sector. The arrival of major investors from India and around the world in Uttar Pradesh today is the result of improved law and order. The arrival of these new scientists in the Forensic Department will make police investigations faster and more accurate. Newly appointed officers said-Their hard work had paid off The newly appointed scientific officers were visibly happy after receiving their appointment letters. Several female and male officers said, "We did not expect to be selected so easily and transparently without any lobbying." A newly appointed female officer said, "The interview board's approach was highly professional. The best part was that we did not have to wait for weeks or months for the result. The list was released that evening, on the day of the interview itself. It feels like a dream come true for us and our families."

stories.title: Mother jailed for life for poisoning three children to death:Mixed Sulphas pesticide in tea in Ghazipur; fourth child survived
stories.summary: The court on Thursday sentenced the mother who killed her three children in Ghazipur to life imprisonment. The court of Additional District and Sessions Judge-I Shakti Singh also fined her ₹50,000. The court had found the woman guilty on 3 November. The woman was at her parents' home when the crime took place. After an argument with her husband, she mixed aluminium phosphide poison in tea and made her two sons and daughter drink it. They died as a result. Her fourth child survived. The child had gone out of the house with their maternal grandmother and was therefore spared. Here is the full case Dhadni Bhanmal Rai village is located in the Suhwal police station area, around 18 kilometres from the district headquarters. Sunita (40), who lived there, was married to Baleshwar Yadav, who worked at a factory in Gurugram. The couple had four children. The eldest was 11-year-old Babbi, also known as Himanshu. Himanshu was followed by Priyanshu (8), Supriya (7) and the youngest son, Sheru (4). On Raksha Bandhan, Sunita had gone to Saitabandh in the Revati Pur police station area, her maternal home. From there, she asked her husband for ₹5,000 for the children's needs. They had an argument over the phone about this. On 15 August 2022, a holiday, Sunita became angry when the children began insisting that she buy them clothes. She first scolded the children and tried to silence them. When they did not listen, she took ₹20 from the house and bought a Sulphas poison tablet from a nearby shop. After returning home, she made tea and mixed the poison into it. She gave the poisoned tea to Himanshu, Priyanshu and Supriya. At the time of the incident, the youngest son, Sheru, had gone to the neighbourhood with his maternal grandmother. He was busy playing, which saved him. When Sunita's mother learnt what had happened, she reached the house. On seeing all three children in a critical condition, she raised the alarm. When she asked her daughter, Sunita told her that she had poisoned the children. The three children were rushed by ambulance to the district hospital, where Priyanshu died. Himanshu and Supriya were referred to Varanasi, where both died the same day. All three deceased children studied at the village council-run school. Himanshu was in Class 6, Priyanshu in Class 3 and Supriya in Class 2. Children's uncle had filed the case When he reached the village from Gurugram after receiving news of the incident, the children's uncle, Baleshwar Yadav, was devastated on seeing their bodies. He had said that his wife had previously spoken of poisoning the children, but he had not imagined that she would actually do it. After the incident, the children's uncle, Bullu Yadav, filed a murder case. The case had been under trial for four years. Sunita was never granted bail after her arrest. Additional District Government Counsel Akhilesh Singh produced seven witnesses.

stories.summary: In Thiruvananthapuram’s rocky coastal belt, mussel harvesting peaks between September and February, pushing the shellfish from rocky shores into bustling city markets and restaurants. stories.title: Couple found murdered in Kannauj government quarters:Wife strangled, husband’s skull smashed; daughter injured
stories.summary: A man and his wife were murdered in their accommodation at a government hospital in Kannauj. Their bodies were found lying in the room on Thursday morning. Their two-year-old daughter was found unconscious. She had injury marks on her face and a broken bone in her neck. She was breathing and was immediately taken to hospital. On Thursday morning, a relative of the couple who lived near the accommodation knocked on the gate of their home. When the door did not open for a long time, he looked inside. The bodies of the husband and wife were lying in the room. He then raised the alarm and called people living nearby. After receiving the information, police reached the spot, broke open the room's door and entered. The wife's body was lying on a wooden cot and the husband's body was on a charpoy. A rope was tightly tied around the wife's neck, while the husband had been struck on the head with a heavy weapon. His head and forehead had been split open. There were bloodstains on his clothes. Police have sent the couple's bodies for post-mortem examination. The incident took place in the Gursahaiganj area. See two pictures Now read the full details of the case The couple originally belonged to Pakhanavihar village in Farrukhabad district. The husband was Sanjeev Kumar (35), son of Vedram, and the wife was Shikha (32). Their two-year-old daughter, who was found injured, is named Vanya. They lived in a government house at the old primary health centre on Railway Road in the town of Gursahaiganj. The hospital has since been shifted to a new building on Tirva Road. It is reported that Sanjeev's mother, Kisuma Devi, worked privately at the primary health centre as a midwife, assisting the nursing staff with deliveries. Kisuma died several years ago. Shikha then began working as a midwife. The couple's elder son is Pratyaansh (seven), who had gone to his father's paternal aunt's house at the time of the incident. The family was living in the house on the hospital premises. Two more pictures from the spot Family members accuse them of murder Family members who arrived from Farrukhabad began protesting, accusing the couple of being murdered. They allege that the police had the bodies removed from the spot before they arrived. The two were killed after the room was locked. The police should arrest the accused. Although police officials assured them that the bodies had been kept in the mortuary and would be brought in shortly, they calmed down after that. SP says: One gate was locked, while the latch on the other was bolted from inside District Magistrate Ashutosh Mohan Agnihotri and SP Vinod Kumar reached the spot after receiving information about the murder. The SP said the initial investigation had found that the house where the couple lived had two doors for entry and exit. One door was locked, while the other had been bolted from inside. Therefore, the possibility of an outsider entering was low, but the condition in which the bodies were found raised a strong suspicion of murder. According to the SP, a boy named Shiv, a relative of the deceased Sanjeev, also lives in Gursahaiganj. When the door of their house did not open after 10 a.m., he climbed onto the roof and saw their bodies lying in the room. The field unit and forensic team have currently been tasked with investigating the case. DIG says-5 teams assigned for investigation Kanpur Zone DIG Yamuna Prasad reached the scene. He spoke to police officers and formed five teams to solve the case. He said the post-mortems of both bodies were being conducted. The entire incident will be solved soon.

stories.title: Diwali brings festive cheer to Lucknow markets:Demand rises for everything from earthen lamps to handmade idols
stories.summary: Diwali festivities are beginning to brighten Lucknow's markets. Earthen lamps and handmade Lakshmi-Ganesha idols are being displayed in some places, while colourful string lights and terracotta products are attracting shoppers elsewhere. What stands out this time is that the shopping also reflects tradition and employment for local artisans. Some people are buying earthenware to revive childhood memories, while others are doing so to connect their children with their old traditions. The largest crowds of women are being seen in the markets of Aminabad, Patrakarpuram, Yahiyaganj, Nishatganj and Chowk. See 3 pictures... Lakshmi-Ganesha idols priced between ₹100 and ₹5,100 Manoj Gupta has been selling Lakshmi-Ganesh idols during Diwali for the past 15 years. He has idols priced from ₹100 to ₹5,100. Alongside ordinary traditional idols, fancy and Kolkata-style idols are also available. He said the price of the idols depends on their size and decoration. The ₹5,100 idol features intricate kundan work. Lalita has been setting up a Diwali stall for 10 years Lalita, who is from Rajasthan, has been setting up a stall in Lucknow during Diwali for the past 10 years. She sells decorative items that are hung on both sides of doors. Their prices range from ₹100 to ₹500, depending on their size. Lalita said that because she has a young child, she has to sell the items while sitting at the stall. One-rupee diya, bargaining even for sets Reshma has been making and selling earthenware since childhood. The business has been passed down in her family since her grandparents' time. The shop stocks several types of lamps, including khappars with five, seven, 10 and 11 diyas. The plain diya is the best-selling item. Reshma said the small diya costs ₹1, while a full set is available for ₹50 to ₹60. Despite this, customers ask for the set at ₹20 to ₹30. There was not as much bargaining earlier, but now customers bargain extensively. Handmade idols have a distinct identity Vineet Rawat, who sells terracotta items, has been in this business for 10 to 12 years. His shop stocks elephants, Buddha figures, urlis, bowls, tables, tortoises and Ganesha idols. Ganesha idols are priced at ₹1,500 to ₹1,600, while Buddha figures cost ₹2,500 to ₹2,600. Vineet said that POP idols are made in moulds and are available for ₹250 to ₹300. Clay idols, on the other hand, are made by hand. Their prices range from ₹700-800 to ₹1,000-1,200. Some items come from Gorakhpur, Kolkata and Delhi, while many products are made locally. Connecting children with the tradition of clay utensils Himangi, who had come to Anaura Kala to shop, bought household items instead of decorative Diwali products. For her four-year-old child, she bought a traditional grinding stone, a chakla-belna and other household items. She said she wanted to familiarise the child with the old household items used in everyday life. Himangi said that amid the glitter of the markets, earthen pots add to the beauty of Diwali. This tradition is gradually disappearing. She wants her child to experience the things she saw during her own childhood. Childhood memories brought back by earthenware Pushplata Singh, who came from Banaras, was reminded of childhood traditions after seeing earthen houses, small jata-jatoli, ghariya and plates. She said that worshipping earthen lamps and utensils is part of their tradition. It also provides employment to potters. She bought the items after liking the shop. Shopping at the market instead of online Dr Rashmi Singh, who came from Arjunganj, does not shop online. She said that small shopkeepers and people from poor families work hard to sell goods during the festival. They wait for customers. Therefore, she buys Diwali items, including lamps, wicks and candles, only from local shopkeepers so that their livelihoods receive support.

stories.title: I will protect the Constitution as long as I live:Chirag Paswan promises participation in 2027, motivates party workers
stories.summary: Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) national president and Union minister Chirag Paswan launched a sharp attack on opposition parties from Kashi. Targeting the Congress and the Samajwadi Party, he criticised the opposition over reservation, the Constitution and social justice. Chirag said some political parties speak about the Constitution and social justice, but when it comes to giving people their rights, their voices fall silent. Addressing the public rally, Chirag Paswan said his father and former Union minister Ram Vilas Paswan were no longer alive, but fulfilling his dreams was his responsibility as a son. He wanted to work towards building the Uttar Pradesh his father had dreamed of. Chirag's blunt message on reservation and the Constitution Chirag Paswan accused the Opposition of misleading the public during elections by claiming that reservation would be scrapped and the Constitution would be under threat if the NDA came to power. He said there was no need for anyone to be misled about the protection of reservation and the Constitution. Taking a pledge, he said, "As long as Chirag Paswan is alive, neither will reservation face any threat nor will the Constitution be in danger." He said his priority was to move forward with people from every caste and class, guided by the idea of social justice. Questions asked of the Congress and SP Targeting the Congress and Samajwadi Party, Chirag raised the issue of respecting Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar. He asked why parties that speak of respecting the Constitution and Babasaheb should also answer for their political history. Referring to the contribution of his father, Ram Vilas Paswan, he said that Paswan had played an important role in taking forward Babasaheb's ideas and struggles. He also mentioned the recommendations of the Mandal Commission, the rights of backward classes and the efforts made to protect the interests of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes. Advocating employment and better education for young people Chirag Paswan praised the talent of Uttar Pradesh's youth and said that young people from the state were making their mark in the country and around the world, but were not getting adequate opportunities for better education and employment in their own state. He said that, instead of dividing young people in the name of caste and religion, there was a need to provide them with opportunities for employment, education and development. Questioning the policies of previous governments, he said that young people from Uttar Pradesh had been forced to move to other states in search of employment. "I have set out with a shroud tied around my head; I will not rest until I make Uttar Pradesh a developed state" At the public meeting, Chirag Paswan reiterated his resolve to make Uttar Pradesh a developed state and appealed to workers and young people to support him. He said, "I have set out with a shroud tied around my head to make Uttar Pradesh a developed state. I have resolved that I will not rest until I make Uttar Pradesh a developed state." He said that this goal could not be achieved alone. The blessings of the elderly, the love of mothers and sisters, and the support of the youth were essential for this. Addressing the youth, Chirag said they would have to carry this torch forward. Only when everyone's support and blessings were received could a developed Uttar Pradesh of their dreams be built. Appeal to unite above caste and religion Chirag Paswan called on people to unite by rising above caste, religion and faith. He said it would be necessary to reach every family in the village and every individual in society to raise awareness among them. A new path of development could be created only by taking everyone along. Making an emotional appeal to the people, he said, "Friends, just support me. stories.title: Brahmins, Kshatriyas and Santhals shared common ancestors:DNA scientist makes claim at Kashi cultural parliament; says castes evolved in India
stories.summary: Science has posed a question to a society divided along caste and community lines, challenging beliefs that are centuries old. Were the ancestors of Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and tribal communities different, or did they once share the same roots? At a cultural parliament held in Kashi, DNA scientist Prof. Gyaneshwar Choubey said, citing his research, that the ancestors of several communities with different identities today were once one people thousands of years ago. Citing the study of the Y chromosome, he said that a Brahmin, a Kshatriya and members of the Santhal tribe share a genetic link dating back around 8,000 years. He said the shared ancestry of Brahmins, Kshatriyas and the Gujarati Patel community dates back around 4,500 years. According to him, regardless of caste identities, the roots of various communities in India are interconnected. Castes did not come from outside; they evolved in India itself Prof. Choubey said that the present-day form of castes and tribes in India was not a structure brought by any external group. It developed here amid the country's historical and social conditions. Thousands of years ago, caste identities did not exist in the form they do today. Different social groups developed over time. He said that around 1,700 to 1,800 years ago, the practice of endogamy - marriage within one's own caste or group - became firmly established among communities. This preserved the distinct genetic identities of different communities and influenced the structure of India's population. Shared ancestors found in DNA from north to south According to Prof. Choubey, the DNA of people living in northern, southern, eastern and tribal regions contains several shared genetic components. Although their languages, food habits, physical features and geographical conditions may differ, their ancestors share a deep connection. He said modern genetic studies challenge the colonial view that India's diversity should be seen as a division into different races. Mitochondrial DNA comes from the mother, Y chromosome from the father In the lecture, he also explained the process of studying DNA. He said that mitochondrial DNA is passed from mothers to their children, while the Y chromosome is passed from fathers to sons. By studying the two, scientists can trace maternal and paternal lineages dating back thousands of years. Referring to the worship of Shakti, he described the mother as a source of energy. He also discussed the links between Indian traditions and modern science. Human presence in India dates back 74,000 years Referring to archaeological evidence found in the Jeru Valley of Karnataka, Prof. Choubey said that humans have been present in India for at least 74,000 years. He also mentioned human migration from Africa, the Indus Valley Civilisation and ancient trade links with Mesopotamia. Ancestors from two regions also found in the DNA of the Northeast Referring to DNA studies conducted on the population of northeastern India, he said that the genetic makeup of the region's people reflects contributions from ancestors originating in both the Ganga Valley and Southeast Asia. This also raises questions about the view that the population of northeastern India can be attributed solely to migration from outside. Note: A shared genetic link identified through DNA does not mean that the identities or histories of present-day communities are the same. It indicates a biological relationship between their ancestors.

stories.title: Hardoi girl dies after consuming cough syrup:Mother found her unresponsive when she went to wake her; doctors say overdose caused her death
stories.summary: In Hardoi, a 4-year-old girl died on Thursday after drinking cough syrup before going to sleep. The innocent child had gone with her parents to attend the naming ceremony (Namkaran) of her cousin. There, she mistakenly consumed her grandmother's cough syrup and then went to sleep. Believing the child had fallen asleep out of fatigue, the family members did not wake her up. In the morning, when she did not wake up for a long time, her mother went to wake her. Finding no movement, they immediately rushed her to the medical college, where doctors declared her brought dead. The incident occurred in Peradi village under the Sandi police station area, located 22 km from the district headquarters. Dr. Amit Anand, Emergency In-charge at the Medical College, stated that the child had taken an overdose of cough syrup, which could be one of the reasons for her death. Here is a breakdown of the complete incident: Center's Advisory on Giving Cough Syrup to Children Under 5 Years On October 3, 2025, the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) under the Union Ministry of Health issued an advisory to all states and Union Territories regarding the use of cough syrups in children. The advisory stated that cough and cold medicines should not be given to children under two years of age. Such medicines are generally not recommended for children under five years either. If needed, medical examination, doctor supervision, and strict adherence to the prescribed dosage are essential. Many cases of common cough in children resolve naturally without medication. In such situations, it is crucial to consult a doctor before administering any medicine and to strictly follow the recommended dose.
