stories.title: Hindu Mahasabha leader dies by gunshot in UP's Barabanki:Family rushes out after hearing gunfire at 3 am; rifle found nearby
stories.summary: Akhil Bharatiya Hindu Mahasabha state vice-president Anupam Kumar Singh, 38, shot himself and died in Barabanki. At around 3 a.m., his family members came outside after hearing the sound of a gunshot and found him lying on the verandah, covered in blood. His licensed rifle was lying nearby. The family informed the police about the incident. The police reached the spot along with a forensic team. The rifle was seized from the scene, and the body was sent for post-mortem. The family said he had been suffering from depression for the past month. He had also stopped going outside the house. The incident took place in Aladaspur in the Ram Sanehi Ghat Kotwali area, 40 km from the district headquarters. Kotwali in-charge Dayashankar Dwivedi said: “Anupam left his room at night and went to the verandah, where he died after being shot. Further action will be taken based on the post-mortem report and the investigation.”

stories.title: Gadkari promises new roads worth ₹2 lakh crore in UP:Warns contractors of action for poor work; 100% ethanol-powered Innova to be launched
stories.summary: Union Minister Nitin Gadkari said in Jaunpur, “I am a farmer. I run four sugar mills. Nobody wins in the 10 Lok Sabha constituencies in my area without putting up my photograph. Everyone puts up my photograph.” “All the farmers are associated with me. 10,000 farmers in my area have died by suicide. I have been working for them for 30 years,” he said, adding, "Our farmers will now become energy providers, not just food providers. I am launching Toyota's Innova this month. It will run on ethanol made by farmers. The vehicle will run on 100 per cent ethanol." Gadkari also warned contractors: "I want to make it clear to contractors that I haven't taken a single penny from any contractor. If the work is substandard, I will grind you down so hard that you won't be able to work ever again." Nitin Gadkari arrived in Jaunpur on Thursday. He laid the foundation stones for and inaugurated various projects worth ₹3,677 crore. This included the laying of foundation stones for two projects, bhoomi pujan for three, and the inauguration of three. He then addressed a public meeting at the Public Inter College in Mungra Badshahpur. Gadkari arrived by helicopter at around 1:30 p.m. Rajya Sabha MP Seema Dwivedi and minister Girish Chandra Yadav welcomed him at the helipad on the college campus. He then travelled to the venue in an open e-car. He will remain in the district for around two hours. See two pictures... Read the key points from Nitin Gadkari's speech... I have 10 doctoral degrees: Gadkari Nitin Gadkari said, "I am the Transport Minister. I have launched several motorcycles made by TVS, Hero, and Honda that run on ethanol produced by farmers." "I also have an electric car and a hydrogen-powered car. Its name is Mirai, which means 'future' in Japanese. That vehicle is better than a Mercedes." Gadkari said, "I openly speak about what I do" Union Minister Gadkari said, "I do what I say, and I openly speak about what I do. I work in the agriculture sector itself. I have 10 doctorate degrees for work related to farmers." Every year, we send ₹22 lakh crore out of the country on petrol and diesel imports. If this money is saved, it will benefit the country's farmers. Union minister claims farmers will become hydrogen producers and poverty will be eradicated Gadkari said that farmers would prosper in the coming years through sugar, sorghum, maize and wheat. Farmers themselves would produce fuel for aircraft. These farmers are now set to become hydrogen providers. This would help eradicate poverty. When we decided to produce ethanol from maize, its price was fixed at ₹2,600 per quintal. As a result, farmers in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar received ₹45,000 crore. Greenfield roads being built in Uttar Pradesh at a cost of ₹2 lakh crore Union Minister Gadkari said that he was building greenfield roads in Uttar Pradesh at a cost of ₹2 lakh crore. A six-lane road would be built from Gorakhpur to Shamli at a cost of ₹1 lakh crore. Its proposal has been sent to the Cabinet. A greenfield highway would be built from Gorakhpur to Siliguri at a cost of ₹35 lakh crore. I am getting a road built from Varanasi to Calcutta at a cost of ₹22,000 crore. In addition, an elevated road is going to be built along the Ganga in Varanasi. Its tender has been awarded. stories.title: 68,500 teacher recruitment aspirants surround UP Education Minister’s residence:Blow 'shankh' and ring bells; allege police kicked them and broke a leg
stories.summary: Candidates seeking appointments under the recruitment drive for 68,500 assistant teachers staged a protest outside Uttar Pradesh Education Minister Sandeep Singh’s residence in Lucknow on Thursday (5 November). The demonstration continued for around an hour, with protesters raising slogans and demanding that the government issue appointment letters. The candidates repeatedly blew conch shells and rang bells to draw the minister’s attention and urge him to come outside. They said they were resorting to these methods because their voices were not reaching him. Candidates raise slogans over alleged reservation irregularities During the protest, candidates raised slogans such as, “What is the compulsion? This is theft of reservation” and “The Backward Classes Commission has acknowledged it; this is a reservation scam.” Heated exchanges also took place between the protesters and police personnel. Some candidates lay down in front of the minister’s residence with folded hands, pleading for jobs. Police later removed the protesters from the spot and put them on buses. Protester alleges police kicked candidates while removing them One candidate, who was visibly distressed, alleged that police personnel forcibly pushed them into a bus and kicked them during the removal operation. Meanwhile, a candidate who had been on a hunger strike for 11 days fell ill during the protest. Candidates allege police kicked, beat them during removal from protest A candidate who participated in the protest alleged in tears that police personnel forced them into a bus and kicked them. The protesters accused the police of physically assaulting them, hurling abuses and tearing their clothes. One candidate claimed he was unable to lift his leg after the alleged beating and feared it had been fractured. The protesters also accused the government of ignoring the demands of candidates belonging to Dalit and backward communities. Candidate leaves sick three-year-old daughter behind to join Lucknow protest Ghanshyam, who travelled from Azamgarh to take part in the protest, broke down while speaking about his family. He said he had not returned home for two-and-a-half months. His three-year-old daughter is unwell and calls him every day on video, asking when he will come back. He said his daughter had recently spent 15 days in a medical college hospital. She was required to undergo exercises following an operation, but he left her behind and came to Lucknow to join the protest. Ghanshyam said those in the government did not understand the pain he and his family were going through. Candidate misses sister’s wedding to join appointment protest in Lucknow Ashish Kumar, who travelled from Mainpuri, said his sister’s wedding was taking place at home, but he had come to Lucknow to protest for an appointment. He said family members and relatives had gathered for his sister’s farewell, while he was sitting at the protest site, having left his family behind. Ashish described his decision as a compulsion faced by candidates belonging to the Other Backward Classes (OBC). Demand to revise the result after providing a five per cent relaxation According to the candidates, the recruitment of 68,500 assistant teachers was announced in 2018. They allege that the five per cent relaxation available to candidates with disabilities, ex-servicemen, Scheduled Castes and Backward Classes was not provided. As a result, the results for candidates from these categories were declared on the basis of the general cut-off. The protesters are demanding that the results be revised and a new selection list issued, treating 60 marks, or 40 per cent, out of the recruitment examination's total of 150 marks as the passing mark. ‘Wearing out their slippers seeking jobs for eight years’ Ashutosh Verma, who came from Sitapur, said the candidates had been wandering in search of jobs for eight years. He alleged that reservation rules were not followed in the recruitment process. According to him, the State and National Backward Classes Commissions have also directed that reservation rules be followed in the matter. The candidates are demanding that the commission's orders be implemented and the recruitment process completed.

stories.title: Azam says he is being kept in jail for elections:‘I will die in jail at this rate’; SC asks High Court to decide on bail
stories.summary: Azam Khan did not appear before the Supreme Court in person. He conveyed these statements to the court through his lawyer, Kapil Sibal. The court asked the Chief Justice of the High Court to list the case for hearing before a Division Bench before November 16. The bench must pass an interim order on Azam's petition on November 16 itself. On October 31, the Enforcement Directorate (ED) arrested Azam in a money laundering case at the gate of Rampur jail, as soon as he was released from prison. The next morning, a special PMLA court sent him to Ghaziabad's Dasna jail in 14-day judicial custody. Sibal says goats and cows were described as proceeds of crime Kapil Sibal told the court that the ED's arrest was made with malicious intent. The case dates back to 2006, while the FIR was filed in 2019. He questioned how the PMLA came into the picture. He said, "Look at the allegations. There is a list stating that in 2016, the accused entered a house, looted Rs 5,000 and a pair of gold earrings weighing one tola, and demolished the house using a bulldozer." He added, "Another complaint says that on the same day, the accused entered another house, threatened the family and looted cash. They took away four goats and demolished the house. Goats and cows have been described as proceeds of crime. What is all this?" CJI says, 'There may be merit in your argument' CJI Surya Kant told Sibal, "There may be merit in what you are saying, but we do not want to express any opinion at this stage." What is the case in which the ED arrested Azam Khan? The ED's action is linked to the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar University and the Jauhar Trust associated with it. The agency is investigating the alleged misuse of funds and construction materials meant for government projects, land purchases, and the source of funds used to build the university. According to the ED, the investigation began on the basis of 26 FIRs registered at the Azeem Nagar police station in Rampur. During its investigation, the agency alleged that funds and construction materials linked to government contracts were used to build the university campus. The value of 59 buildings and land acquired through 114 sale deeds was estimated at Rs 499.09 crore, while only Rs 72.63 crore could be accounted for through legitimate sources. The agency has treated the remaining Rs 426.46 crore as alleged proceeds of crime. On this basis, the ED provisionally attached university land and buildings worth around Rs 426.46 crore on October 28. Read what happened after Azam walked out of jail Azam Khan walked out of Rampur jail with his son Abdullah at 7.15 pm on Saturday, October 31, after 11 months. An ED team had entered the jail 15 minutes before his release. A total of 24 CRPF personnel were also deployed. At the jail's main gate, a heated argument broke out between the officials, who had arrived in a white car, and Azam's lawyers. Azam also answered the officials' questions during the exchange, but no agreement was reached. The officials then took him away in their car. During this, Azam raised his hand towards the sky and said, "Allah is watching everything. What more can I say now? This is the punishment for being a Muslim. My mistake is that a Muslim built a university. This is our crime." On October 29, the High Court suspended the 10-year prison sentence awarded to Azam and his son Abdullah in the two-PAN-card case and granted bail to both. Following this, they were released from Rampur jail. Two cases pending against Azam Khan 1. First case: On October 14, the Enforcement Directorate (ED) registered an FIR over alleged financial irregularities linked to the Jauhar Trust and the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar University. The FIR was registered at Azeem Nagar police station in Rampur. The ED suspects irregularities in the sources of funds received by the trust and university and how the money was used. 2. Second case: This case relates to alleged irregularities in the sale of land belonging to the Uttar Pradesh State Haj Committee. A Vigilance Department investigation confirmed a revenue loss of Rs 2.08 crore to the committee due to the land sale. Five people, including Azam Khan, have been named as accused in the case. They include then secretary Akhlaq Ahmed, Dr MAA Khan, Aamish Developers proprietor Mohammad Ayub, and Mustaqeem Ahmed.

stories.title: Yogi announces Diwali bonus for 14.5 lakh employees:Group C, Group D and work-charged staff to benefit
stories.summary: The Yogi government has presented a Diwali bonus gift to state government employees. A 30-day bonus will be provided for the financial year 2025–26. Following the Governor's approval on Thursday, Principal Secretary of the Finance Department, Alok Kumar, issued the order. This move is expected to benefit around 14.50 lakh non-gazetted employees. Eligible employees will receive a maximum bonus of ₹6,908. Who will get the bonus and how much will they receive? Employees up to Level-8 are eligible: Employees who fall under the pay scale of ₹47,600 to ₹1,51,100 will come under the purview of this bonus. Non-gazetted employees up to the grade pay of ₹4,800 in the old pay scale will also be eligible. Maximum bonus of ₹6,908: For the calculation of the bonus, the maximum monthly salary will be capped at ₹7,000. Based on this limit, the maximum 30-day bonus comes out to ₹6,908. Daily Wager Employees to Get ₹1,184: Daily wager employees who have worked continuously for 3 years will receive the bonus. For this, it is mandatory to have worked at least 240 days per year in a 6-day week system, and 206 days per year in a 5-day week system. They will receive a maximum bonus of ₹1,184. How Will the Bonus Be Paid? 75% of the amount deposited into PF: 75% of the total bonus received by the employees will be deposited into their Provident Fund (PF) accounts. 25% of the amount paid in cash: The remaining 25% of the bonus amount will be paid to the employees in cash. If no PF account, amount deposited in NSC or PPF: For employees who do not have a PF account, their 75% share will be invested in National Savings Certificates (NSC) or Public Provident Fund (PPF). Retired employees to get full cash payout: Employees who have retired after March 31, 2026, or who will retire by April 30, 2027, will receive the entire bonus amount in cash. Which Employees Will Not Receive the Bonus? No benefit for penalized employees: Employees who have received penalties in departmental disciplinary proceedings or criminal court cases during the financial year 2025–26 will not be given the bonus. Bonus withheld if investigation or trial is pending: For employees against whom a departmental inquiry or criminal trial is ongoing, the bonus will be withheld until a verdict is reached. If the employee is acquitted, the withheld bonus will be released. One year of continuous service mandatory: The bonus benefit will only be granted to employees who have completed one year of continuous service as of March 31, 2026.

stories.title: Mayawati says Lucknow will be packed on 6 December:Claims rally will break all records; ‘Beware of hypocrites’ posters put up ahead of meeting
stories.summary: The BSP has stepped up preparations for the 2027 Assembly elections. Party chief Mayawati is holding a key meeting with office-bearers in Lucknow on Thursday. The meeting is reviewing the organisation's grassroots position, election preparations and the selection of candidates. Mayawati will give the office-bearers strategies and necessary directions to ensure victory in the elections. A major decision may also be taken regarding the rally on 6 December. According to information issued by the BSP state office, around 550 office-bearers, including state president Vishwanath Pal, national coordinator Akash Anand, his father Anand Kumar, national general secretary Satish Chandra Mishra and Azamgarh divisional coordinator Indu Singh, have arrived for the meeting. They include office-bearers at all levels of the state unit and presidents of all 75 districts. Ukesh Singh is also present at the meeting. At the meeting, Mayawati will seek a progress report on the instructions issued earlier regarding strengthening the party organisation at the booth and grassroots levels, expanding its support base among all sections of society and selecting candidates. A decision will also be taken regarding Akash Anand's upcoming rallies. BSP to hold major rally in Lucknow on 6 December The BSP is preparing to demonstrate its political strength through a major rally in Lucknow on 6th December. The meeting will discuss preparations for the rally. Office-bearers may be assigned responsibility for bringing workers from different districts, mobilising crowds and managing arrangements for the rally. Political circles are comparing the BSP's rally with the proposed rally of Azad Samaj Party (ASP) chief and MP Chandrashekhar Azad at Lucknow's Ramabai Ambedkar Ground on 26 November. It is being seen as a show of strength by the two parties in Dalit politics. BSP has announced more than 100 candidates The BSP has so far announced candidates for around 100 Assembly seats. Mayawati has directed that the names of candidates for most seats be finalised by November. The meeting will review progress in this process. Mayawati may travel to Delhi after the meeting According to party sources, Mayawati may travel to Delhi after the meeting. She has to take possession of the accommodation allotted to her by the government there. She will also attend her younger sister's daughter wedding.

stories.title: Ban non-vegetarian food on Vande Bharat sleeper trains:Saints raise demand at Kashi cultural parliament, urge Railways Ministry to implement rule immediately
stories.summary: The debate over the food to be served to passengers on the proposed Vande Bharat sleeper train between Kashi and New Delhi has intensified. From the platform of the Sanskriti Sansad, Govind Sharma appealed to the Ministry of Railways to stop serving non-vegetarian food on the train after discussions with saints and with their consent. He also called for only vegetarian food to be served on all trains operating from Varanasi. The issue arose amid discussions about the Vande Bharat sleeper train operating six days a week between Varanasi and New Delhi from 31 October. People associated with Kashi's religious and social organisations have questioned why the same arrangement cannot be introduced on trains running from Kashi when only vegetarian food is served on the Vande Bharat trains travelling from Ayodhya to New Delhi and from Delhi to Katra (the Vaishno Devi shrine). Discussion on religious faith and catering arrangements Those associated with Kashi's religious traditions believe that food served on trains connecting religious cities should take local religious and cultural sentiments into account. On this basis, there are also growing demands for vegetarian food to be served on Vande Bharat trains operating from Varanasi. Swami Jitendranand, national general secretary of the Akhil Bharatiya Sant Samiti, said, “When meat is not served on Vande Bharat trains on the Ayodhya and Vaishno Devi routes, why is the same rule not being applied to this train departing from the religious city of Kashi?”

stories.title: Husband ties wife to chair and burns her alive:Incident in Kannauj over suspicion of an affair; couple had a love marriage
stories.summary: A husband burned his wife alive. He allegedly suspected his wife and believed she was having an affair with someone else in Kannauj. At 7 a.m. on Thursday, the husband tied his wife to a chair, poured petrol over her, and set her on fire. Seeing the high flames, local residents rushed to the spot. The police and fire brigade were informed. The fire was brought under control after around one and a half hours of effort. When firefighters entered the house, they found the woman's skeleton. The incident took place in Jagatpur village, under the Chhibramau Kotwali police station area, 40 kilometres from the district headquarters. The deceased has been identified as Sonam. Her husband, Sukhbir Singh alias Monu, has fled with the children. 3 pictures of the incident- Here is the full case, step by step- Sukhbir Singh, a resident of Jagatpur, had a love marriage with Sonam 11 years ago. They have two children. Their elder son is seven years old, and their daughter is five. Sukhbir lives in Hisar, Haryana, where he works in a private job. Villagers said he had come to the village only 15 days earlier. It was then that he learnt about his wife's affair with a young man from the village. He began keeping watch on her. One day, Sukhbir caught Sonam red-handed. She was talking to the young man on her mobile phone at the time. The couple continued to quarrel at home for the next two days. On Thursday morning, he left home in anger. Half an hour later, he returned with petrol in a bottle. After setting the house on fire, he fled. After receiving information about the incident, Chhibramau Kotwali in-charge Kapil Dubey reached the spot with a police team and inspected the scene. He said, “The husband burned his wife alive and killed her. He has fled the spot. People in the surrounding area are being questioned. Raids are being conducted to arrest the accused.”

stories.title: Blood smuggling racket busted in Gorakhpur, 2 arrested:Blood brought from Moradabad; accused tore up notice and threw it at police, showing no fear of being caught
stories.summary: Police have arrested two members of a gang involved in illegally smuggling blood in Gorakhpur. One hundred units of blood were recovered from a car in their possession. Disclosing the operation on Wednesday, police said the blood had been brought from the SS Charitable Blood Bank in Moradabad. It was to be supplied to Arogya Blood Bank in Gorakhpur. The two arrested accused were identified as Faheem Ahmed, a resident of Civil Lines in Moradabad, and Taj Guddu of Sirshwagaur in Bhojpur. After catching the accused travelling in the car red-handed, police served them both a notice for further action. The accused refused to sign it, tore up the notice and threw it in the policemen's faces. The police then began questioning them strictly. The Ramgarhtal police and the Drug Department team were involved in the action. According to the police, information had been received about a gang that was bringing blood from Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh concealed in vehicles and selling it in the district at high prices. The names of more people involved in the illegal blood trade in Gorakhpur have also emerged. The police are gathering evidence about them. SSP orders probe According to the police, they had been receiving continuous information about blood smuggling. Following this, Ramgarhtal police outpost in-charge Amit Chaubey began an investigation on the instructions of SSP Dr Kaustubh. On Tuesday, an informant told the police that a consignment of blood was due to reach Gorakhpur illegally from Moradabad. The police informed Drug Inspector Shridhwajeshwar Shukla and formed a joint team. 100 boxes were kept in the boot The team set up a blockade near the LIC office at Bhagat Chauraha and stopped a white Alto car with a UK registration number. A search found 40 blood bags in a cardboard box on the back seat and 60 in a thermocol box kept in the boot. Smugglers sold it at high prices During questioning, the accused said they bought blood at low prices from SS Charitable Blood Bank in Moradabad and sold it at high prices to different blood banks according to demand. The drug inspector took one unit from each of the two boxes as samples and secured them for testing. Police engaged in further investigation Ramgarhtal police station in-charge Shyama Nand Rai said action had been taken against both accused under Section 318(2) of the BNS and Sections 18/27 of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act. The car has also been seized. The police are engaged in further investigation and action.

stories.title: Denied temple entry, they tattooed 'Ram' across their bodies:Ramnami community recounts its story in Kashi; president says people are now reluctant to get the name tattooed
stories.summary: The name of Lord Ram on their foreheads, hands and across every part of their bodies. From their clothes to the walls of their homes, the same name is everywhere. For the Ramnami community of Chhattisgarh, this is more than an expression of devotion. It is a belief that turned centuries-old caste discrimination into a spiritual identity. When members of the community were denied entry to temples, they chose their own bodies as a way to connect with Lord Ram. They began tattooing his name on their skin and made devotion an inseparable part of their lives. For them, Lord Ram does not reside only in idols but in every living being and every breath. His name is central to their traditions, from birth and marriage to death. Kaushal Ramnami, president of the community, spoke to Dainik Bhaskar during the ongoing Cultural Parliament in Kashi about how this nearly 200-year-old tradition has survived across generations. However, he said fewer people are now choosing to have Ram's name tattooed on their bodies. Denied entry to temples, they began tattooing Ram's name Kaushal Ramnami said the roots of the tradition can be traced to caste discrimination around 1860. At the time, members of the community were not allowed to enter temples. In response to this discrimination, they began tattooing the name of Lord Ram on their bodies. Gradually, the practice became their identity and an essential part of their spiritual lives. According to Kaushal, the community believes that in the present age of Kaliyuga, the name of Ram itself represents God. The tradition has continued for nearly 200 years, and he belongs to its fifth generation. Members of the Ramnami community greet one another by saying 'Ram-Ram'. They also use the same words when calling someone. For them, it is not merely a greeting but a way of recognising the presence of Lord Ram in every person. Earlier, children were tattooed on the sixth day after birth Traditionally, children were tattooed with the name of Ram on the sixth day after birth. However, the practice has changed over time. Today, getting the name tattooed is entirely a matter of personal choice and devotion. Kaushal said only some members of the community now follow the practice. Although a few people from the younger generation are also adopting it, the tradition is no longer as widespread as it once was. The Ramnami community lives in several districts of Chhattisgarh, including Raigarh, Janjgir-Champa, Bilaspur and Baloda Bazar. Its population is estimated at around 5,000. Community emphasises simplicity, discipline and staying away from intoxicants For the Ramnamis, tattooing the name of Ram is not just an external identity. Their faith also places importance on a simple and disciplined lifestyle. Community members avoid intoxicants such as tobacco, bidis and cannabis. They also pay attention to maintaining purity in their food habits. Kaushal said those who carry the name of Ram on their bodies also try to reflect their devotion through their daily routines and conduct. No traditional mourning rituals after death The Ramnami community also follows distinctive customs surrounding death. In most families, a death brings a period of mourning. Many Hindu families observe sutak, during which auspicious activities are stopped. However, the Ramnami consider death a natural part of life. When a family member dies, routine household activities continue as usual. The body is kept in the same room where family members normally sit. Food is prepared at home, and family members continue eating their meals normally. Weddings take place without priests, with Ramcharitmanas as witness Marriage ceremonies in the Ramnami community are also closely linked to their religious beliefs. Families do not need to invite a priest to conduct the wedding. The bride and groom's families perform the rituals in front of a Jaitkham, which is an important symbol of the community. A Jaitkham is a wooden or cement pillar built on a raised platform. It is painted white and topped with a white flag. During the wedding, the rituals are completed with the Ramcharitmanas as a witness.

stories.title: KGMU-Professor named in conversion case joins executive council:Decision on the future of 13 named doctors today
stories.summary: A special meeting of the King George’s Medical University (KGMU) Executive Council (EC) will be held on 6 November following the Special Task Force (STF) report into allegations of religious conversion and ‘love jihad’ at the university. The meeting will discuss possible action against the doctors named in the report. However, the name of Prof. Suresh Babu, head of the Department of Pathology and one of the doctors named in the STF report, has also been included in the invitation for the EC meeting. This has raised questions within the university. The STF investigation has reportedly brought several details about his role to light. He has been accused of pressuring the victim’s family members. Teachers’ association to seek action against 13 doctors Earlier in the day, the teachers’ association will hold a General Body Meeting (GBM) at Brown Hall at 2.30 pm. An invitation asking all members to attend was circulated in the group on 4 November. The meeting is being organised to put pressure on the university administration to take action against the 13 doctors named in the STF investigation. Serious allegations against HOD in STF report The STF report contains serious allegations against Prof. Suresh Babu, the head of the Department of Pathology. It states that Prof. Suresh Babu is anti-Hindu. He takes decisions under the influence of Sumaiya Qayum, an additional professor working in the same department. During a conversation with the family members of the victim resident doctor, he had declared Dr Rameez innocent. This made the family feel pressured to reach a compromise. At a departmental meeting, Prof. Suresh Babu also gave Dr Rameez a clean chit, denied the allegations by describing the victim as mentally disturbed, and attempted to suppress the matter. The report also alleges that Prof. Suresh Babu saves categories first and names afterwards in his phone. After taking charge, he had a category-wise list prepared of the residents in each batch. HOD included as the senior-most faculty member Prof. Suresh Babu is included in the KGMU Executive Council as the senior-most faculty member. This is why he has been sent an invitation to the 6 November meeting. It is also significant that he will be KGMU's next Dean of Academics. He is due to take charge of the post once the term of the current dean, Prof. Virendra Aatam, ends in around two months. In such a situation, if action is taken against them after their names appear in the STF report, it could also affect their administrative positions and future claims. Teachers' Association Also Divided into Two Factions There is no consensus within the Teachers' Association on the issue. The teachers appear to be divided into two factions. One faction is defending the doctors named in the investigation, while the other is demanding action based on the STF report. There is also discussion that one faction of the teachers may boycott the meeting. Invitations Sent to 22 Executive Council Members According to a letter issued by the KGMU Registrar's Office on 2 November 2026, a special meeting of the Executive Council has been convened at 3 p.m. on 6 November in the boardroom of the Administrative Building. The meeting will be chaired by Vice-Chancellor Prof. Sonia Nityanand. Invitations have been sent to 22 members of the Executive Council. See the names of the members invited to the Executive Council

stories.title: Husband and wife burnt alive in house fire in Hathras:Couple were asleep when the fire broke out; children had gone out to attend a wedding party
stories.summary: A massive fire broke out at a house in Hathras around 2 am on Wednesday night, killing a 71-year-old man and his 65-year-old wife. The couple were asleep when the fire started and did not get a chance to escape. Neighbours noticed flames and thick smoke rising from the house and alerted the police, fire brigade and State Disaster Response Force (SDRF). Firefighters brought the blaze under control after nearly two hours of efforts. During the rescue operation, two bodies were recovered from inside the house. They were so badly burnt that identifying them proved difficult. According to the police, a short circuit caused the fire. The family was engaged in tailoring work and had stored a large quantity of material at home for the festive season. The material is believed to have helped the fire spread rapidly, engulfing the entire house within minutes. The deceased have been identified as Shahzad (71) and his wife, Salma Begum (65). Other family members had gone to attend a wedding ceremony when the incident occurred. The fire broke out in the Sadabad Kotwali area, around 20 km from the district headquarters. 2 pictures of the incident- First, learn about the family- Shahzad (70), a resident of Kaharan locality in Sadabad, owns a two-storey house. He used to work as a tailor. He married Salma Begum (65) for the second time a year and a half ago. His first wife, Hasina, died of an illness two and a half years ago. They had four sons-Sanu, Salman, Saddan and Sabbu. All of them are married. The youngest son, Sabbu, lived with Shahzad along with his wife and children. The other sons live elsewhere with their families. Sabbu and Salman sell goods by hawking, while Sanu does sewing and embroidery work. Saddan, meanwhile, runs a business selling imitation anklets. Neighbours said Sabbu had gone to Mathura on Wednesday to sell goods by hawking. He then went to his in-laws' home in Agra, where there was a wedding. His wife and children were already in Agra. Now, let us understand the entire matter in sequence- According to police, the husband and wife slept on the lower floor of the two-storey house, while their younger son lived with his family on the upper floor. As the son was not at home on Wednesday, the couple were sleeping on the first floor. They had dinner and went to sleep at night. The house caught fire at 2 a.m. As it was the festive season, a large stock of new clothes for stitching had been stored in the house. Because of this, the fire spread rapidly. On receiving the information, the police and fire brigade teams reached the spot. Given the intensity of the fire, an SDRF team also reached the site and began relief and rescue operations. SDRF officer Rajat Kumar said, "His team was on duty in Vrindavan. As soon as he received information that a house had caught fire in Sadabad, he reached the spot with the personnel and had the rescue operation started." Couple died of suffocation after inhaling smoke, doctor says Dr Neeraj Verma of Sadabad Community Health Centre (CHC) said both bodies had suffered burns covering more than 50% of their surface. Initial findings indicate that the couple died of suffocation after inhaling smoke. Several parts of their bodies were also badly burnt.

stories.title: Fog engulfs 10 UP cities, cold to intensify on Diwali:Visibility drops to 10 metres on roads; air quality deteriorates in Noida and Ghaziabad
stories.summary: Light chill is now being felt in the mornings and evenings in Uttar Pradesh, and fog has begun to form in several districts. On Thursday morning, fog covered 10 cities, including Lucknow, Sambhal, Shravasti and Deoria. In Shravasti, visibility fell below 10 metres, making it hard to see anything on the roads. Weather scientists say the cold will deepen across the state in the week of Diwali. Temperatures to fall further in Diwali week Prof Manoj Srivastava, a weather scientist at Banaras Hindu University (BHU) in Varanasi, said temperatures were likely to fall further during Diwali week. “Fog may persist in the mornings. With the change in weather, the morning and evening chill will increase,” he said. See the weather pictures- Four districts’ air unfit to breathe as GRAP-2 comes into force Air quality in NCR districts has entered the red zone ahead of Diwali. Noida’s AQI has crossed 400, while the air in Ghaziabad, Hapur and Baghpat has also reached the red zone. The second stage of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP-2) has been imposed across the NCR. Under the measures: Jhansi hottest, Muzaffarnagar coldest According to figures for 4 November, Jhansi recorded the state’s highest maximum temperature at 33C. Varanasi and Bahraich followed with 32.2C, while Prayagraj logged 32C and Gorakhpur 31.6C. Among minimum temperatures, Varanasi recorded 20C. Lakhimpur Kheri registered 20.2C, Ayodhya 20.5C, Ballia 20.7C and Fatehpur 22C. Muzaffarnagar felt the coldest, with the mercury dipping to 15.3C on Tuesday night. CM orders immediate compensation for crop losses Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has taken up the damage caused to crops by continuous rain from Storm Arnab between 29 and 31 October. He has directed all district magistrates to go into the field and assess the losses immediately. He also ordered prompt compensation for farmers and said the government would bring a special package for them. With rain likely in November, farmers have been advised to be cautious in managing rabi crops. In Purvanchal in particular, they should keep drainage in fields in good order while sowing wheat, gram, peas and mustard. Farmers urged to take care while sowing rabi crops Waterlogging in low-lying fields can damage crops. Farmers should avoid unnecessary irrigation in fields that already have enough moisture from the rain, and decide on sowing and irrigation based on the weather and soil moisture. stories.title: Lucknow to run buses every 10 minutes for Diwali, Chhath:Fleet to be expanded from November 6 to 17, making travel to Delhi and Gorakhpur easier
stories.summary: Passengers travelling home for Diwali and Chhath will get relief from the shortage of roadways buses. The Uttar Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation (UPSRTC) has arranged around 900 regular buses and more than 350 additional buses for 13 major cities from Lucknow. The services will operate from November 6 to 17. The frequency of buses to Delhi, eastern Uttar Pradesh and neighbouring districts will also be increased according to passenger demand. Buses will be available from Alambagh, Kaiserbagh and Awadh bus stations. Five additional pick-up points have also been designated for passengers. 107 buses for Delhi, 44 for Gorakhpur The highest number of buses, 107, will operate between Lucknow and Delhi during the festive period. The arrangements include 44 buses for Gorakhpur, 37 for Azamgarh and 36 for Bahraich. Additionally, 23 buses each will be available for Prayagraj and Gonda-Balrampur, 20 each for Rae Bareli and Mathura, and 17 for Kanpur. The corporation has also arranged 11 buses for Dehradun and 10 each for Haridwar and Varanasi. These are route-wise bus allocations. Buses available from three major bus stations Passengers will be able to board buses from three major bus stations in Lucknow. The number of buses will be increased depending on passenger demand. Five additional pick-up points designated Apart from the main bus stations, passengers can board buses from five designated pick-up points across the city: These locations will make it easier for passengers living in different parts of Lucknow to board buses without travelling to the main bus stations. Seats available in 120 AC buses UPSRTC has announced that seats are currently available in 120 AC buses. Passengers can book advance or Tatkal tickets through the corporation's official website and the Rahi app. Booking is available for journeys up to November 17. The corporation has advised passengers to purchase tickets only through authorised channels to avoid paying extra money to touts. Ticket booking and helpline details: Drivers and conductors to get incentives of up to Rs 4,800 To ensure uninterrupted bus services during the festive rush, UPSRTC will also provide incentives to drivers and conductors. Employees completing 11 days of duty and covering an average of 300 km per day will receive Rs 4,400. Those completing 12 days and meeting the prescribed criteria will get a lump-sum incentive of Rs 4,800. Contractual and outsourced employees have also been included in the scheme. For every kilometre travelled beyond the prescribed distance, they will receive an additional payment of 55 paise. Drivers operating electric buses and covering 3,300 km in 11 days will be eligible for an additional incentive of around Rs 1,000.

stories.title: Two sisters from Lucknow die in snowfall:Brother learns of tragedy through social media; bodies to reach home today
stories.summary: Two sisters from Lucknow died after being caught in heavy snowfall and an avalanche during a trek to Kedartal in Uttarkashi district of Uttarakhand. The bodies of Vartika Verma and Deepika Verma were recovered during a search operation on Wednesday morning. Of the eight people who went missing in the incident, six have died so far. After the post-mortem examination on Wednesday evening, the family members left for Lucknow with the sisters' bodies. They are expected to reach home at around 1 pm on Thursday, after which the last rites will be performed. The sisters had set out from Gangotri for the Kedartal trek on October 27, along with seven other trekkers and five support staff members. The three-day trek was scheduled to end on October 29. However, the weather deteriorated during the expedition. Heavy snowfall and an avalanche blocked the return route, leaving eight members of the group stranded. On October 30, some members of the group contacted the trekking agency and sought help, reporting that they were stranded near Kachcha Dhang. A rescue operation was subsequently launched. Four members of the support team were rescued safely on October 31. Three more bodies were recovered on Wednesday morning, including those of the two sisters. Both sisters were passionate about trekking Their father, Shree Narayan Verma, originally from Sarai Pandey in Barabanki, is retired from the Agriculture Department. He has three children. Vartika worked for a private company in Noida and was also a freelance influencer. She had gone on the Kedartal trek as part of a tour package provided by her company. Deepika worked as a graphic designer with a private company in Mumbai. She was currently staying in Lucknow while working from home. Both sisters were passionate about trekking and had completed several treks in India and Nepal. Around two months ago, they had returned from a trip to the Valley of Flowers and Hemkund Sahib. A year earlier, they had also completed the Kedarkantha trek in Uttarkashi's Mori area with their brother Atul and some friends. Brother learnt about the tragedy through social media Atul Verma, the sisters' brother, travelled to Uttarkashi with other family members to search for them. According to Atul, the trekking agency did not inform the family about the incident. He learnt about the tragedy after seeing news reports on social media. The family has raised questions about the trekking agency's role. They allege that the trek was allowed to proceed despite bad weather and that the agency failed to inform them promptly after the incident. The family said that if they had received the information in time, they could have reached the area immediately to seek help.

stories.title: Healthy kidneys labelled 'failed' to extract money from patients:UP labs allegedly prepare false reports at doctors' behest; camera captures deal
stories.summary: Doctors in Uttar Pradesh are allegedly exploiting patients by showing them as suffering from illnesses in pathology reports. Patients whose liver and kidneys are functioning normally are being diagnosed with serious infections and admitted to hospitals. The entire racket is allegedly being run through a nexus between doctors and pathology lab operators. After receiving information about such labs, the Dainik Bhaskar team conducted an investigation. It found that doctors were striking deals with pathology lab operators through agents who collect samples for medical tests. The labs were then allegedly persuaded to prepare reports as required by the doctors in exchange for hefty commissions. The entire operation revolves around keeping patients admitted to hospitals for longer periods and charging them large sums in the name of prolonged treatment. During the investigation, we reached four such pathology labs in Lucknow. Read the full investigation... To expose pathology labs involved in malpractice, three Bhaskar reporters got two blood samples each collected from themselves. The first sample of each reporter was submitted to a major pathology laboratory in the city. The second was given to different labs where reports showing patients as ill were allegedly being prepared in collusion with doctors. A Bhaskar reporter posed as a sample collection agent, also known as a collection boy, and met the lab operators. He told them that he could provide samples worth ₹2,000-3,000 every day, on the condition that some reports would have to be altered at the doctors' request. This meant that even a patient with an ordinary fever would have to be shown as suffering from dengue or a serious liver or kidney infection. In return, the lab operators would get business, while doctors and collection agents would receive a hefty share of the fees as commission. At one pathology lab, we met a technician named Nisha. She claimed that she could alter normal reports according to the doctor's requirements. The diagnostic centre is run by Man Singh, whose signature appears on the reports. However, he is not a doctor but a pharmacist who runs a medical store. She said that the doctors generally stay elsewhere and visit the lab once or twice a week. We met Man Singh at his medical store. During the sting operation, he told the reporter on camera that readings in CBC, malaria, dengue and typhoid samples could be adjusted as required. Reporter: I cover the Indira Nagar area. You will receive samples every day. How much commission will I get? Man Singh: 70% for you and 30% for me. Reporter: The doctors we work with want reports according to their requirements. Will there be any problem? Man Singh: There won't be any trouble, will there? Reporter: The reports will remain with the doctors. They are our customers, so we have to look after their interests as well. Man Singh: Sometimes, patients take their reports to another doctor. Reporter: If a patient shows symptoms, the doctor asks us to get the report altered accordingly. Shall we start sending samples from tomorrow? Man Singh: Yes, bring them in, but don't get the readings increased too much. Reporter: No, no, we won't get them increased too much. Man Singh: Earlier, doctors used to send samples and ask us to increase the readings, didn't they? Reporter: If a doctor asks for higher readings, you will understand what is required. Man Singh: A little adjustment is fine, but don't get them increased too much. Reporter: How does your lab's system work? If we send samples here, will there be any benefit for us? Arijit: We can offer you up to 65%. You will bring samples from doctors as well, won't you? Reporter: We have many doctors. Through us, you will get samples worth ₹2,500-3,000 every day, but the doctors want reports according to their requirements. Arijit: There can always be a slight variation in the sample readings. Reporter: If the readings are too high, the patient could reach a critical condition. If someone has a fever and the doctor asks you to show dengue, you can show it as borderline, can't you? Arijit: We can adjust the platelet count. Showing dengue in the report could create a problem because dengue treatment is covered under insurance cards. (Arijit was reluctant to directly show a patient as dengue-positive because data on dengue patients has to be uploaded to the Chief Medical Officer's office website every day.) The lab reduced the reporter's platelet count by 50,000 The next day, one reporter's sample was submitted to Shaurya Diagnostic Centre. The lab was told that the doctor had asked for dengue to be shown in the report because the patient had to be admitted to hospital. The platelet count was to be reduced to 1.10 lakh. Arijit: How can we show a lower platelet count without a CBC test? We will not be able to show the patient as dengue-positive. Reporter: Fine, please conduct the CBC test as well. How much will it cost? Arijit: It will cost ₹2,800. What platelet count do you want? Reporter: Keep it around 1 lakh. Arijit: All right. Lab operator says: The report is normal, but we will alter it In the evening, Arijit called the reporter and said that the patient's report was completely normal, but he would get some changes made. Arijit: Brother, all the results are coming back negative. The patient has neither typhoid nor dengue nor malaria. Reporter: Yes, the patient is experiencing some weakness. No problem, just reduce the platelet count to 1 lakh and show dengue. Arijit: We can make it 1.60 lakh. Reporter: Please do it. The report will remain with our doctor. Arijit: Should I make it 1.20 lakh? Reporter: Come on, just make it 1 lakh and show dengue in the report. Arijit: How can we show dengue in the report? The dengue test is negative. Reporter: Make it positive, since you are already reducing the platelet count. Arijit: Yes, we will reduce the platelet count. The pathology lab prepared the report as requested by the reporter A short while later, the test report arrived on the reporter's mobile phone. The platelet count had been reduced to 1.10 lakh. The report from the reporter's second sample, which had been submitted to another lab, showed a platelet count of 1.74 lakh, indicating a normal level. (During the deal with the pathology lab, it emerged that centres reduce platelet counts at doctors' requests. Doctors then use these reports to show patients as having a serious dengue infection and admit them to hospital.) A young man at the reception arranged a phone conversation with the lab operator, Ahmed Ansari. Ahmed asked the reporter to meet him at Tedhi Puliya to discuss the deal. He said that he also operated labs in Varanasi, Balrampur and Siddharthnagar, besides Lucknow. He proposed a deal to shift patients from the medical college (KGMU) to private hospitals and collect their samples. Reporter: We collect samples for both patients and laboratories. Ahmed: Yes, where do you get patients admitted? From which places do you get work? Reporter: We have many doctors and a large number of our own patients through our personal network. Ahmed: You don't have anything at the medical college? We need to get patients shifted from there. There is demand for specialised tests. Both you and we will make money from it. Reports are not available on the same day there. Even CBC reports take 2-3 days. Reporter: We know the president of the employees' union there. Ahmed: Yes, that will help you get a good number of samples. If you also get patients shifted and admitted to private hospitals, you will earn at least ₹4,000 per patient. Reporter: We can even divert patients from Gorakhpur. Ahmed: Go ahead. Anyone coming to Lucknow from Gorakhpur will bring at least ₹10-15 lakh. We have a good hospital near Paharpur crossing. All the doctors are available at our Medico Hospital. Reporter: Yes, we will look into both. Ahmed: You will collect samples as well, so you will earn double. There is a hefty commission for patients. Reporter: The Gorakhpur and medical college arrangements will both be sorted. You can explain the system, and we will come for a meeting. Ahmed: There is no need to explain anything. The people involved already know everything that goes on behind the scenes. Some people don't do it, but those who do, do it openly. The reporter then handed Ahmed a sample, claiming that it belonged to a patient whose doctor wanted a serious kidney infection to be shown in the report. The reporter asked him to conduct a KFT (Kidney Function Test) and increase the creatinine level to 8-10 because the patient's condition had to be shown as critical. Reporter: For now, this is only a sample for a kidney function test. We will also provide a surgical profile sample by the evening. Ahmed: Is this an actual patient or has a file been created? Reporter: No file has been created. The patient is ill. The report will be close to normal, but the doctor has made a request, so please do it. Ahmed: Give me a 30% cut. Reporter: You can decide the arrangement for the doctor's share, because the doctor will get the report prepared according to his own requirements. Ahmed: (Holding the blood sample) What name should I put down for the doctor? Where does he practise? Reporter: Write AK Shukla (a fictitious name). There is a hospital near Ghoda Wala Temple. Ahmed: All right, we will send the report. You take care of the rest. All the PROs here know me. By evening, the report arrived on the reporter's mobile phone. The creatinine level was shown as 8.1, whereas the normal range is 0.55-1.1. The report of the reporter's second sample, which had been submitted to another pathology lab, showed a creatinine level of 0.85. (Generally, a healthy person's creatinine level is between 0.6 and 1.2 mg/dL. A level of 8-10 mg/dL indicates that more than 85-90% of kidney function may have been lost.) Raj: Approximately how much business will we get? Reporter: You can assume that the samples will be worth more than ₹3 lakh a month. But the doctors want reports according to their requirements. Raj: There is always some variation in the readings. Reporter: Sometimes it is 18-20 as well. Will that be a problem? Raj: No problem. It will be done. Reporter: The place I used to go to earlier offered a lower percentage. That is why we have come to you. Raj: There will always be some minor adjustments. I have worked in the medical field for 15 years. I was the ICU in-charge at National Hospital. I know everything. Reporter: My doctor mostly deals with seasonal dengue and malaria cases. Raj: That will not be a problem. Bring the samples every day. After striking a deal with Raj, the reporter handed over a sample. He told Raj that he would check with the doctor and inform him over the phone about the readings required in the report. In the evening, the reporter called Raj and asked him to increase the TLC to 15,000-20,000. Raj sent the report with the TLC recorded as 15,600, whereas the report from the other laboratory was normal. TLC stands for Total Leukocyte Count, which measures the number of white blood cells in the body. These cells play an important role in strengthening the body's immune system. A healthy adult should have a normal TLC level of 4,000-11,000 cells per microlitre. A TLC count of 15,000 indicates that an infection may be present in the body.

stories.title: Pankaj Chaudhary will be CM face… read what he said:On defections from BJP, says those who left were not 'pure BJP members'
stories.summary: The countdown to the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections has begun. On the politics of defections, UP BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary says, “Those who left were never pure BJP members…” On the election slogan, he says the party is not aiming for 300 or 400 seats this time but is set to register a bigger victory than in the previous election. Responding firmly to questions about public dissatisfaction with BJP MLAs, he says their report cards are ready and the organisation will take a decision. On the demand for a ‘Kurmi Chief Minister’, Pankaj Chaudhary put forward his views without mincing words. He made it clear that he has only one goal: “A BJP government in 2027.” Read the full interview... Question: The Samajwadi Party is trying to engineer defections. Dharmendra Kashyap from Bareilly has also left the party. Why is this happening? Pankaj: The leaders you are referring to were never pure BJP members. They had also joined us from elsewhere. This is their decision, and they must have felt that leaving was the right thing to do. Those workers in the BJP who are committed to working for the party are standing firmly with it. Question: No one from Brij Bhushan or his family attended Yogi's programme in Gonda. Is he still upset with the BJP? Pankaj: Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh has raised questions about Rahul Gandhi today. It is possible that he had some personal reasons at the time of the programme. I will look into the matter. Question: Will the slogan this time be 300, 350 or 400-plus? Pankaj: Look, our target is to win. We will register a bigger victory than our previous one, whether it was the 2017 or 2022 result. Question: There is a demand for a Kurmi Chief Minister. Are you also a contender for the post after the election? Pankaj: Look, this may be an issue for those who engage in caste-based politics. The BJP is a party that represents all sections of society. The decision on who will be the Chief Minister is taken after the election. Our aim is to strengthen the organisation, nothing more. Question: Is becoming the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh your dream? Pankaj: I am a BJP worker. I am already a minister in the Union government and have been sent here with a responsibility. Like Arjuna's eye fixed on the target, I have only one goal: to ensure that the BJP forms the government in 2027. Question: The RSS and the BJP themselves acknowledge that their social media reach has declined. What is the reason? Pankaj: We started in 2014, when no other political party had that kind of network. Over the past 12 years, other parties have also built their networks. That is why workers are being asked to adopt new patterns and move forward accordingly. Question: Why does Akhilesh say that the BJP has lost its political ground and ask where it will plant its foot, referring to Angad? Pankaj: Look, when Amit Shah says something, he does so after giving it considerable thought. It is also true that once the BJP establishes its foothold, it does not lose it easily. Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh are examples, along with several other states. People may be unhappy with the party, but they still vote for the BJP. The way Modi and Yogi have worked for the people gives me confidence that the BJP will form the government in Uttar Pradesh for the third consecutive time. Question: What will be the criteria for selecting candidates for the Assembly elections? Pankaj: The BJP seeks reports from its organisation. Report cards are also prepared for all MLAs in their respective constituencies. Both victories and defeats in each seat are reviewed. A decision is then taken based on the prevailing circumstances at the time of the election. Question: What will happen to MLAs who face public resentment? Pankaj: Look, in politics, anyone holding a position is bound to face some resentment at one point or another. It is true that there is some dissatisfaction with certain faces within the party as well. There is still time, so we are also informing such MLAs about the concerns. They are working to address them, and party and organisational workers are also making efforts. We will therefore be able to reduce the impact. But let me make it clear that every decision will be taken by the organisation. Question: How prepared is the BJP for the 2027 Assembly elections? Pankaj: Look, BJP workers in Uttar Pradesh remain prepared for elections throughout the year. During the Covid pandemic, people saw how BJP workers risked their lives to serve others. It is true that their activity increases slightly as elections approach. From the BJP's organisational strength to its smallest unit, the booth committee, every level is very important from an election perspective. We held conferences across all 403 Assembly constituencies at 1.66 lakh of the state's 1.77 lakh booths. All booth presidents marked their attendance by carrying their booth numbers in their hands. We also sent leaders from other districts to physically verify the 10-member teams of the committees. This means that preparations at the lowest organisational level have also been completed. The mandal, district and metropolitan executive committees are also already working. You can understand from this that we are fully prepared for the elections. Question: By when will the BJP finalise candidates for all 403 seats? When will the first list be released? Pankaj: The process has not even begun yet. We will be able to say when the first list will be released only after it begins. Question: There is a major controversy over Dhirendra Shastri's statement. What is your stand on the issue? Pankaj: I have not seen his statement yet. I will be able to comment only after I see what he has said.

stories.title: Why Azam refused to stay in the 'quarantine barrack':Will wife's claim of being 'forced to live in filth' benefit the SP?
stories.summary: Azam Khan refused to stay in the ‘quarantine barrack’ at Dasna Jail in Ghaziabad. He said, “I cannot live in conditions meant for prisoners…” The jail superintendent tried to reason with him and took him to another barrack. However, Azam was also unhappy there because it did not have a bed or bedding. Following this incident, the jail's quarantine barrack suddenly came into the spotlight. Although it is similar to an ordinary barrack, inmates who arrive from outside are kept here separately for 15 days. This helps the jail administration determine two things: The conditions in which Azam Khan is currently being held in jail came to light three days ago, on November 6, when his wife, Tazeen Fatima, visited Dasna Jail. After meeting Azam, she said, “Azam Khan has been an MLA, MP and Cabinet minister 10 times, but he is being treated as if he were an absconding criminal.” A special ED court has sent Azam to Dasna Jail in judicial custody for 14 days in connection with a money laundering case linked to Mohammad Ali Jauhar University. His next court appearance is scheduled for November 13. After more than 100 cases related to land disputes and fraud were registered against Azam Khan, he was lodged in the district jails of Sitapur and Rampur for 4 years and 2 months. During this period, neither Azam nor his family ever raised questions about the jail facilities. This is the first time that the ED has taken Azam to Dasna Jail in a money laundering case just ahead of an election. Questions are now being raised about the arrangements under which he is being held, both by Azam himself and his family members. Could this have any impact on the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections? We discussed the issue with senior journalist Rajendra Kumar, who closely follows politics in western Uttar Pradesh. He says, “This issue has both political and practical dimensions. In politics, when a major leader has to face jail or harsh conditions, it often creates sympathy among his supporters.” Muslim and local support base may rally behind him: Azam Khan has been a strong pillar of the Samajwadi Party in Rampur and the surrounding areas. His supporters are describing the allegations of poor health conditions, his advancing age and unhygienic conditions in the quarantine barrack at Dasna Jail as an act of ‘political vendetta’. A narrative for the Samajwadi Party: The SP and its supporters may present the issue as an example of the government's ‘harsh approach’ and a ‘strategy to harass him’, in an attempt to mobilise their vote bank once again. The question is whether this can actually translate into significant political gains. Senior journalist Rajendra Kumar says, “The extent of political mileage will largely depend on how long the issue remains relevant on the ground.” If the perception grows among supporters that a 10-time MLA and former minister is being subjected to inhuman treatment, it could boost the morale of party workers and strengthen the SP's political position in Rampur and western Uttar Pradesh in the coming elections. Azam has been embroiled in several legal cases for a long time. The BJP is presenting the matter as one of ‘everyone being equal before the law’ and ‘action taken on the court's orders’. In such circumstances, the general public may view the issue merely as part of the legal process. Understand the differences in conditions at the jails as well: The quarantine barrack is not a Covid-era arrangement but a decades-old practice People often assume that ‘quarantine barracks’ came into existence during the Covid pandemic. Separate barracks were prepared to protect inmates from infections, but this is not the case. According to the jail administration, the arrangement has existed for decades. It came into public attention only when Covid infections spread. DIG (Prisons) PN Pandey says, “The word ‘quarantine’ has been used in the prison department since a time when ordinary people were not even familiar with it. An epidemic spread in India in 1928, during which 40-60% of inmates in jails died due to infections. This happened because it was not possible to prevent inmates from infecting one another.” Following this, the prison department introduced rules requiring newly admitted inmates to be kept in isolation for at least 14 days. Those rules have remained in force to this day. According to the DIG (Prisons), some inmates are granted bail within the first 14 days and are therefore released directly from the quarantine barrack. If an inmate is found to have an infection before entering the jail, he is sent directly to the quarantine ward of the jail hospital. When the Covid pandemic spread across India, these rules were made even stricter. At the time, temporary jails and quarantine barracks were set up to keep new inmates separate from existing prisoners and prevent infections from spreading throughout the jail. During the Covid period, inmates admitted over a 15-day period were kept together in a common quarantine barrack. In the language of the jail manual, these are called ‘Mulahaja barracks’. Here is the process followed during the 15 days that inmates are kept in a quarantine barrack: Does the jail superintendent have special powers? According to a retired Director General of Prisons, jail superintendents can, in many cases, assess the situation and circumstances before deciding where an inmate should be housed. For example, following the recent arrests of Saurabh Das and Ashutosh Ranka of the ‘Cockroach Janata Party’ in Delhi, they were lodged among convicted prisoners at Tihar Jail from the very first day. They were exempted from the initial 15-day quarantine barrack procedure.

stories.title: Miscreants flee after stealing ₹4,000 worth of petrol in Lucknow:Drag sales attendant for 500 metres before pushing him to the ground
stories.summary: After getting the car's tank filled at a petrol pump in Lucknow, miscreants fled without paying. When the sales attendant tried to stop them, the car occupants dragged him for around 500 metres. They then pushed him onto the road and drove away. The sales attendant was seriously injured in the fall and has been admitted to a trauma centre, where his condition remains critical. The incident took place at around 4:19 a.m. on Sunday at a petrol pump on Sultanpur Road in the Gosainganj police station area. The petrol pump operator lodged a report at Sadar police station. With the help of CCTV footage, police are working to identify the accused based on the car's registration number. See three pictures related to the incident... Read the details now... According to the staff, a black car had stopped at nozzle number five at the petrol pump. The occupants had filled the car with around ₹4,000 worth of petrol. After this, when employee Satyanam asked for payment, the driver began distracting him by pretending that he was going to pay. Employee had reached the car window with the swipe machine According to the pump's CCTV footage, Satyanam reached the driver's side window of the car carrying a swipe machine. At around 4:21, he extended his hand to collect the payment, when the driver suddenly sped away. In an attempt to save himself and stop the car, Satyanam clung to the window. Despite this, the driver did not stop and dragged him for about 500 metres along the highway. The accused then pushed the employee onto the road and fled. Employee found bleeding on road The other petrol pump employees who ran after the car found Satyanam unconscious some distance away. He was bleeding. His colleagues took him to the Gosaingunj Community Health Centre. After providing first aid, doctors referred him to the PGI Trauma Centre in view of his serious condition. His condition is currently reported to be critical. Police investigating based on CCTV footage The petrol pump manager filed a complaint at Gosaingunj police station against the unidentified occupants of the car. The incident was recorded by two CCTV cameras installed at the pump. Police are working to identify the car and the accused based on the footage. Footage from other cameras installed along Sultanpur Road and the highway is also being examined.

stories.title: WATCH | Muslim women celebrate Diwali by performing Ram's aarti:Say, 'Lord Ram is ancestor of everyone living in India'
stories.summary: Today is Diwali. People will light lamps and celebrate in the evening. There will be plenty of fireworks. Before this, Chief Minister Yogi celebrated Diwali with forest-dwellers (Vantangia) in Gorakhpur district. He set off fireworks by pressing a button from the stage. On Sunday morning, Yogi worshipped at the Ram temple and Hanumangarhi in Ayodhya. He ate with the saints. The Chief Minister met Nritya Gopal Das, president of the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Trust. He celebrated Diwali with people in a Nishad settlement. He went from house to house distributing fruit and sweets. Meanwhile, Muslim women in Kashi worshipped Lord Shri Ram. They offered bhog. They performed an aarti for Shri Ram and Mata Janaki. They then recited the Hanuman Chalisa. With folded hands, they sought the Lord's blessings. Nazneen Ansari, national president of the Muslim Mahila Foundation, said, "Changing our religion will not make us Arab, Turkish or Iranian. The ancestors of everyone living in India are Shri Ram. Religion may change, but ancestors and traditions do not." WATCH the video…

stories.title: Home Guard candidates break down in tears on Diwali:Cover heads with shrouds, lie on the ground as police drag them into vans at protest
stories.summary: Candidates for the Uttar Pradesh Home Guard Recruitment-2025 protested in Lucknow on Sunday. Several candidates broke down and started crying during the protest. They said the final result of the recruitment examination had been released without a waiting list. If a waiting list was not released, many candidates who applied for the recruitment would become overage. The protesters suddenly gathered near the Gandhi statue in Hazratganj at around 2 p.m. They were carrying banners and posters, and all of them had tied white cloth around their heads. The candidates said they had come to Lucknow with shrouds tied around their heads. They said they would die but would not leave the place. When the police tried to remove the protesters from near the Gandhi statue, the candidates lay down on the road. Despite this, the police continued trying to remove them. The police grabbed the clothes and hands of the protesters one by one, dragged them along the road and lifted them into vehicles. During this, the candidates kept pleading with the police with folded hands. Later, the police took everyone to the protest venue at Eco Garden. See 3 pictures- Candidates say those excluded from final selection should be given a chance The Uttar Pradesh Police Recruitment and Promotion Board had announced recruitment for 41,424 Home Guard posts in 2025. The written examination was held on 25, 26 and 27 April. Medical verification of the selected candidates has begun at the police lines in the respective districts from 12 October. The candidates said those excluded from the final selection should be given a chance. 'If we do not get the job, we will take our own lives' Uma Verma, who came from Rampur, made an emotional appeal for a job. She said, "I have left my sick mother alone at home and come here on a festival day. We have come with shrouds tied around our heads. We will die, we will take our own lives, but we will not leave without a job. Life is worthless without a job. "Yogi ji is sending greetings, but our Diwali has turned black. So many lamps are being lit in Ayodhya-will that get us a job? We will either leave with a job or our funeral procession will be taken out. The administration may shoot us in the chest if it wants, but we will not return empty-handed." 'We are demanding our rights, not begging' Candidate Deepak Rajvanshi, who came from Sitapur, said tearfully, "There is no Diwali for us. I have crossed the age limit. If my name does not make it in this recruitment, I will not get a government job. Despite the continued protests, no one is listening. We have all the qualifications. We are eligible in every respect. We are not begging for a place on the waiting list. It is our right." Between 15,000 and 20,000 Home Guard posts may remain vacant The protesting candidates claim that recruitment drives for Home Guards, the Uttar Pradesh Police and UPSSSC are being conducted at the same time. As a result, many candidates may be able to appear for more than one recruitment drive. They say that after being selected for other posts, 15,000 to 20,000 Home Guard posts could remain vacant. The candidates are demanding that a waiting list be released under the recruitment rules and that eligible candidates be given an opportunity to fill the vacant posts. They say this would provide employment to rural youth and reduce the fear of missing out on future recruitment opportunities because of becoming overage.

stories.title: Husband called her 'ugly', wife dies by suicide:Mother alleges daughter was murdered and hanged in Kanpur; married 9 months ago
stories.summary: A 30-year-old woman's body was found hanging from a noose in Kanpur on Sunday. Her husband called her family and informed them. The woman's mother, who reached the spot, said- My daughter was harassed by her in-laws. My son-in-law taunted her by calling her dark. He also assaulted her frequently. My daughter could not have committed suicide. She was murdered. The woman was identified as Ruchi Mishra, a resident of Sisamau. She had got married only about nine months ago. Wedding took place in February; began harassing her after three to four months Sushil Trivedi, who lives in Baikunthpur village in the Bidhnu police station area, is a private-sector employee. His family includes his wife, Manju Trivedi, sons Manish and Ashwani, and daughter Ruchi. Sushil said, “I married my daughter Ruchi to Gopal Mishra, son of Rajesh Mishra, who lives in Jawahar Park in Sisamau, on 18 February.” Rajesh makes television circuits at a factory in Dadanagar. Gopal also helps his father with work at the factory. Everything remained fine for the first three to four months of the marriage. After that, her in-laws began harassing his daughter in various ways. At times, she was taunted about her complexion, while at other times she was insulted for allegedly receiving insufficient dowry. Her husband often told her, "You are dark." When she protested, his daughter was also assaulted. Ruchi told family members about her problems several times. Woman's maternal family created a ruckus, alleging murder The woman's maternal family created a ruckus, alleging dowry harassment and murder. The police managed to pacify the family members and sent the body for a post-mortem examination. Late on Saturday evening, a day before her death, Ruchi called her mother, Manju Trivedi, and told her that she was being harassed at her marital home. She told her mother, "Mummy, take me away from here. These people harass me a lot." Her mother assured her that she would bring her home after Diwali, but the news of her death came the very next day. Brother says, ‘My sister was killed and hanged’ Rajesh Trivedi said, "My sister was murdered. She was killed and hanged. We now want justice for ourselves and for that girl. She was always harassed." Sometimes it was because of her dark complexion, and sometimes over something else. She had been reduced to living like a domestic worker. We feel that the boy was involved in something else. He did not even speak properly. ACP says-Action will be taken based on the post-mortem report ACP Sisamau Anand Ojha said that the body of the newlywed woman was found hanging from a noose. The police have sent the body for a post-mortem examination. Her family have alleged murder. The family have not filed a complaint so far. As soon as a complaint is received, a case will be registered and strict action will be taken.
