stories.title: Son lived with father's body for 7 days:Foul smell coming from Kanpur house; daughter discovered death when she arrived with sweets on Dhanteras
stories.summary: In Kanpur, the son slept beside his father's decomposed body for seven days after the doctor died. On Dhanteras, his elder sister bought a car and went to the flat to give him sweets. When she knocked on the door, her brother opened it and a strong stench came from inside. When she entered the room, she screamed on seeing her father's decomposed body lying on the bed. She called people living nearby. After receiving the information, the police and forensic team reached the spot. The incident took place at Aman Enclave in Ratanpur, Panki. The daughter had bought a new car on Dhanteras Archana, who lives in Ashok Nagar in the Nazirabad police station area, is a homemaker. Her family comprises her husband, Vinay Kumar, and their son, Anmol. Archana said she had bought a new WagonR car on Dhanteras. Late on Friday night, she drove the car first to Panki Temple and offered prayers. After that, she went to feed sweets to her 82-year-old father, Dr Prem Prakash, and brother Vijay Srivastava, who live in Aman Enclave in Ratanpur. Father's decomposed body found on bed When they knocked on the flat's door, Brother Vijay opened it. As soon as Archana entered, she noticed a strong stench. Household items were scattered around the house, and filth was spread everywhere. When she reached her father's room, his body was lying on the bed. The body had decomposed, as it was several days old. Archana screamed when she saw it. The family then called 112 and informed the police. Archana said that they are four siblings. Vijay is the youngest. Their father ran a private clinic but stopped practising after 2015. Son stayed in the same room even after his father's death Dr Prem Prakash used to run a private clinic. His son Vijay lived with him. He worked at Elmco but lost his job a few years ago. Since then, he had been mentally distressed. According to relatives, Vijay's mental condition was not stable. His father looked after him and cooked for him. Even after his father's death, he continued to stay with him in the same room. It is not clear why he did not realise that his father had died. Food had been kept beside the body; utensils were rotting in the kitchen Archana said that their father would cook food for her brother and feed him. When she reached the flat, food had been placed near their father's body. Dirty utensils and food were lying in the kitchen, and the food had started to rot. There was a strong stench in the room. This indicated that the body had been lying there for several days. What did Vijay eat for seven days? According to the family, their father would cook food and feed Vijay every day. In these circumstances, the question remains what Vijay ate for five to seven days after his father's death. Did he cook for himself or eat food that had been prepared earlier? According to the police and forensic team, the body was around five to seven days old. The exact time and cause of death will be established from the post-mortem report. ACP says action will be taken after post-mortem report ACP Panki Amit Chaurasia said: The body appeared to be around five to seven days old. It has been learnt that the son was present in the room. The family described him as mentally distressed. The cause of death will be known after the post-mortem report is received.

stories.title: Woman boxer found murdered in Kanpur:Mother suspects boyfriend; 26-year-old gym trainer had gone shopping for Diwali
stories.summary: The body found in Kanpur on Friday morning was that of woman boxer Mantasha Kumari. The 26-year-old was working as a trainer at a gym in Jajmau. Her parents and family members reached the post-mortem house on Saturday afternoon. The body was identified then. Her mother said that her daughter had gone out to shop for Diwali and had gone missing. She said her daughter had been murdered and her body dumped. They have suspected that her daughter's boyfriend was behind the murder. The police are now searching for the killer. The case concerns the Kanpur-Prayagraj National Highway in the Maharajpur police station area. See two pictures... Now, the full story... A blood-soaked body was found near the Maholi Cold Storage turn along the Kanpur-Prayagraj Highway on Friday morning. On Saturday afternoon, the woman was identified as 26-year-old Mantosha Kumari, a resident of Ikhlaq Nagar in Unnao's Gangaghat police station area. Her mother Sanjana, father Prem Kumar and other family members reached the post-mortem house and identified the body. On seeing their daughter's body, the parents broke down and became inconsolable. Mother says-She went shopping for Diwali on 5 October Mantasha's mother Sanjana said, "At around 5 pm on Thursday, my daughter went to Kanpur's Chakeri Lalbangla market to shop for Diwali. She did not return home after that. Her mobile phone had been switched off since around 7 pm." After her daughter went missing and her phone was switched off, the family filed a missing-person report at Gangaghat police station on Saturday. After a girl's body was found in Kanpur, Gangaghat police informed the family. The family then reached the hospital. Father says daughter was killed and her body dumped; suspects her friend Her father, Prem Kumar, said, "Mantasha was the youngest of two sisters and one brother. Her elder sister Khushboo is married. My son Deepak and Mantasha lived at home." Mantasha began learning boxing with her father after completing Class 12. Her father used to teach boxing to children at Sports Line. He is also a gold medallist. Mantasha has won a gold medal at the Uttar Pradesh level Mantasha had also won a gold medal in boxing at the Uttar Pradesh level. In addition, she had worked as a gym trainer at several places. She was currently a trainer at Fusion Fit Gym in Jajmau. She underwent surgery two months ago The father said that Mantasha had undergone surgery around two months ago after a lump was found in her uterus. As a result, she had not been going to the gym for some time. She had started going out of the house only two days earlier. Mantasha used to travel to Lalbangla market on a scooter, but she went by auto-rickshaw on Thursday because she was unwell. The father said that a young man used to come to the gym for training and would talk to his daughter. When she was ill, the young man also visited her in hospital several times. The father has suspected the same man of carrying out the murder. However, the motive for the murder has not yet been established. Niece's wedding on 18 November; preparations were under way at home The family said that Mantasha's niece was due to get married on 18 November. Mantasha was also involved in the wedding preparations. She had gone to the market to shop for the wedding. The family's wedding celebrations turned into mourning following her death. Meanwhile, Unnao City Circle Officer Vini Singh said, “A missing person report was registered on the family's complaint. The entire matter is being investigated. Further action will be taken based on the facts that emerge from the evidence found at the scene, the forensic examination and the post-mortem report.”

stories.title: UP raises government employees' dearness allowance by 3%:Rate rises to 63%, taking this year's increase to 5%; 28 lakh employees to benefit
stories.summary: The Yogi government has given a major Diwali gift to state government employees and pensioners. The government has increased the Dearness Allowance (DA) of employees from 60% to 63%. The enhanced dearness allowance will come into effect retrospectively from 1st July 2026. There are 1.6 million employees and 1.2 million pensioners in the state. In total, 2.8 million individuals will benefit from this decision. Employees will receive the increased DA amount with their November salary. Meanwhile, the arrears for the period from July to October will be credited to their PF accounts. For pensioners, the arrears of the increased dearness allowance will be deposited into their pension accounts. Apart from state government employees, staff from aided educational institutions, technical education institutions, and local urban bodies will also benefit from this decision. Prior to this, the government had increased the dearness allowance by 2% in May. This means that in the year 2026, the dearness allowance of employees and pensioners has seen a total increase of 5%. How much will salaries increase? Understand the calculation Dearness allowance is calculated on the basis of an employee's basic salary. Let us understand through an example how much extra money this 3% increase will put into the pockets of UP government employees. Suppose an employee's basic salary is ₹30,000. At a 60% DA rate, they were previously receiving ₹18,000. Now, with a 63% DA rate, they will receive ₹18,900. Accordingly, the salary will increase by ₹900. Similarly, employees with a basic salary of ₹100,000 or more will see a monthly salary increase ranging from ₹3,000 to ₹6,000. Dearness allowance was also increased twice last year The UP government had increased DA twice in 2025 as well. The first time, in April, DA was raised from 53% to 55%, with the increased salary applicable from 1st January 2025. The second time, in October, DA was raised from 55% to 58%, with the increased salary applicable from 1st July 2025. 30-day bonus gift granted on Diwali Two days ago, the Yogi government gifted a 30-day bonus to government employees for Diwali. Eligible employees will receive a maximum bonus of ₹6,908 for the financial year 2025–26. Of this, 75% of the amount will be credited to their PF accounts, while the remaining portion will be paid in cash. What is DA and why is it important? Dearness Allowance (DA) is a cost-of-living adjustment provided to government employees. It is calculated as a percentage of the basic pay. Its main objective is to protect the real income of employees amidst rising prices so that their salaries keep pace with inflation.

stories.title: Sweets priced up to ₹60,000/kg in Lucknow:Gold-coated treats, baklava in demand; ₹400 crore business expected
stories.summary: Lucknow is once again seeing brisk sales of sweets priced at ₹60,000 per kilogram this Diwali. This gold sweet is made with dry fruits from 10 countries. Besides being suitable for ordinary people, it is also beneficial for those who are ill. Alongside gold-plated sweets, firecracker-themed sweets have also arrived in the market this year. Sweets made with figs, dates and mango are available. Chhena, khoya, motichoor laddoos, Turkish baklava, milk cake, son papdi, white chocolate and date sweets are also selling briskly. Along with taste, full attention is being paid to health. The manufacturing and expiry dates are being printed on the sweets. See 3 pictures: Hampers priced from ₹20 to ₹3,000 Renowned brand Chhappan Bhog has adopted a highly creative approach to Diwali gifting this year. Instead of traditional boxes, sweets and dry fruits are being packed in special containers shaped like red cylinder-shaped firecrackers, green sutli bombs, anar fireworks and chakris. Not only that, attractive gift hampers decorated on a paper hot-air balloon theme are also drawing customers in large numbers. These hampers, featuring unique and premium packaging, are priced from ₹20 to ₹3,000. Blueberries from the USA and pistachios from Iran used The super-luxury gold-plated sweet has attracted the most headlines. Shopkeeper Kshitij said, "The most unique sweet at our shop is Exotica, which is coated with a layer of gold and costs ₹60,000 per kilogram. We began making the most expensive sweet in 2009, when it was priced at ₹25,000 per kilogram." Its speciality is that ingredients from different parts of the world are used in it. Blueberries from the USA, pistachios from Iran, almonds from Afghanistan, macadamia nuts and Brazil nuts from South Africa, chilgoza from Kinnaur, saffron from Kashmir and a layer of gold make it special. We keep this special sweet decorated in a chest. With a single bite, a person can taste flavours from around the world. 50 types of sweets Dinesh Sharma, owner of Sharma Sweets House, said there are more than 50 varieties of sweets. This time, however, fig cutlets, date ladoos and mango bites have been specially prepared. The sweets made from figs and dates have been prepared keeping in mind the health of patients with conditions such as diabetes and high blood pressure. These are premium sweets made with roasted dry fruits, which further enhance their taste. He said mango bites cost ₹1,000 per kg. Kaju katli is priced between ₹1,400 and ₹5,000 per kg. People are buying sweets priced between ₹1,500 and ₹5,000 in gift packing. Business worth more than ₹400 crore expected More than 3,000 small and large sweet shops have been decorated across the city. Traders said they were receiving large corporate orders for sweets. People continue to buy sweets until the final day of Diwali and have them packed as gifts. Accordingly, the sweet business is expected to exceed ₹400 crore.

stories.title: Jhansi youth crushed to death as gravel-laden tractor overturns:Child playing outside house escapes by running away
stories.summary: A young man from Jhansi died in a road accident. He was travelling home in a gravel-laden tractor-trolley when the speeding tractor lost control and overturned on the road. The young man was trapped underneath. People managed to pull him out and brought him to Jhansi Medical College, where doctors declared him dead. The accident took place on Friday in the Chakarpur area of Madhya Pradesh, adjoining Jhansi. Live CCTV footage of the incident has emerged. The camera was installed at a house on the roadside. A child closes the gate of the house and walks towards the road. Just then, the speeding tractor suddenly turns on the road and overturns. The trolley's hook (hitch) also breaks. As the tractor moves towards the child, he panics and runs towards the house. His slipper is left behind on the way. He survives because he saw the tractor in time. After this, people nearby rush to help. Two young men were injured in the accident. Watch 3 CCTV Footage Clips Read the full story in detail He was the fourth of seven brothers The deceased was identified as Lakhan Yogi (37), son of Kailash Yogi. He was a resident of Khajraha Buzurg village in the Babina police station area of Jhansi. Lakhan was the fourth of seven brothers. He also had three sisters. Lakhan was unmarried. His father, Kailash Yogi, had died. Lakhan lived with his brother, Manoj Yogi. He was returning home on a tractor The deceased man's brother, Manoj Yogi, said, "My brother Lakhan Yogi worked on a tractor. As usual, he had gone to work on the tractor. The tractor-trailer was returning towards the village after being loaded with gravel in Jhansi's sawmill area. Sandeep and Rupendra Parihar were travelling on the tractor with Lakhan. Part of the route falls in Madhya Pradesh. When the tractor reached near Kali Pahadi in the Chakarpur area of Madhya Pradesh, the driver lost control and it overturned. My brother was trapped under the tractor in the accident. The gravel from the trailer also spilled all over the road." Died on the way while being taken to medical college People from the surrounding area gathered after the accident. Sandeep and Rupendra were thrown some distance in the accident, while Lakhan was trapped underneath. After a great deal of effort, the injured Lakhan was pulled out from under the tractor. He was being taken to Jhansi Medical College in a blood-soaked condition, but he died on the way. On reaching the medical college, doctors declared him dead. After receiving the information, his family reached the hospital in tears. The family was inconsolable after seeing Lakhan's body. Jhansi police completed the inquest formalities and had the body post-mortem examined. The body was then handed over to the family.

stories.title: 8-year-old girl raped, murdered in Bulandshahr:Neighbour lured her away; crushed her head with iron rod, dumped body in vacant plot
stories.summary: An eight-year-old girl was raped and murdered in Bulandshahr. On Friday afternoon, the accused took her out of the house on the pretext of buying her golgappas. He raped her in an empty plot 500 metres from the house, then killed her by striking her on the head with an iron rod and fled. When the girl did not return home for a long time, her family began searching for her. Despite an extensive search, they could not find her. Meanwhile, the police informed the family about the incident. At 2 a.m. on Saturday night, the police recovered the girl's body. The incident took place in the area under the jurisdiction of the Industrial Police Station, 30 kilometres from the district headquarters. The accused, Raju Kashyap (36), worked at a factory with the girl's father. The accused lived with his wife in the same building as the girl's family. The police are questioning his wife. According to the police, the girl's family is originally from Badaun but lives in a rented house in Bulandshahr. The family has taken the girl's body to Badaun, where her last rites will be performed. City SP Abhishek Pratap said the police had begun investigating as soon as they received the information. Police teams have been deployed to arrest the accused. Raids are being conducted at his possible hideouts.

stories.title: ₹5 crore gold theft was planned in MP, not UP:Maharashtra criminals targeted the loot to repay ₹20 lakh debt; arrived in a Scorpio
stories.summary: "Our gang carried out thefts and robberies in seven states, including Karnataka, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, but had never committed an offence in Uttar Pradesh. This time too, we had planned to carry out the crime in Madhya Pradesh. The plan was to steal gold worth ₹5 crore from a businessman in an area adjoining the Jhansi border, but the plan failed. The businessman boarded a bus, and the bus reached Jhansi. He was using his mobile phone. During this time, we stole two bags filled with jewellery and fled. Later, we learnt that we had committed the crime in Uttar Pradesh. If we had known we were in Uttar Pradesh, we would not have stolen." This was stated by Maharashtra-resident accused Amol Maruti Pitekar (29), who was arrested. He committed the crime in Jhansi on 29 October along with his father and other members of the gang. The robbery was carried out to repay a ₹20 lakh loan. All six accused in the gang are from Maharashtra. They had travelled to Jhansi in a Scorpio. At present, five accused, including Amol's father, are absconding. Police are searching for them. The stolen jewellery has also not been recovered. Read the full case in detail Punjab businessmen were travelling to Jhansi to supply jewellery Jhansi SSP Vikas Kumar said, "Gurkirat Singh, who lives in Amritsar, Punjab, is a major bullion trader. He makes gold jewellery and supplies it to Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh." This time, he travelled from Amritsar to Jhansi first. From there, he went to Jabalpur in Madhya Pradesh and then to Chhatarpur. He supplied jewellery at both places. After this, he boarded a private bus in Chhatarpur on 29 October to travel to Jhansi. Five bags filled with jewellery were kept above their seats Businesspeople travel carrying jewellery in ordinary bags like regular passengers. They placed five bags filled with jewellery on the luggage racks above their seats. Two of the bags were placed on their side and three on the other side. Three gang members were already travelling on the bus. As soon as the bus stopped at Mauranipur bus stand, the three criminals got off with two bags filled with jewellery. The criminals fled in a white Scorpio CCTV footage shows the three men getting off the bus with the bags. They then escaped in a white Scorpio. The bags contained 6,937 grams of gold jewellery. After removing the stones and other attachments, the haul included 3,152 grams of gold and 200 grams of pure gold. It was valued at ₹5 crore. The bags also contained ₹15 lakh in cash. CCTV footage across 2,000 km searched before vehicle number was found SSP Vikas Kumar said eight police teams were deployed to crack the case. It was a difficult case because the police had no concrete clues. They had only one blurry CCTV recording. The investigation was launched on the basis of this footage. The police team searched CCTV footage covering more than 2,000 kilometres while tracking the Scorpio. This led them to the vehicle's registration number. The police then reached the gang in Maharashtra through the FASTag details. On 3 November, police arrested Amol Maruti Pitekar (29), an accused member of the gang, with the stolen money. He is a resident of Mahalangi village in the Karjat police station area of Ahilyanagar district, Maharashtra. According to the SSP, the accused has been brought to Jhansi from Maharashtra on transit remand. He will be produced in court, where the police will seek custody remand. The Scorpio used in the crime is registered in Amol's name. Police suspect: Businessman's close associate provided the gang with his location Police suspect that someone close to the businessman or a local person was also involved in the gang. That person provided the criminals with the businessman's location. According to the police, more details about the conspiracy may emerge after the arrest of gang mastermind Amol's father, Maruti Rajaram Pitekar. Eight police teams are searching for the father and five other absconding criminals. Father gave ₹20 lakh to repay debt According to the SSP, Amol told investigators during questioning that his father, Maruti Rajaram Pitekar, was the gang leader. They travelled in a Scorpio via Jabalpur to Chhatarpur and then Mauranipur. After the theft, they returned to Maharashtra by the same route. According to Amol, after the crime, his father called him to Rashin town. After selling the stolen jewellery, he gave Amol ₹20 lakh and told him to repay his debt. Amol deposited the money into his bank accounts. On 3 November, he was on his way to the registry office to repay the debt when the police arrested him. The police recovered ₹1.40 lakh in cash and two mobile phones from the accused. In addition, they had ₹17.06 lakh deposited in his three bank accounts frozen.

stories.title: Gangster trains inmates in beauty skills at Gorakhpur jail:Woman accused of cheating people of ₹12 crore teaches children; BSA offers career guidance
stories.summary: Garima Singh, an accused in a ₹12 crore fraud case who is lodged in Gorakhpur District Jail, is teaching children. Meanwhile, Anshika Singh, who is accused in a gangster case, is providing beautician training. Former BSA Shalini Srivastava, who is lodged in connection with a teacher's suicide case, is giving other women inmates tips on building their careers. All three women are using their skills to help women inmates in the jail. There are currently 73 women inmates in the district jail. Six children are also living with them. The jail administration is providing books, notebooks and essential supplies for education and training so that the women can become self-reliant after their release. Read the report... Gangster Anshika providing beautician training Anshika Singh, alias Antima, who is in jail, is now training other women inmates as beauticians. She has completed a beautician course at a reputed college. Anshika used to live in rented accommodation in the Singhadia area. She is accused of blackmailing 165 people, including circle officers and sub-inspectors, over five years. On 20 January 2026, she got into a dispute with the manager of a private hospital during a birthday party in the Singhadia area. She was accused of pointing a pistol at the manager. During the scuffle, the bullet struck the manager's friend in the abdomen. The police subsequently arrested Anshika and her associates. Several obscene videos were found on Anshika's mobile phone During the investigation, the police found several obscene videos on Anshika's mobile phone. She contacted people through Messenger and WhatsApp. She recorded the person on the other end during video calls. She then extorted money by threatening to make the videos viral and implicate them in rape cases. It also emerged that more than 15 police personnel had fallen into her trap. The police subsequently took action against her under the Gangster Act. Accused in ₹12 crore fraud teaching children Garima Singh, who is in jail, holds a PhD. She is the daughter of a railway official. Her husband, Bhanu Pratap Singh, is a teacher. In jail, she teaches the children of women inmates. According to the police, Garima defrauded doctors and officials along with her father, husband and other members of the gang. The gang has been accused of fraud amounting to more than ₹10 crore. So far, 10 complaints have reached the police. FIRs have been registered in five of these cases. On 13 August, 45-year-old Dr Paramatma Singh died by jumping from the eighth floor of an apartment. Police found a suicide note in their pocket. In it, they held Garima responsible for their death. The doctor had been defrauded of ₹1.40 crore. Complaints from six other victims are also being investigated. Former BSA jailed in teacher suicide case gives career advice Suspended Deoria BSA Shalini Srivastava is in jail for allegedly forcing teacher Krishna Bhagwan Singh to die by suicide. Teacher Devaria, a resident of Kushinagar, was an assistant teacher at Laghu Madhyamik Vidyalaya Madarson in the Gauri Bazar development block of Deoria. On 20 February 2026, he died by suicide at his brother's house in Shivpur Shahabganj, in Gorakhpur's Shahpur area. In his suicide note and video, he accused Shalini Srivastava and Sanjeev Singh, a clerk at the BSA office, of harassment. Police arrested Shalini, who carried a ₹25,000 reward, in Delhi. Shalini has good knowledge of education and careers. In jail, she gives other women inmates tips on building their careers. Efforts to make inmates self-reliant through training Jail Superintendent Dilip Pandey said help is being sought from several organisations to make women inmates self-reliant after they leave the jail. They are being provided training in beauty therapy and sewing and embroidery. He said efforts were being made to provide inmates with a positive environment through education, training and other creative activities. The prison administration is also providing books, notebooks and the materials needed for training. The aim is to help inmates begin a better life after leaving prison, using their skills.

stories.title: Fog blankets 15 cities in UP, haze engulfs Lucknow:Night temperatures drop below 20°C across state; cold conditions likely to intensify on Diwali
stories.summary: Cold conditions have intensified across Uttar Pradesh. Fog covered 15 cities, including Shravasti, Deoria, Maharajganj, Sambhal and Barabanki, on Saturday morning. A layer of haze was also visible in Lucknow as air pollution levels rose, with the Air Quality Index (AQI) nearing 200. Meanwhile, rising pollution levels in the NCR and western Uttar Pradesh have become a major concern. Noida's AQI crossed 400, while air quality in Ghaziabad, Hapur and Baghpat also slipped into the red zone. Over the past 24 hours, night-time temperatures fell below 20°C across the state. Hardoi recorded the lowest temperature at 14°C. Daytime temperatures also dropped below 35°C, with Jhansi recording the highest at 34°C. Prof. Manoj Srivastava, a meteorologist at Banaras Hindu University (BHU) in Varanasi, said, “Temperatures are likely to fall further during Diwali week. Fog may persist in the mornings. With the change in weather, the chill during the morning and evening hours will become more pronounced.” 2 pictures of fog and haze- What will the weather be like from western Uttar Pradesh to Purvanchal on Diwali? Western UP: The weather is expected to remain dry for now in Noida, Ghaziabad, Meerut, Saharanpur, Muzaffarnagar, Agra and Mathura. Light mist may be seen in the morning. Central UP: There is currently no possibility of rain in Lucknow, Kanpur, Unnao, Sitapur, Hardoi and Rae Bareli. The day may remain sunny, while light chill may be felt at night. Purvanchal: The weather is also expected to remain dry in Varanasi, Ghazipur, Ballia, Mau, Azamgarh, Jaunpur, Gorakhpur and Deoria. Light mist may be seen in some places in the morning. Bundelkhand: There is currently no indication of rain in Jhansi, Banda, Chitrakoot, Mahoba, Hamirpur and Lalitpur either. Exercise caution while sowing and irrigating rabi crops In view of the possibility of rain in November, farmers have been advised to remain vigilant in managing rabi crops. In particular, they should ensure proper drainage in their fields while sowing wheat, gram, peas and mustard, especially in Purvanchal. Waterlogging in low-lying fields could damage the crops. Avoid unnecessary irrigation in fields where there is sufficient moisture due to rainfall. Make decisions on sowing and irrigation only after considering the weather conditions and soil moisture. stories.title: Blast at Ghaziabad police outpost, ACs and windows shattered:1 injured; Tehreek-ul-Mujahideen claims responsibility
stories.summary: A powerful blast occurred at a police outpost in Ghaziabad on Friday night. The blast was so powerful that the windows in the rooms were shattered. Air conditioners exploded, and a crack appeared in the wall. The sound of the blast could be heard nearly one kilometre away. Fortunately, no police personnel were inside. However, a 20-year-old food delivery worker was injured in the incident. He is undergoing treatment at a nearby hospital. Meanwhile, the terrorist organisation 'Tehreek-ul-Mujahideen' claimed responsibility for the blast in a social media post. Police have begun investigating the social media post. ACP Indirapuram and DCP Trans Hindon Rijul also reached the spot and gathered information about the incident. The incident took place at 9 p.m. at the Vasundhara police outpost in the Indirapuram police station area. See pictures of the blast- Police examine CCTV footage from elevated road The Vasundhara police outpost is located beneath an elevated road. Police sources claim that someone may have thrown an explosive substance from the road above, triggering the blast. CCTV footage from cameras installed along the elevated road is being examined as part of the investigation. Blast may have been caused by seized firecrackers Local residents said police personnel used to keep firecrackers seized from shops selling them illegally in the area at the outpost. They suspect the explosion may have occurred due to these seized firecrackers. However, the police have not openly commented on the possibility of a firecracker blast. Forensic team examines site, says DCP DCP (Trans Hindon) Rijul said an investigation was underway after the police received information about the blast. A forensic team is present at the spot. He said it would be appropriate to comment on the cause only after the investigation is complete. He also said the outpost remained closed for most of the time. Terror outfit claims responsibility, says police were targeted Following the blast, a terror outfit named Tehreek-ul-Mujahideen Hindustan posted a video on social media claiming responsibility for the explosion. The group also shared a note in English alongside the video. The video shows a masked man speaking first in Urdu and later in Hindi, claiming responsibility for the blast. He says the group targeted the police as part of an action against the “saffron regime”. He also claims that they have the right to protect their homes and alleges that the police, Army and judiciary are all being used against them. After the video surfaced, the police stepped up their investigation, while the cyber cell also began examining the matter. Police and investigating agencies found that the account from which the video and post were uploaded during the night had since been deleted. BJP MLA warns of strong retaliation against those behind the blast BJP MLA from Loni, Nand Kishore Gurjar, said the organisation claiming responsibility for the blast should know who governs Uttar Pradesh. He said the government would not tolerate such acts by what he described as jihadists during the festival of Diwali. He added that the police would soon send those responsible “to the 72 virgins”. Appealing to people not to worry during Diwali, Gurjar urged them to celebrate the festival without fear. “They will receive such a response that their next seven generations will remember it. Even if we have to enter Pakistan and strike them, our country will not back down,” he said.

stories.title: BMW worth ₹2.86 crore sold in Lucknow on Dhanteras:4 cars cross ₹2 crore; Mercedes, Audi sell 100+ units each
stories.summary: Luxury car purchases in Lucknow saw a major spending spree this Dhanteras. Around 2,500 cars were sold in the city between 20 October and 6 November. These included four cars priced at more than ₹2 crore and 20 cars priced above ₹1 crore. The most expensive car, a BMW X6, was sold for ₹2.86 crore. The on-road price of the BMW i7 is as high as ₹2.80 crore. During this period, demand for electric vehicles also rose sharply alongside luxury cars. Mercedes and Audi cars were also in high demand. Around 45 cars were delivered at BMW showrooms, while 15 MG Majestor vehicles and between 80 and 100 MG Windsor vehicles were sold. 3 pictures of luxury cars... Customers opened their wallets for cars worth crores This festive season, the luxury car market in Lucknow saw strong interest in cars worth crores. Customers bought cars worth crores of rupees on Dhanteras this year. Twenty cars priced above ₹1 crore were sold. This clearly shows that the luxury car market in the city is continuing to expand. Large business owners, industrialists and customers in the premium segment are showing a preference for expensive cars. BMW X6 has an on-road price of ₹2.86 crore Around 45 cars were delivered at BMW's showroom in Chinhat during this festive season. According to the showroom's marketing head, Parampreet Kaur, bookings increased significantly this year compared with last year. Cars from BMW's MINI brand also received a good response from customers. According to information from the showroom, the BMW X6 has an ex-showroom price of ₹1.77 crore and an on-road price of around ₹2.86 crore. The BMW i7 has an ex-showroom price of ₹2.65 crore and an on-road price of around ₹2.80 crore. The BMW M4 has an ex-showroom price of ₹1.10 crore and an on-road price of around ₹1.30 crore. Meanwhile, the BMW i5 has an ex-showroom price of ₹79.60 lakh and an on-road price of around ₹84 lakh. Pictures of people who arrived to buy the cars... Demand for cars such as the M2 and M40i as well According to Parampreet Kaur, models such as the BMW M2, M4 and M40i were in demand among ultra-luxury and performance cars. Three to four ultra-luxury cars were delivered around Dhanteras. Around 45 cars were handed over to customers at BMW showrooms during this festive season. These included SUVs, sedans and electric models. She said that compared with last year, demand for BMW cars had increased this year not only in Lucknow but also in Agra and Kanpur. Customers buying luxury cars are no longer limited to petrol models and are also showing interest in electric cars. Electric cars becoming the preferred choice of doctors and business owners The biggest change in the luxury car market is visible in customers' preferences. According to Parampreet Kaur, doctors, clinic operators and business owners who travel daily within the city are prioritising electric cars. However, demand for petrol cars remains strong for long-distance travel and other requirements. BMW's electric portfolio is receiving a good response for the i5. Its on-road price is around ₹84 lakh. Customers are now showing a growing preference for environmentally friendly mobility alongside luxury. 15 MG Majestor deliveries worth ₹54 lakh, Windsor sales reach 100 Premium and electric vehicles also recorded good sales at the MG showroom this Dhanteras. According to Abdul Rahman, around 15 units of the company's premium SUV, the Majestor, were delivered. Its ex-showroom price starts at around ₹46 lakh, while the on-road price is approximately ₹54 lakh. Demand for the MG Windsor was the highest in the electric vehicle segment. Around 80 to 100 Windsor cars were sold during this festive season, with an average ticket size of around ₹20 lakh. Meanwhile, MG's new electric model, the Tomahawk, received more than 300 bookings. However, deliveries could not be made for all the bookings due to a supply shortage. Customers shifted from petrol and diesel to electric and hybrid vehicles According to Abdul Rahman, the electric vehicle market has undergone a major transformation over the past five to six years. EVs previously accounted for a very small share, but demand for them is now steadily increasing. In addition to petrol and diesel vehicles, customers are also considering electric, hybrid and CNG options. He said customers are no longer making purchases based solely on a vehicle's price, but are also prioritising features, running costs and better technology. This is why demand for electric cars is rising in the premium segment. Mercedes-Benz and Audi also sold more than 100 units In Lucknow's luxury car market, demand remained strong for brands such as Mercedes-Benz, Audi, Volvo and Jaguar Land Rover, besides BMW. According to available market data, Mercedes-Benz and Audi sold more than 100 units each. Expensive models such as the Audi RS7 and RSQ8 were also among customers' choices. SUVs and premium cars dominated the automobile market this time. When buying a car, customers are now considering not just the price and mileage, but also the EMI, maintenance, safety, charging facilities and resale value.

stories.title: 3 killed as truck rams bus carrying 50 passengers:Bus was travelling from Delhi to Kushinagar; victims were heading home for Diwali
stories.summary: A bus and truck collided in Kushinagar early on Saturday, killing three passengers and injuring six others. The passengers were travelling to their respective homes for Diwali and Chhath Puja. The collision was so severe that the front of the bus was completely mangled. People seated at the front broke through the windscreen and fell onto the road. Police reached the spot after receiving information from passers-by and pulled the passengers out. The passengers were taken by ambulance to Tamkuhiraj CHC, where doctors declared three of them dead. The accident occurred near Labania village in the Patherwa police station area. According to the police, the bus was travelling from Anand Vihar in Delhi to Muzaffarpur. There were 50 people on board. Two killed after speeding vehicle collides with sleeper bus Shiva Travels' AC sleeper bus had departed from Anand Vihar at 1.30 pm on Friday. Dharmendra, a resident of Kamalpura village in the Paru police station area of Muzaffarpur, Bihar, said he and other passengers were asleep when the accident occurred. More than 60 people were travelling on the bus. At around 4.30 am, they suddenly felt a strong jolt. Several passengers fell from their seats, triggering panic and screams inside the bus. When they stepped outside, they saw that the bus had been hit on its left side. A young girl and a man had died on the spot. According to the police, the deceased girl was identified as three-year-old Nandini, daughter of Pawan, a resident of Taryal Chhiram village under the Taraya Sujan police station area of Kushinagar. Her father, Pawan, was also injured in the accident. The identity of the second victim, a man aged around 40, is yet to be established.

stories.title: Inspector and CO jailed for 20 years for gang-raping woman:Victim was two-and-a-half months pregnant; had gone to Saharanpur to secure her husband's release
stories.summary: A court has sentenced a retired Deputy SP (CO) and an inspector to 20 years each for gang-raping a two-and-a-half-month pregnant woman at a police station in Saharanpur. The court sent both convicts to jail. They were seen hiding their faces with gamchas and towels. The case dates back to 2015. The police had sent the woman's husband to jail in a case. The woman alleged that her husband had been falsely implicated. She had gone to the police station to seek information about her husband and ask for help. During this time, the then station house officer, Brajmohan Yadav, and Inspector Vegpal Singh gang-raped her. Brajmohan Yadav was later promoted to Deputy SP and retired from that post. The woman has finally received justice after a legal battle that lasted around 11 years and three months. Read the full story now Lawyer says investigating agencies had given them a clean chit Advocate Rajeev Tomar said that on 6 August 2015, the then SHO Brajmohan Yadav, SI Vegpal Singh, police officer Pankaj Dhama and a constable gang-raped a woman from Deoband in the police station's government quarters. The victim received no hearing anywhere after the incident, and even her FIR was not registered. She then approached the High Court. A case was registered and the investigation was handed over to the CBCID on the High Court's orders. However, the investigating agency gave the accused a clean chit and filed a final report. Rajiv Tomar said a protest petition was filed against this. The court then summoned the accused again. The trial was first heard in the CJM court and then in the fast-track court. The court had convicted both accused on 5 November. After hearing arguments on the quantum of sentence on Friday, it sentenced both to 20 years' imprisonment and fined each ₹1 lakh under Section 376D. They were also sentenced to five years' imprisonment and fined ₹20,000 under Section 506 of the IPC. The advocate said the court considered the victim's statement and the testimony of her husband's sister important. The sister-in-law was an eyewitness to the incident. Victim said: "I had gone to the police station to get information about my husband; the policemen gang-raped me there" The survivor said she was a resident of Deoband. On 6 August 2015, police personnel had picked up her husband in a false case. She had gone to the police station with her sister-in-law to seek information about him and ask for help. There, a constable said that the outpost in-charge was calling them. Pankaj Dhama then took her and her sister-in-law to the police station. According to the survivor, Brijmohan Yadav, Pankaj Dhama, a revenue official and a constable gang-raped her in the police station's station house officer's room behind the station. The survivor alleged that she was attacked during her fight for justice and that false cases were also registered against her husband. She demanded an impartial investigation into all these cases so that she could receive complete justice. Outpost in-charge claimed he was mentally ill In the case, outpost in-charge Pankaj Dhama had told the court that he was mentally ill. He had presented several claims in this regard. Therefore, proceedings could not be initiated against him. Meanwhile, no hearing was held against the constable either because his identity could not be established and he could not be traced. Both convicts had previously been jailed Both retired police personnel had previously been jailed in this case. They were later granted bail by the High Court and the Supreme Court. After the court sentenced them, both were sent back to jail. The victim's lawyer alleged that the woman and her husband were subjected to continuous pressure during their struggle for justice. They were also accused of being assaulted and of attempts being made to cause an accident. Some cases have also been registered against the victim and her husband at Deoband police station, and are still pending trial.

stories.title: Fire breaks out at an RO shop in Gorakhpur:Triggering panic; electronic goods gutted, fire brigade brings blaze under control
stories.summary: A fire broke out at an RO shop in the Tiwari Pur police station area of Gorakhpur late on Friday night, causing panic. Nearby shopkeepers kept trying to douse the flames by throwing water with buckets. Police and fire brigade personnel arrived after receiving the information. After around 45 minutes of arduous efforts, the fire was brought under control. No one was killed in the incident. The electronic goods kept in the shop were reduced to ashes. The cause of the fire is being investigated. A sudden fire broke out at around 11 p.m. in the Shivanshi Enterprises (RO) shop in Suryavihar Colony. On receiving the information, Tiwari Pur police and the fire service reached the spot and brought the fire under control in time. At the time, people were shopping at the Dhanteras market at Suryavihar Crossing. As soon as the fire broke out, hundreds of people gathered along the roadside. The fire did not spread to the nearby shops or houses. The cause of the fire is being investigated. Swift action by the police and fire brigade prevented major damage.

stories.title: Swati Singh eyes 2027 election from Sarojini Nagar:Claims seeking BJP ticket is her right; party never explained why she was denied a ticket in 2022
stories.summary: Former BJP minister Swati Singh wants to contest the 2027 Assembly elections. Her first and only choice is the Sarojini Nagar seat in Lucknow. She had helped the BJP win this seat in 2017 after a gap of three decades. However, in 2022, the party denied her a ticket and fielded Rajeshwar Singh instead. Swati says she has still not been told why her ticket was cancelled. She received calls from then BJP national president JP Nadda and Dharmendra Pradhan. She was assured that she would be given a position in the organisation, keeping her above electoral politics. However, even after waiting for five years, that promise was not fulfilled. Swati said, "I have put forward my claim for the 2027 elections before the party forum. It is my right to seek a ticket from Sarojini Nagar." She spoke openly about her political struggle, her relationship with Dayashankar Singh and the functioning of the Yogi government. Here are the excerpts from the interview… Swati said, "I have started preparing for the elections. I have complete faith in the party." Question: Will Swati Singh contest the 2027 Assembly elections? Swati: I want to contest the elections from Sarojini Nagar once again. I have every right to do so, and I believe the party will understand this too. Question: You had won the Sarojini Nagar seat with a record margin. Why was your ticket cancelled in 2022? Swati: Even after so many years, I have not been able to understand why my ticket was cancelled. The party's top leadership can explain this better. Question: Did any senior party leader speak to you after your ticket was cancelled? Swati: At that time, I received calls from national president JP Nadda and Dharmendra Pradhan. The national president did tell me that they were looking at me beyond electoral politics. I was assured that I would be given a position somewhere in the organisation over the next five years. However, that promise was never fulfilled. Question: What happened after Dayashankar Singh's controversial statement in 2016 that made you come forward and protest? Swati: Dayashankar had made an objectionable statement about BSP chief Mayawati. BSP workers protested against it. Dayashankar is a politician, and they could have protested against him in any way they wanted. But my children were dragged into the controversy. Objectionable remarks were made about my daughter and the women in my family. That was when I had to come forward before the cameras. Question: A woman who was managing her home entered politics after this incident. She went on to become the state president of the women's wing, an MLA and then a minister. How has this journey been? Swati: I have taught at a university and also worked in the corporate sector. No woman can deny that she is capable of managing a home. The party made me the state president of its women's wing and later made me a minister after I won from Sarojini Nagar. I worked on several issues concerning women during my five-year tenure. Some tasks remained incomplete. Had I received a ticket in 2022, I would certainly have completed them. Question: The BJP has supported 33% reservation for women in politics. Will the party give women tickets on such a large scale in the UP elections? Swati: I believe it should. The Prime Minister repeatedly says that he gives credit for electoral victories to women, who make up half the population. When their participation is so positive, women should certainly be given more opportunities. Question: The state and national executive committees have been formed, but why was Swati not given a place? Swati: I feel very hurt about this. The party has not given me an opportunity anywhere. I even asked the national president to point out one mistake I had made. I have still not received an answer. Over these five years, the party sent me to campaign in five to seven states. Wherever I went, I was assigned very difficult seats, but I managed to win there too. I had hoped that I would be accommodated somewhere in the organisation later. Question: Were you not offered a ticket by any other party in 2022? Swati: I think we have left 2022 far behind. There is no point discussing it now. I hope the BJP gives me a ticket and fields me in the 2027 elections. Question: Rajeshwar Singh is currently the BJP MLA from Sarojini Nagar. Will you still stake your claim on this seat or seek another constituency? Swati: I am not such a senior leader that I can say, give me any seat in the state and I will win it. I want Sarojini Nagar because I worked there for five years. I know every lane, every party worker and the people of my constituency. Question: If the party offers you an organisational post instead of a ticket for the 2027 Assembly elections, what would you do? Swati: Decisions in the BJP are not taken by asking individuals. If the party decides that Swati should be given a ticket, it will certainly give me one. If it does not make that decision, I will not get a ticket. However, my wish is to contest from Sarojini Nagar. Question: What will be Swati's next step if the party does not give her a ticket? Swati: That is something only the future can tell. I do not know because we cannot see the future. Question: Have you met Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath recently? Did you discuss politics or personal matters? Swati: I met CM Yogi Adityanath just a few days ago. We discussed several things, both political and personal. Question: Did you express your wish to contest the elections before him? Swati: (Laughs) We discuss many things among ourselves. I do not think it is appropriate to share everything everywhere. Question: You have served as a minister and closely witnessed the government's first term. What difference do you see between its two terms? Swati: It is the same BJP government. Yogi Adityanath is leading it as Chief Minister. The government is functioning with the same strength and determination as it did during its first term. Question: Amit Shah and the national president recently attended the executive committee meeting. Did you meet them? Swati: I was not informed about the meeting. I feel that if no information was shared with me, perhaps I was not expected to attend. I could not understand why I was not informed, as sitting and former MLAs are usually notified. Question: Tell us about your struggle. Was your marriage to Dayashankar Singh arranged or a love marriage? Swati: Sometimes I feel that this question simply refuses to leave me alone. So many years have passed, but this question is always asked of Swati. Nobody ever asks Dayashankar Singh about it. Anyway, I have got used to it now. I hold an MBA and an LLM degree. My mother arranged my marriage with Dayashankar Singh. Well, marriage is a relationship between two people. It also brings two families together. Question: You got married and had two children. Then what went wrong? Why did you part ways? Swati: I think these are very old matters now. There is no point discussing them anymore. I have two very lovely children. Both are very intelligent and good at studies. They understand the value of family. I am happy in my own world. Question: You are both in the same party. Do you speak to each other when you meet at party meetings? Swati: We never speak. Even if we happen to meet occasionally, we do not talk. Question: Has Swati suffered politically because of dynastic politics? Swati: If you are talking about dynastic politics, I think this question should be put to people in the party. They can answer it better. Does dynastic politics apply only to Swati? Swati said, "I am a disciplined party worker. I will follow whatever instructions I receive." Question: Where did the BJP go wrong in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections in UP, where it won considerably fewer seats? Swati: I was assigned responsibility in Odisha during the Lok Sabha elections. Assembly elections were also held there at the same time, and the results were quite good. Whatever mistakes or shortcomings there may have been in UP during the Lok Sabha elections, I believe the senior leadership must have found ways to address them. Question: There was recently a Gen-Z protest, and now the Opposition is questioning the role of the Election Commission. What is your view? Swati: I believe Gen-Z should certainly ask questions if they have concerns. However, they should also be careful about the words they use. Everyone has the right to ask questions. My children are also part of Gen-Z. They ask many questions too. There should be dialogue. Question: You want to contest from Sarojini Nagar. Have you prepared any strategy to take on a strong SP-Congress alliance there? Swati: Whenever anyone sets out to do something, they work with a strategy. The same applies to elections. I have also thought about what I need to do and how I should move forward. Question: You are a woman and have also witnessed Mayawati's government in UP. How was her tenure? Swati: I have seen Mayawati ji's strong leadership abilities. As a woman, I can understand the challenges a woman has to face. Despite these challenges, she was a very strict Chief Minister. Question: Akhilesh Yadav talks about PDA. What is PDA, and how well have you understood it? Swati: Every political party has its own agenda. Akhilesh ji must have introduced this agenda with some positive ideas and is moving forward with it. Question: BJP's alliance partners are staking claims to each other's seats. How difficult will the 2027 elections be? Swati: You should put this question to the party organisation. Discussions must be taking place about how many seats the alliance partners will get and who will contest from where. I am not in a position to comment on this. Therefore, it would not be appropriate for me to answer this question.

stories.title: Mother in Prayagraj waits for husband as daughter returns:Both went missing 10 years ago; family had cremated daughter, believing her to be dead
stories.summary: My daughter did not go “missing”; she was kidnapped. Everyone had come to know that after receiving the body, we were going to lodge an FIR for murder. The very people who hatched the conspiracy had a phone call made from Vadodara informing us that our daughter was at a Nari Niketan there. Twenty-five-year-old Preeti's mother, Kamla Devi, gets choked up with emotion as she narrates the story of her daughter going missing for three years and then suddenly being found. Gathering her courage, she says, "Our daughter is mentally a bit weak, which is why she is unable to reveal much before the police, and that is the reason we are unable to get a case registered. Her father also went missing in the same way 10 years ago; we do not even have a single photograph of him to hand over to the police." Preeti went missing on 13th May 2023 from Lalgopalganj in Prayagraj. After nearly three and a half years, on 26th October 2026, she was found in Vadodara, Gujarat. While the family is overjoyed to get their daughter back, they are equally astonished. In fact, just 15 days before Preeti was found, on 4th October, the family had performed her last rites. They had even hosted a feast for 300 people on her Tehravin (13th-day mourning ritual). The counsellor at the Vadodara Nari Niketan, where Preeti had been staying for the last three years, mentioned that Preeti was brought to them on 5th August 2023—nearly 4 months after she went "missing" from home. Where was Preeti during this period? No one knows. Since Preeti is mentally weak, she too is unable to tell anything. The Dainik Bhaskar team tried to understand the entire matter from the family. Let us know everything step-by-step… First, the story of Preeti's marriage… ‘Daughter was married at the age of 22, went missing just 6 months later’ In the Lalgopalganj town, about 45 km away from Prayagraj district headquarters, there is a hamlet named Umraowganj. This is where Kamla Devi's two-room house is located. The family is so financially weak that they have not even been able to get the walls plastered, and there is no proper bedding inside. They manage to feed themselves twice a day solely on the government food rations they receive. Kamla Devi's family consists of three daughters and a son. Kamla Devi and her younger son somehow manage the household by working as daily wage labourers. The Dainik Bhaskar team found Kamla Devi and her daughter Preeti at their home. Kamla Devi says, "Preeti has been mentally a bit weak since childhood. We thought if we got our daughter married early, her mental condition might improve. On 4th November 2022, we married her into a family in Rajasthan. The groom used to work as a tailor. Preeti stayed at her in-laws' house for about a month and a half, and then we brought her back to Prayagraj after her farewell. She stayed here for about two months." Now, the story of Preeti going missing… Kamla Devi says, "One day we had gone out for manual labour. When we returned, Preeti was nowhere to be seen. We searched for her extensively. We inquired everywhere among relatives and acquaintances, but Preeti could nowhere be found. Her in-laws kept calling continuously to ask, but out of fear and shame, we could not reveal anything to them. When they put more pressure, we told them about her disappearance. The in-laws also searched for Preeti for a few days, and then forgot about her. We lodged a missing person complaint for our daughter at the Nawabganj police station. However, no trace could be found anywhere. We feel that the police did not carry out any investigation at all. One year passed since Preeti went missing, then two and three years went by as well. We were gradually beginning to forget her. We thought that she would never be found now. Then, after 3 years, on 30th September, we received a phone call from the Gorakhpur police. The police said that a girl's body had been found in the Gulriha area. Come and identify... check if it might be your daughter? Upon hearing this, I and my neighbour Santosh Kumar reached Gorakhpur. The corpse had a mole near the nose and burn marks on the body. Preeti also has the exact same marks. Therefore, we mistook it to be our daughter." Performed Preeti's last rites after identifying the wrong body Kamla's neighbour Santosh says, "That body was decomposed, but visually it appeared to be Preeti's. A long time had passed since Preeti went missing, so we could not figure out much. We brought the body home. On 4th October 2026, we performed her last rites. We also conducted the Tehravin. We felt that she had been murdered, so we wanted to lodge an FIR with the police, but before that, Preeti was found alive." Santosh explains that 15 days after performing the Tehravin, on 24th October, a phone call was received from Vadodara in Gujarat. The caller said, "I am speaking from the Women's Protection Centre. Preeti is with us. She was found by us in an unclaimed state on 5th August 2023." After listening to Santosh's statement, it became clear that Preeti is mentally not very strong in terms of thinking and understanding, which is why she kept wandering here and there between April 2023 and 5th August 2023. The Dainik Bhaskar team asked Preeti about these things, but she remained silent. We asked Preeti whether she did not remember home during all these days? Why did she stay away from her mother for so long? To this, Preeti says, “I had given a slip with a phone number to a sister there. She said she would make the call tomorrow. The next day when I reminded her, she replied that the slip was lost, and by then I did not remember the number myself.” ‘My daughter was kidnapped…’ Preeti's mother Kamla Devi calls this part of a major conspiracy. Expressing suspicion towards a few people, she says, "Preeti did not even use to step outside the house. I feel someone must have taken her away from here. After keeping her with them for a few days, they left her at the Nari Niketan. We were preparing to file a case, which is why they had a phone call made from Vadodara informing us that the girl is here. I suspect certain people, but when our own girl is unable to tell anything, what can we do?" After saying this much, Kamla Devi remains silent for a moment. We tried to speak to Preeti again. When asked how she reached there and who took her away, she goes silent. We asked her what she used to do there? Then Preeti says, "We were made to do cleaning work there. Sometimes they made us cut grass, and sometimes they had us water the trees. Whenever those people asked me about my home, I used to tell them Umraowganj and Lalganj. I did not know the name of my city." Nari Niketan authorities said—Preeti's home was not found on Google Maps The Bhaskar team contacted the Nari Niketan officials over the phone. Counsellor Preeti Pandey picked up the call. She stated that their team was continuously trying to trace Preeti's address. Based on Preeti's information, they had also searched for Lalganj on Google. However, it was appearing at multiple locations on the map. It was not clear which Lalganj Preeti's home was located in. Then one day Preeti mentioned Lalgopalganj, after which they started searching again. Eventually, they managed to trace her house address. Preeti's father has also been missing for 10 years, hasn't returned home yet Kamla Devi's husband Banwari Lal used to work in Indore, Madhya Pradesh. Earlier, he used to come home every six months or a year. In 2016, they married off their eldest daughter. After that, when he went to Indore, he never returned. Kamla says, "We searched for him a lot; the people who lived with him also kept looking for him, but nothing could be found out. When we went to the police, they asked us to bring his photo and details related to his identification card. Now, we neither have any photograph of his nor any identification card."

stories.title: Shami's ex-wife says 'God's wrath has struck him':Challenges him to contest elections; celebrates Diwali with their daughter
stories.summary: Cricketer Mohammad Shami's wife, Hasin Jahan, took a dig at his retirement from Test cricket. She said Mohammad Shami had not quit Test cricket; rather, God's wrath had befallen him. Speaking over the phone to Samvad News Agency, Hasin Jahan said, "Because of his good performances and the praise he received from fans, Shami had begun to consider himself God." She said a person's true identity was defined by their humanity, not by fame or playing cricket. Hasin Jahan reiterated her earlier stance regarding Shami's family. She said that if Mohammad Shami, his brother, sister-in-law or any other member of his family contested an election, she would also enter the electoral fray against them. She made it clear that she would not back down if any member of the family contested an election. Hasin Jahan celebrated Diwali with her daughter; see 4 pictures... Allegations raised over Shami's age Haseen Jahan claimed that Shami was born in 1982, while his educational certificates record his year of birth as 1990. She alleged that Shami continued to portray himself as younger for a long time because of an alleged discrepancy in the age mentioned on his certificates. However, these allegations have not been independently verified. Haseen questioned why, if Shami was younger, he did not play under-19 cricket and why he started playing cricket only after the age of 22. She also said that Shami was not given enough opportunities in the team despite his good performances. According to her, his age is affecting his career. Shami retired from Test cricket on 6 November Mohammed Shami announced his retirement from Test cricket on 6 November by sharing an emotional message on social media. He said he was bidding farewell to the white jersey, but the memories associated with it would always remain with him. He thanked his teammates, coaches, family, fans, the BCCI and the Cricket Association of Bengal. Shami made it clear that he would continue playing one-day and T20 cricket. Shami played 64 Tests for India and took 229 wickets. He made his Test debut against the West Indies in 2013. He also holds the record for taking five or more wickets in an innings on six occasions. Shami married Hasin Jahan in 2014 Shami and Hasin Jahan got married in 2014. Their daughter, Aira, was born on 17 July 2015. According to Hasin Jahan, Shami learnt after their daughter was born that his wife had been married before and had two children from her first marriage. In 2018, Hasin Jahan accused Shami and his family of domestic violence. Hasin divorced her first husband in 2010 Mohammed Shami is from Sahaspur Alinagar village in Uttar Pradesh's Amroha district. Haseen was a model by profession and had also worked as a cheerleader for the Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR). The two met during this period, and Shami decided to marry her. When Shami told his family about the relationship, they did not approve. Despite this, the two got married. This was Haseen Jahan's second marriage. In 2002, she had a love marriage with Saifuddin from Birbhum district. Saifuddin ran a stationery shop. Haseen has two daughters from her first marriage. Their relationship deteriorated in 2010, and they got divorced.

stories.title: Akhilesh says next election will pit women, youth against BJP:Condemns the ruckus at the Mahila Vandan programme in Ayodhya
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party national president Akhilesh Yadav has targeted the BJP over the alleged mistreatment of women during a party programme in Ayodhya. Describing it as a violent display of the so-called "Nari Vandan", he demanded that the National Commission for Women take cognisance of the matter and legal action be taken against the organisers. Akhilesh said that BJP workers do not respect women but insult them. The upcoming Assembly election will be a contest between women and youth on one side and the BJP on the other. In a post on X on Monday, Akhilesh said that people who had suffered, grieved and been humiliated due to the BJP's oppression would permanently wipe it out this time. He also referred to the alleged public humiliation by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath of the mother of a young man who lost his life in the Lucknow fire. He said no woman in the state would forget the incident. The curse of women never goes unanswered. The PDA government will provide mustard oil with rations Akhilesh also attacked the BJP government over the ration distribution system. He said that in a few months, they would form a PDA government in the state and provide mustard oil with the ration. This would ensure that no exploited, deprived or poor person would have to face a situation where they are beaten with sticks or humiliated by BJP workers. Akhilesh alleged that the poor and deprived were being harassed under BJP rule. He has demanded that Aadhaar cards be linked to voting, metal voter cards be issued and a biometric identification system be implemented. He claimed that this would prevent bogus voting. The balloon of the BJP's false promises has burst Referring to the 2024 Lok Sabha election and the recent 2026 Legislative Council election, the SP chief said the BJP's defeat in both elections had proved that the balloon of its false promises had burst among the people. Taking a dig at the party, he said the BJP was on a slippery slope and that the people were determined to defeat it permanently. Akhilesh claimed that politicians linked to the BJP were either quitting politics or seeking a place in other parties out of fear of public anger. He concluded his post by saying that the next election would be women and young people versus the BJP.

stories.title: Aligarh man beats cousin to death with an iron rod:He had come to celebrate Diwali; his younger brother welcomed a baby girl that morning
stories.summary: A 40-year-old man was beaten to death in Aligarh on Monday morning. His cousins attacked him with iron rods and lathis (sticks). In an attempt to save himself, the man ran into a neighbour's house, but the attackers pursued him there as well. They struck him on the head more than six times with an iron rod. He was taken to the hospital in critical condition, where doctors declared him dead on arrival. Following the incident, the accused locked their house and fled with their families. Just earlier that morning, a baby girl was born at the victim's younger brother's home, and the family was celebrating. Now, the entire family is engulfed in mourning. The deceased has been identified as Somveer alias Sonu (40), a resident of Bhupal Nagla village. He worked as an electrician and lived in Delhi with his wife Sadhna, two daughters Diksha (11) and Pariksha (9), and son Golu (8). He had returned to the village on Diwali night. The incident took place around 9:30 AM. Entered a Neighbor's House, but Could Not Escape According to family members, Somveer was repairing a faulty submersible pump at home. He stepped outside to fetch some supplies when Arjun, Praveen, and Arjun's son Anuj, who were allegedly lying in wait near the house, confronted him. It is alleged that the three surrounded him and attacked him with lathis and an iron pipe. To escape the attackers, Somveer ran toward his neighbor Nagendra Singh's house, about 20 meters away, and went inside. However, the attackers pursued him. They cornered him and dealt multiple blows to his head with the iron pipe. Suffering severe injuries, he collapsed. Hearing the commotion, his father Reshampal Singh and other relatives rushed to the spot. The attackers then fled while issuing threats. The houses of both families are located adjacent to each other. Referred from CHC to District Hospital; Doctors Declare Him Dead The family rushed Somveer to the Community Health Center (CHC) by ambulance. As his condition was critical, he was referred to the District Hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Upon receiving the information, ASP/CO Gabhana Srishti Jain, local police, and a forensic team reached the scene. The team inspected the site and gathered evidence. Police have deployed teams to trace and arrest the accused. Dispute Started 1.5 Months Ago Over Field Irrigation Water According to the family, the motive behind the murder stems from an old dispute over irrigation water overflowing into fields. On September 16, water from the field belonging to Somveer's uncle Bhanwarpal Singh overflowed into the field of Arjun, son of his elder uncle Vijendra Singh. Over this issue, Arjun and his son Anuj went to Reshampal Singh's home, abused the family, and assaulted them. Somveer's brothers Deepak and Dheeraj were injured in that clash. A case regarding that incident was registered on October 8 based on Deepak's complaint. Police had also initiated breach of peace proceedings against the accused. Family members stated that Arjun was shouting abuses again on Sunday night. The police were informed, but the matter was temporarily defused at the time. Daughter Born to Younger Brother; Elder Brother Killed Hours Later Somveer was the eldest of three brothers. On Monday morning, a baby girl was born to his younger brother Dheeraj. The family was filled with joy over the newborn's arrival, but just hours later, news of Somveer's murder turned their celebration into grief. His mother Gudiya, wife Sadhna, and three children are devastated. Following the crime, the accused party locked their house and absconded. Police remain on high alert given the tension in the village. ASP/CO Gabhana Srishti Jain is monitoring the investigation. Police are awaiting a formal complaint from the family, and the body has been sent for post-mortem.
