stories.summary: India has achieved a remarkable decrease in extreme poverty, yet challenges persist in specific regions and demographics. The World Bank notes that major poverty concentration exists in some states in North and East India. About 57% of India’s poor live in a contiguous belt stretching from Uttar Pradesh to West Bengal, according to the World Bank’s October 2026 Poverty & Equity Brief.

stories.title: 'Silent on hate crimes against Indians': MEA tears into US agency over religious freedom report
'This is not UCC, but Hindu Civil Code': Owaisi targets Maharashtra govt, says move seeks to 'snatch' Muslims' identity
'Our ties enjoy bipartisan support': India's first reaction to US midterm results
Digital arrest scams: SC seeks prevention plan from WhatsApp & others, sends notice to RBI
'Unfortunate': Govt condemns anti-India campaign by Chinese vloggers, urges Bangladesh to take action
Do boond zindagi ki: India hits immunisation milestones, but why are millions still missing their shots?
stories.summary: India's vigorous vaccination campaigns have made remarkable strides in eliminating diseases such as smallpox and polio. Yet, disparities still exist in immunization coverage between various states and communities. Current initiatives aim to enhance accessibility and monitoring of vaccinations, especially addressing caregiver hesitancy and obstacles encountered by migrants. Raising awareness and consistent follow-up will be vital in boosting vaccination rates in the future.

stories.title: 'No, I won't let our baby be thrown into river': Sonia recalls loss of first child before Rahul
‘No order required’: Delhi HC on Central Secretariat Club’s plea against de-recognition after Centre rules out fresh allotment
Clinton's 'old habit', 'arrogant' Sarkozy & 'real star' Diana: Sonia's candid accounts of world leaders
'Next target is to finish Dimagi Naxals': Kiren Rijiju slams Rahul Gandhi for attacking PM Modi
'No real contact with him': Sonia Gandhi recalls face-to-face meetings with PM Modi in memoir
stories.summary: Sonia Gandhi reveals in her memoir that she has had minimal contact with PM Narendra Modi. Their encounters are restricted to formal greetings at political gatherings, often avoiding eye contact. Gandhi contrasts her vision of an inclusive India with Modi's more exclusionary ideology shaped by the RSS. She also revisits the violence of the 2002 Gujarat riots during Modi's tenure as chief minister.

stories.title: Oklahoma family turns 1903 ancestral ranch into wildlife haven, rotating 600 cow-calf pairs across 25 paddocks
stories.summary: A ranch in Oklahoma has been awarded for its sustainable management practices that support both cattle and wildlife. It implements rotational grazing across 25 paddocks to protect native grasslands and improve ecosystem health. The management system is designed to promote water conservation and soil retention properties. Wildlife species, including deer and various birds, benefit from the preserved habitat.

stories.title: 'Should've called it Whitewashing, not Belonging': BJP mocks Sonia Gandhi's memoir
stories.summary: BJP spokesperson CR Kesavan criticized Sonia Gandhi's memoir, arguing it attempts to whitewash the historical mistakes of the Congress party. He highlighted her emotional responses to key incidents while questioning her silence on the 1984 anti-Sikh riots and other tragedies. The memoir details Sonia's childhood, her marriage to Rajiv Gandhi, and her experiences as part of the Gandhi family.

stories.title: Fake GoFundMe raises $17,750 after deadly DC plane crash, then gets exposed
Netanyahu's daily calls to Trump over Iran war spark pushback within White House: Report
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has reportedly been urging President Donald Trump daily to resume military action against Iran. This comes as several Arab and Muslim leaders have advised Trump to pursue diplomatic avenues rather than escalate the conflict. Amid these discussions, Trump has indicated that further military intervention is not currently necessary. Iran has threatened to retaliate against any fresh US attacks, raising regional concerns.

stories.title: Hidden Gold Spurs Ownership Probe: Belgian workers uncover €9mn stash; legal claims may take years
stories.summary: Eighteen-year-old Kobe stumbled upon a staggering €9 million in gold while performing drainage work in Belgium, finding the treasure ingeniously concealed behind a wall in a previously operational brewery. After alerting the property owner and law enforcement, an investigation commenced to unveil the treasure's history. With multiple stakeholders, including the current property owner and potential heirs to its original proprietor, the legal battle over ownership could drag on for years.

stories.title: 'Managing hashtags and state are different': BJP takes swipe at Vijay over alleged fund theft in Tamil Nadu
DIAL rains for relief: Choked Delhi to see another cloud seeding attempt
stories.summary: India’s capital, New Delhi, will attempt cloud seeding to induce rain and address severe pollution. The initiative involves Delhi International Airport Ltd, the Delhi government, and IIT Kanpur. A specialized aircraft from Kyathi Climate will undertake the operation on Tuesday and Wednesday. A fresh western disturbance is expected to bring rain to northwestern India later this week. Cloud seeding aims to enhance precipitation as the air quality deteriorates.

stories.title: Missouri county drops land sale bid near golf course after protests
stories.summary: Jackson County in Missouri cancelled its request for bids on public land along the Blue River Parkway on November 9 after residents and conservation groups protested the proposed sale. The land has more than eight miles of volunteer-built trails used for hiking and mountain biking. Residents have called for stronger legal protection against future development.

stories.title: 'Warrants urgent attention': SC flags vehicular pollution in Delhi-NCR, seeks action plan
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has mandated that Delhi and three adjacent states intensify measures to combat vehicle emissions. Officials are tasked with reporting on the implementation of laws governing aging and non-compliant vehicles. With rising pollution levels in the National Capital Region, the court emphasized the need for inter-state collaboration on vehicle management and stricter adherence to emission standards. The matter will be reviewed again on November 23.

stories.title: Over 2,000 teachers, students face political persecution in Bangladesh: Report
stories.summary: Since August 2024, over 2,000 students and teachers have reportedly faced politically motivated persecution across Bangladesh. The persecution includes academic exclusion, physical attacks, and criminal proceedings targeting individuals linked to the Bangladesh Awami League. Numerous teachers have experienced exclusion from professional activities, physical assaults, and legal issues. JusticeMakers Bangladesh has called for independent investigations into these reported abuses.

stories.title: Russia's last major independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta shuts down after 33 years
stories.summary: Novaya Gazeta, an independent newspaper critical of the Kremlin, has shut down its Moscow office after three decades. The closure came as a result of mounting government pressure and sustained restrictions on independent media. Journalists mourned the loss of their office while recalling the legacy of their investigative work. Some staff members have relocated abroad and continue reporting under a new publication called Novaya Gazeta Europe.

stories.title: Business drainage changes flood neighbour's home; court cuts damages to $102,000
stories.summary: A Michigan business's drainage changes sent excess rainwater onto a neighbouring property, causing years of flooding and damage to the house and garage. An appeals court revised the homeowner's $170,000 award to $102,000, while upholding $50,000 in emotional distress damages under the nuisance claim.

stories.title: California teens collect 22,000 sports balls in 24 hours for recycling
Rubio warned Trump about Nvidia CEO's Chinese 'spy' affair months ago. Did he ignore it?
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump expressed confidence in Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang regarding allegations of ties to a Chinese spy. Trump stated he believes Huang was unaware of the alleged spy's identity during an FBI investigation. Rubio's memo on Huang's relationships surfaced before Trump's visit to Beijing, indicating prior knowledge of the situation. The FBI is scrutinizing the implications on national security concerning Nvidia's technology and partnerships.

stories.title: 'I'd quake in my seat': Sonia Gandhi recalls Indira Gandhi's temper, early days as bride in memoir
stories.summary: Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, offers an intimate account of Indira Gandhi’s temper, recalling how staff were made to stand in corners, a senior Congress leader ordered to face a wall and others ignored for days. Sonia also describes Rajiv’s reassurance during her mother-in-law’s outbursts, Indira’s domestic routines, love for sarees and photographs, and how grandchildren gradually softened her temperament.

stories.title: Charity shop worker wins £600,000 inheritance battle after murder accusation
After 30 historic wall stones were stolen, UK councillor hid an AirTag in one; police tracked the thief
stories.summary: Determined to protect an ancient wall from persistent thefts, an English mayor cleverly employed an Apple AirTag embedded in one of the coping stones. This initiative ultimately directed police to a thief in Wigan, who confessed to the charges. The recovered stones, estimated at £7,000, have revitalized community spirit, allowing local residents to rally together and restore this historic structure.

stories.title: Idris Elba backs £500,000 UK creative careers programme for 400 youths
High Pollution Alert Issued: Sadiq Khan warns of very high PM2.5; experts seek burn alerts
stories.summary: London Mayor Sadiq Khan issued a high air pollution alert for the capital urging residents to take precautions. Vulnerable groups were particularly advised to minimize their exposure to polluted air, following high pollution levels. Government monitoring indicated that numerous locations exceeded healthy particulate matter levels due to weather conditions and celebrations. Experts suggested that domestic burning and transportation significantly contribute to air quality issues.

stories.title: After 800 years with one family, 9,500-acre UK estate bought for wildlife with 25,000 donors' help
stories.summary: The Rothbury Estate in Northumberland has successfully been bought for nature conservation, thanks to the generous contributions of over 25,000 supporters from across 50 countries, amassing nearly £30 million. The Wildlife Trusts and Northumberland Wildlife Trust will oversee restoration efforts, plan a nature corridor, and engage with local farmers to align conservation with farming. This purchase heralds a fresh chapter of conservation initiatives and community involvement.

stories.title: US evacuates aircraft from UK air base after Iran threat: Report
What made Sonia Gandhi turn down PM post after UPA’s 2004 victory? Memoir revisits moment
stories.summary: Sonia Gandhi reveals her thoughts in her memoir about declining the prime minister role after the UPA's victory. She describes her inner voice guiding her decision and her conversation with Rahul. Gandhi highlights why she chose Manmohan Singh for the position, noting his integrity and governance experience. Her memoir also covers her personal journey, including significant tragedies and cultural adjustments after moving to India.

stories.title: Atacama Desert: Where ancient life reveals the secrets of our planet’s beginnings
stories.summary: In the unforgiving Atacama Desert, ancient stromatolites stand as a testament to early life on Earth and how microbes can adapt to extreme conditions. Researchers are exploring the resilience of microorganisms in this arid environment, revealing insights that might help us understand the possibilities of life on Mars. These findings emphasize how organisms can not only survive but thrive in harsh settings, raising intriguing questions about extraterrestrial existence.

stories.title: Turning trash into treasure with oyster recycling: Alabama's oyster shell recycling program supports local fisheries and habitats
stories.summary: Since 2016, Alabama’s oyster shell recycling program has successfully collected over 31 million shells, contributing to the restoration of an impressive 120.1 acres of oyster habitats in coastal waters. Local restaurants play a key role by properly disposing of their used shells. This initiative not only bolsters marine life and local fisheries but also encourages student involvement in learning about oyster ecology and its vital impact on the ecosystem.

stories.title: Iran war, cost of living drag Trump’s approval rating near career low: Survey
stories.summary: Donald Trump's approval rating stands at 32 per cent, close to his lowest in recent years. Concerns about the cost of living have significantly affected his standing among voters. The Republican Party experienced losses in both chambers of Congress during the midterm elections. Trump has taken action to address immigration, which resonates more positively with his supporters compared to his economic policies.

stories.title: Charlie Kirk murder trial set for June 2028 as judge rejects defence's push for 2029
stories.summary: Tyler Robinson, implicated in the assassination of Charlie Kirk, will begin trial in June 2028. The judge aimed to balance the interests of both the defense and Kirk's widow, Erika Kirk. Prosecutors originally sought an earlier trial start, highlighting the family's desire for swift justice. Robinson's lawyers are preparing a substantial defense, examining extensive evidence and potentially seeking a change of venue.

stories.title: India, US plan joint crackdown on transnational drug cartels, synthetic drug trade
stories.summary: Top security officials from India and the US gathered in New Delhi to address narcotics syndicates. The discussions focused on establishing a framework to combat synthetic drug flows and secure supply chains. NCB Director General Anurag Garg emphasized a network-centric enforcement model to target cartels and facilitators. Both nations endorsed operational milestones, including initiatives to prevent the diversion of synthetic drug precursors.

stories.title: Three workers killed during water tank maintenance at Tata iPhone parts factory in Tamil Nadu
Hasina seeks passport, Dhaka calls it political stunt & seeks extradition
stories.summary: Ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has requested a new passport from the Bangladesh High Commission. The request aims to facilitate her planned return to Bangladesh after two years in exile. Bangladesh authorities have labeled the request a political stunt and emphasized her extradition due to criminal convictions. Indian officials have stated that the extradition matter should be handled through existing legal processes.

stories.title: 'Global capital for Sanatan pilgrimage': Akhilesh's big Ayodhya promise ahead of 2027 UP polls
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav has articulated a bold vision to elevate Ayodhya as the ultimate hub for Sanatan pilgrimage on a global scale. He stressed the importance of honest temple management and top-notch infrastructure to rejuvenate devotees' trust. Additionally, Yadav has committed to tackling local economic challenges and safeguarding the interests of traditional boatmen.

stories.title: ‘Locked and loaded’: Donald Trump warns Iran as Tehran demands US ‘surrender’
Robbie Williams gives his $40 million Florida mansion a rock-star makeover
Paris Hilton's former Beverly Park home seeks $159,000 a month in rent
Defamation Case Moves Ahead: Kai Cenat says lawsuit enters new phase; McDonald’s livestream clash revives RaKai claims
stories.summary: Kai Cenat has confirmed that his defamation lawsuit against former friend Reggie is moving forward after a McDonald's employee confronted him over allegations involving streamer RaKai. The unexpected exchange happened during his GTA streaming marathon. Kai revealed that his legal team had completed the first stage of the case and was preparing for the next, while expressing frustration over facing the accusations in everyday situations.

stories.title: Massachusetts neighbours ordered to pay $3.7 million after 18-year dispute over oceanfront home construction
stories.summary: Margaret Reichenbach and her husband encountered relentless challenges from their neighbors throughout their home construction project in Massachusetts. After a prolonged legal struggle, they secured a $3.7 million verdict for damages. The Massachusetts Appeals Court affirmed the ruling, citing ample evidence of harassment and intrusion. The Reichenbachs' victory also includes a permanent injunction against further neighbor harassment, finally allowing them peace in their home.

stories.title: Rufus Wainwright lists his $2.3 million Spanish-style Laurel Canyon cottage
Princess Diana's private cottage preserved as her former retreat goes on sale
Ahead of peace talks, Zelenskyy seeks PM Modi's help on ceasefire
stories.summary: Asks For More Steps On Food, Energy Security

stories.title: Paul McCartney's Scottish farm inspired Mull of Kintyre after Beatlemania
Fearing winter polls, Ladakh political parties, social bodies plan protests
Massachusetts neighbours lose appeal over $3.7 million verdict for disrupting couple's home construction
stories.summary: In the divorce proceedings between Vernon and Nichole McIntosh, the court mandated a substantial division of assets following Vernon's misappropriation of funds. Nichole is awarded 55 percent of the marital estate, amounting to over $138,000. The trial established that Vernon hid and mismanaged marital assets during the divorce. Properties purchased during their marriage will be sold, with net proceeds evenly distributed. Vernon must also cover Nichole's attorney fees.

Chinese nationals stream from poor localities of Dhaka, claim those are in Delhi: Report
SC: Govt has wide powers to compulsorily retire staffer, improve efficiency

stories.title: Texas appeals court overturns tenant's $250,000 award over defective legal notice to landlord
stories.summary: A Texas appeals court has overturned a significant $250,000 default judgment that was previously granted to a tenant due to flaws in the service documentation. Lavender Apartments LLC contested the validity of the delivery records, claiming they did not adhere to Texas legal standards. As the court found the required service was inadequately demonstrated, the case will go back for additional litigation and examination in the trial court.

stories.title: Alice Huang boasted about Nvidia AI chip access to investors, told them Alibaba would be a client for the project
Utah court backs family's claim to disputed farmland after 1965 fence outweighs neighbour's survey
stories.summary: A Utah family successfully upheld its legal rights to a disputed piece of farmland after a court ruling. The Christiansen Family Trust contested boundary claims made by Haas Land & Livestock, which purchased neighboring property. The property dispute centered around a fence built in 1965 that marked the boundary. The Utah Court of Appeals affirmed earlier decisions favoring the Christiansens' long-accepted boundary.

stories.title: Now, Cong-led Keralam govt follows Karnataka on 'ethanol test'
stories.summary: Those Creating Controversies For Political Purposes Will Have To Face Consequences: Union Minister

stories.title: Adult vaccination remains low; elderly miss cover against flu and shingles
Lawyers' boycott makes man stay in jail despite bail
Prince Harry exits BetterUp chief role after 5 years on $1 million salary, takes senior adviser post
stories.summary: Prince Harry has stepped down as chief impact officer at BetterUp after five years, moving into a senior adviser role at the US-based mental health and coaching company. The Duke of Sussex reportedly earned $1 million annually during his tenure. The development comes weeks after his return to the UK with Meghan Markle and their children, drawing attention to his professional plans.

stories.title: JD Vance says a lot of infighting, reshuffling going on, people asking if No 2 has what it takes to lead. Then he clarifies he is talking about Ohio State Buckeyes
Ohio residents push data center ban as $5bn Amazon project faces November 10 hearing
stories.summary: Residents in Butler County are rallying against the proposed Amazon data center, voicing worries over possible water shortages, noise pollution, and pollution from backup generators. Local zoning authorities have suggested prohibiting data centers in St. Clair Township, where this project is slated to occur. A crucial public hearing is set to address these issues alongside zoning matters. Recent trends show rising voter favor for restrictions on similar undertakings across Ohio.

stories.title: Diwali is 'Eid of joy', says Kharge; Congress insulting Sanatan culture: BJP
US court rejects malpractice claim over lawyer's missed deadline to correct $100,000 divorce debt error
stories.summary: In a recent ruling, an Arizona appeals court upheld a decision to dismiss a woman's malpractice claim against her ex-attorney. The court concluded she suffered no direct financial loss from the attorney's missed deadline, despite a $200,000 error in the divorce decree regarding familial debt. It was established that the obligation to pay the debt remained unchanged and fully enforceable.

stories.title: 19 runners hospitalized after 'unusual symptoms' at California half-marathon; heat exhaustion might be a reason as Santa Barbara temperatures reached 86 degree Fahrenheit
Unions dismiss France's 24-euro minimum wage increase
Oregon couple in their 70s win over $8 million after firms foreclose on home they still lived in
stories.summary: An Oregon couple in their 70s have been awarded more than $8 million after a jury found companies liable for unlawfully foreclosing on their home while they were still living in it. The Salem couple had also been denied more than $175,000 left over from the foreclosure sale, which took place in 2022. The jury found that the companies had carried out unlawful trade practices and financially abused the elderly homeowners.

stories.title: Meet Leo Toake, 16, who turned potato peels into weedkiller and restored 15 acres in New Jersey
stories.summary: At just 16 years old, Leo Toake from New Jersey is on a mission to create a revolutionary herbicide sourced from food scraps. Through his nonprofit, Re:Imagine Inc., he's mobilized over 70 volunteers for habitat restoration and invasive species removal. Early trials of Toake's S.A.F.E. clearly show an 82.5% effectiveness against Japanese stilt grass, all while repurposing over 500 pounds of food waste and contributing to a cleaner environment.

stories.title: Kublai Khan’s warship sank in 1281; 745 years later, dice reveal how its crew spent breaks
stories.summary: Archaeologists recently found gaming pieces and dice from a Mongol invasion shipwreck near Takashima Island. These discoveries suggest that sailors engaged in leisure activities during voyages. The ship may measure around 30 metres, potentially the largest of three identified wrecks. Other artefacts discovered nearby include food containers and tools indicative of daily life aboard the ship.

stories.title: Bihar govt bans firecrackers, private boat operations near ghats ahead of Chhath Puja
Delhi Police issues notice to Mamata Banerjee as witness in 2013 protest case
Residents raise $30,000 to bring first grocery store to Alabama neighbourhood in 70 years
stories.summary: After nearly 70 years without a grocery store, Birmingham's Fountain Heights neighbourhood has opened the We All Eat Market. Developed by a local farming cooperative, the $1 million project received $30,000 in grassroots contributions and $150,000 from the city. The market will sell locally grown food, support small farmers and offer discounts to eligible customers.

stories.title: Mona Vale beachfront home fetches record $29 million
stories.summary: A Mona Vale beachfront house recently set a new record by selling for A$29 million in a private sale. The property was previously owned by McDonald's Australia's chief executive and sold for A$7.65 million in 2014. The sale was conducted discreetly without public marketing, ensuring privacy for the owners. The previous record for Mona Vale was A$13.5 million, established in October 2025.

stories.title: 'Anybody believe this was honest?' Trump revives fraud claims after midterm results
Norway’s largest Viking hoard yields rare King Olaf coin not found in country since 1924
stories.summary: A rare coin minted during King Olaf Haraldsson's reign around 1025 has been identified in Norway's Morstad Viking hoard. It is only the second coin of this type found in Norway, the previous one dating back to 1924. The coin also offers clues about the king's use of Christian symbols and its circulation in commercial transactions.

stories.title: Kentucky court keeps father 500 feet from home despite sole ownership claim after wife's death
stories.summary: A Kentucky court has upheld a key decision safeguarding the welfare of two boys by ruling against their father's attempt to rescind protective orders. Although he is the property owner, the court has ordered him to maintain a 500-foot separation from his home. This ruling, following the untimely death of the boys' mother in 2025, emphasizes the priority given to their security over the father's interests.

stories.title: Amateur prospector finds 1.2-kg gold nugget worth A$150,000 in Australia
stories.summary: In a remarkable discovery, a hobbyist prospector unearthed a significant gold nugget weighing 1,218 grams in New South Wales. With approximately 940 grams of pure gold, its value is estimated between A$150,000 and A$200,000. The Tibooburra area continues to draw gold seekers and tourists, with this nugget serving as a testament to the dedication and perseverance required in the thrilling quest for gold.

stories.title: $180,000 Bitcoin, Pokemon cards feature in North Carolina divorce appeal
stories.summary: A North Carolina appeals court upheld a divorce court's valuation of three Bitcoin at $180,000, Pokemon cards at $1,800 and its unequal division of marital assets. However, it overturned a $15,261.40 attorney’s fee award and an order requiring the husband to pay the entire forensic accountant’s bill, citing missing findings needed to establish the reasonableness of the fees.

stories.title: 'Scrap Rs 500 notes': CM Naidu seeks to phase out big currency to curb corruption
stories.summary: Andhra Pradesh chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu advocates for the abolition of Rs 500 and other high-value banknotes to combat corruption and promote a shift to digital transactions, which he believes is vital for economic enhancement. The recent local election results revealed a strong tilt toward the National Democratic Alliance, especially in urban regions, indicating a robust affirmation of democratic ideals and effective governance across Andhra Pradesh.

stories.title: ‘There is only the United States of America’: Erika Kirk slams Abdul El-Sayed’s ‘Arab America’ remark after historic Senate win
Canada has protected more than 81,400 hectares of Ontario taiga forest and peatlands
stories.summary: A significant investment of $64 million is underway to safeguard over 81,400 hectares of taiga forests and peatlands in Ontario. This project focuses on preserving habitats for wildlife, including vulnerable species such as the red-headed woodpecker and the bobolink. It represents Canada's commitment to conserving 30 percent of its lands and waters by 2030 through a collaborative effort involving various organizations, government entities, and private donors.

stories.title: Russell Brand sentenced to 10-and-a-half years in prison for rape and sexual assault
'There is an old saying': BJP MLA Papiya Adhikari explains her 'firecrackers cure illness' remark, apologises
Idaho reconnected 8 acres of floodplain and built 2,000 feet of side channels
stories.summary: Warm Springs Preserve in Ketchum is currently undergoing significant habitat restoration, aimed at reviving local ecosystems. The initiative includes reconnecting floodplains and building new channels to support aquatic species. An enhanced irrigation system is projected to conserve roughly 50 million gallons of water annually. Furthermore, the project will introduce accessible trails and improved public facilities for the community, marking a commendable step towards better environmental management and habitat preservation.

stories.title: After surveys found only dead oil beetles in 2022 and 2025, volunteers discovered larvae
stories.summary: Exciting news from Pembrokeshire, Wales: conservationists have unearthed short necked oil beetle larvae, a positive sign of the species' reproduction in its sole habitat in the country. Surveys just a year ago had only identified deceased adults. Thanks to the Bumblebee Conservation Trust's diligent monitoring, efforts are in place to safeguard this beetle's ecosystem, emphasizing the vital need to protect its environment for lasting survival.

stories.title: North Carolina court backs review process after father demands $3,000 for children's overseas trips
stories.summary: In a significant ruling, a North Carolina Court determined that a parenting coordinator has the authority to dictate travel regulations for divorced parents. This case highlighted conflicts regarding international trips with minors, driven by one parent's financial motivations rather than genuine safety worries. The decision underscores the importance of prioritizing children's welfare in travel arrangements, clarifying parental rights during custody disagreements in North Carolina.

stories.title: Arpita Singh, celebrated artist who painted real women, dies at 89
Harrison Ford and Calista Flockhart to Receive First Joint Philanthropy Award
Meet Indian-origin Anjali Sud, the new CEO of SiriusXM, succeeding Jennifer Witz
320 acres around 200-year-old North Carolina iron mine bought to protect five bat species
stories.summary: A former iron mine in North Carolina, which operated from the 1820s to the 1930s, now provides a winter shelter for five bat species, including rare and endangered ones. The Southern Appalachian Highlands Conservancy has purchased 320 acres around the historic mine to protect its underground tunnels, recovering forest and wildlife habitat. The move strengthens earlier conservation efforts to safeguard bats from habitat disturbance and white-nose syndrome, a deadly fungal disease.

stories.title: PM Modi speaks with Zelenskyy, discusses efforts for Russia-Ukraine peace deal
'I warned you before too': Kejriwal takes swipe at Yogi over SIR, congratulates Akhilesh in advance
'Why spend on R&D?' Rajeev Chandrasekhar mocks China's 'easier way' over Nvidia spy claim
stories.summary: Rajeev Chandrasekhar highlighted the recent honeytrapping allegations against Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang involving China. He criticised China's ethical standards in technology acquisition and alleged espionage practices. China responded by denying these allegations and labeling them as baseless. An independent investigation has been launched by Nvidia's board regarding the claims. Huang has also admitted to personal issues but maintains no national security breaches occurred.

stories.title: Evening newswrap: Nvidia boss in Chinese spy scandal; Delhi's AQI turns severe; Iran's hidden oil network in China, and more
Gang posing as Army suppliers dupe Assam firm of Rs 11.5 crore, key accused held in Bengal
BJP's third-term bid, Congress's comeback hopes: What will decide Uttarakhand elections 2027?
Manipur census on hold till April 2027 as high court seeks answers from the Centre
stories.summary: The Manipur high court has ordered the postponement of the Census 2027 until late April 2027. This ruling aims to address significant concerns regarding how recent ethnic violence and subsequent displacements might skew population counts. The court requested the Census Commissioner to review seven representations. Following the authorities' decision, a further four-week delay will apply, allowing anyone unhappy with the outcome to seek legal recourse.

stories.title: Karnataka, Keralam governments launch E20 petrol quality checks amid ethanol blending concerns
stories.summary: The Keralam civil supplies department conducted inspections of petrol pumps in Kochi to examine the ethanol mix in E20 petrol. Officials took six samples, forwarding two for lab tests in Kakinada. Rising concerns over high ethanol blending have been highlighted by Karnataka Minister Rizwan Arshad. However, the union ministry of petroleum claims all samples adhere to quality norms, disputing allegations of excessive mixing.

stories.title: India, Lebanon hold first Foreign Office consultations; discuss trade, investment, digital cooperation
stories.summary: India and Lebanon embarked on their first-ever Foreign Office Consultations in New Delhi, aiming to strengthen their bilateral relationship. Important topics of discussion included cooperation in political-security, economic, and socio-cultural arenas. Ambassador Sripriya Ranganathan's visit to Lebanon set the stage for deeper ties, as key areas like trade, investment, digital infrastructure, and pharmaceuticals were reviewed, along with pressing regional and international matters.

stories.title: 'He called us Naxals': Rahul Gandhi hits back at PM Modi, renews debate challenge
'Semantically ignorant': Congress defends Kharge's 'Diwali a khushiyon ki Eid' remark
stories.summary: Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge stirred controversy by referring to Diwali as 'khushiyon ka Eid'. BJP officials accused the Congress of misrepresenting Diwali, asserting each festival has its unique identity. Pawan Khera of Congress defended Kharge's statement, emphasizing the meaning of 'Eid' as 'festival.' The BJP responded by questioning the appropriateness of comparing Diwali with Eid, which they deemed disrespectful. This disagreement highlights ongoing political tensions regarding religious and cultural identities.

stories.title: Delhi pollution sparks row: BJP alleges 'conspiracy'; AAP and Congress question AQI data
Jaishankar extends national day greetings to Cambodia, hails strong civilisational ties
stories.summary: S Jaishankar conveyed warm National Day wishes to Cambodia, celebrating the deep-rooted civilizational connections between the two countries. He praised the successful conclusion of the recent Cambodia-India Bilateral Army Exercise, CINBAX-II, which focused on collaborative training to bolster operational synergy among their armed forces. The exercise allowed both teams to display their professionalism and exchange valuable operational insights, further solidifying the defense partnership between India and Cambodia.

stories.title: Wisconsin family manages 500-acre forest for wildlife and timber; shortlisted for state conservation award
stories.summary: Jesse and Kylie Sebero are managing over 500 acres of forest in Marinette County, Wisconsin. They focus on timber production while ensuring ecological balance and wildlife conservation. The couple also opens their land for educational tours, helping others learn about forest management. They have been nominated for the 2026 Wisconsin Leopold Conservation Award for their significant contributions. The award will be announced during an upcoming meeting on November 12.

stories.title: South Carolina woman protects 146-acre family land after promise to mother
stories.summary: Alice Smith has placed her family's 146-acre property in South Carolina under a conservation easement, fulfilling a promise to her mother. Her grandparents bought the land in the 1940s. Along with another family, she has permanently restricted development on more than 250 acres through Upstate Forever.

stories.title: South Carolina father arrested after leaving 6-year-old alone for Pokemon cards
Princess Margaret's wedding gift: Mustique villa now rents for $50,000 a week
'True colours exposed': BJP's Giriraj Singh tears into Kharge over Diwali 'khushiyon ka Eid' remark
‘We’re losing a hell of a lot’: Cessna carrying 5 men vanished over Australia in 1981; 45 years later, no trace found
stories.summary: In August of 1981, a Cessna aircraft disappeared in Australia's Barrington Tops, carrying five men. Despite numerous searches and thorough investigations, both the plane and its passengers were never discovered. Reports indicated that severe turbulence and ice accumulation likely played a role in the incident. The mystery remains captivating for amateur sleuths and volunteers, while the families of the missing continue their quest for answers about their loved ones' fate.

stories.title: Louisiana court upholds a trust protector's powers to change beneficiaries and approve early closure
stories.summary: A Louisiana appeals court upheld a trust protector's authority to change future beneficiaries and require approval before a trust could be ended early. The case involved a trust created by a stepfather for his stepson in 2004. The stepson challenged the powers given to his stepbrother, but the court upheld the lower court's decision.

Vance lances Trump as MAGA enters week of the long knives
3 injured in shooting at US post office in Iowa, suspect detained
Arkansas man loses challenge to sale of ex-wife's share of their jointly owned land
stories.summary: A couple bought land together in Arkansas in 2021 but divorced within a year, retaining equal ownership. After the woman filed for bankruptcy in 2023, a trustee sold her share to an investment company. Her former husband challenged the sale, but the US Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit dismissed his appeal because he had not challenged the buyer's good faith before the bankruptcy court.

stories.title: Kim Kardashian’s former mansion, where Kris Humphries proposed, listed for $8.5 million after makeover
stories.summary: Kim Kardashian’s former Beverly Hills mansion, where Kris Humphries proposed to her on camera in 2011, is heading to the market for nearly $8.5 million after an extensive makeover. Kim bought the property for $3.4 million in 2010 and sold it for $3.6 million in 2013. The five-bedroom estate now boasts luxurious modern interiors.

stories.title: Washington court broadens rules on divorce legal fees
stories.summary: Washington's Court of Appeals ruled that trial courts can award legal fees despite prenuptial agreements. This decision allows judges to consider broader divorce aspects for fee awards. In the case reviewed, a wealthy husband was ordered to pay his wife's legal costs. The trial court is to reassess the specific fee awards granted to the wife.

stories.title: Once homeless himself, he is on a mission to end food insecurity
stories.summary: Dion Dawson founded Dion's Chicago Dream in 2020 to provide fresh produce to families facing food insecurity. After experiencing homelessness and food scarcity, he aimed to improve food distribution methods. The non-profit now delivers 80,000 pounds of fresh produce weekly to over 5,400 households. Paid staff members maintain a steady workforce while providing dignity to recipients through efficient service.

stories.title: He survived Hiroshima, returned home to Nagasaki and was hit by a second atomic bomb three days later: The story of Tsutomu Yamaguchi
stories.summary: Tsutomu Yamaguchi, a survivor of both atomic bombings, faced immense physical and emotional trauma from his experiences. Initially reluctant to share his story, he eventually became an advocate for a world free of nuclear weapons. His journey from hibakusha to spokesperson illustrates the lasting impact of nuclear warfare on individuals and communities.

stories.title: 'Memory of the world': Rajatarangini, Mahabharata & Arthashastra get UN recognition
stories.summary: Three significant works from India's literary heritage have been added to Unesco's Memory of the World Regional Register. Kalhana's 'Rajatarangini', the 'Mahabharata', and Kautilya's 'Arthashastra' received this recognition recently. These inscriptions reflect various aspects of India's intellectual traditions, including historical writing and governance. This announcement follows India's previous regional register recognitions in 2024 for other literary works. The initiative aims to preserve and digitise India's manuscript heritage for future generations.

Cabinet approves Rs 14,500 crore VGF scheme for energy storage

Delhi riots case: Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam challenge Delhi HC's bail refusal in Supreme Court
stories.summary: Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam have filed for bail in the Supreme Court concerning the Delhi riots case. They contend that the prosecution has failed to call any witnesses during their extensive period of detention. The activists pointed out the looming deadline for submitting new bail applications as established by the Supreme Court.

Eight Lakshmis, 1.4 billion oceans: Aruna Lohia Goenka's vision of an awakened Bharat
Indian Medical Association wants CBFC to refuse certification to Sunny Deol film ‘Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak’
stories.summary: The IMA wants the board to refuse certification to any trailer, teaser or promotional material that shows violence against doctors, nurses or hospital staff, or carries dialogue imputing corruption to doctors as a class.

stories.title: Hardeep Singh Puri elected unopposed to Rajya Sabha from Madhya Pradesh
stories.summary: Hardeep Singh Puri was elected unopposed to the Rajya Sabha from Madhya Pradesh after other candidates failed to qualify. The nominations of Rajkumar Lohani and Kante Sayanna were rejected for not meeting necessary requirements. Puri's election follows the resignation of Union minister of state L Murugan in mid-October. Hemant Khandelwal, among other officials, was present when Puri collected his election certificate.

Scottish rescuer fights to keep badger cub he says cannot survive in the wild
‘If death is my destiny’: Sheikh Hasina firm on returning to Bangladesh in December
stories.summary: Sheikh Hasina has confirmed her intention to return to Bangladesh, despite facing a death sentence. The former Prime Minister is aware of the risks associated with her return, including potential arrest or worse. Hasina's Awami League party has been banned, resulting in widespread political repression and violence against its members. She expressed concerns over the rising influence of extremist groups in the current political climate.

stories.title: US midterm fallout: Trump's India envoy Sergio Gor may replace Marco Rubio - report
Classroom to billion-dollar fortune: How Chinese siblings struck gold in the stock market
stories.summary: Michael Mai and his sister, Mai Huixia, reached billionaire status following the public debut of Crown New Materials Technology on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, where shares surged nearly eightfold in just one day. This company, known for producing adhesives for major clients like Tesla and Apple, prompted a call for rational investment behavior amidst recent challenges and government interventions in China's stock market.

stories.title: Jantar Mantar violence: SC gives panel 1 month to file report, flags lack of complaints
US woman says co-op staff took her pets, hid dog's whereabouts; court allows lawsuit
stories.summary: A New York woman who accused co-op employees of entering her apartment without permission, removing her dog and cat, and concealing her dog's whereabouts can continue pursuing two legal claims. Nearly three years after the incident, an appeals court allowed her trespass and emotional distress claims to proceed. Court records indicated that her dog was euthanised after spending nearly two months at a shelter.

stories.title: Small Listing Spurs Protection: Indiana saves 3,950 acres; new wildlife area opens
stories.summary: An effort to save a 191-acre parcel in Indiana led to the protection of nearly 4,000 acres. The land was acquired to prevent fragmentation and protect wildlife habitats in the area. Various organizations and public agencies collaborated to complete the acquisition. The Busseron Creek Fish and Wildlife Area opened to the public in April 2025 for outdoor recreation.

stories.title: Titanic's owners received $5 million within 30 days of the sinking; 114 years later, original insurance certificate resurfaces and could sell for $67,000
stories.summary: An authentic insurance document related to the Titanic's last journey is slated for auction in Britain. This significant paperwork details the insurance sought mere weeks before the 1912 sinking. The owners received their payout shortly after the tragedy, contrasting sharply with the delays faced by bereaved families. The piece also underscores the important insurance arrangements for the Titanic, along with a selection of other artifacts that commemorate its storied past.

stories.title: Youth Congress suspends 200 office-bearers across 7 states for skipping INDIA bloc anti-CEC rally
'Contemplating to appoint a committee': Centre to SC on UGC's equity rules
Russell Brand Trial: Jury weighs seven sexual offence charges; deliberations to resume Wednesday
stories.summary: Jury discussions are now underway regarding comedian Russell Brand's sexual offences trial at Southwark Crown Court. Faced with multiple charges from six women about occurrences between 1999 and 2009, the prosecution argues that Brand leveraged his celebrity status for sexual manipulation. In his defense, Brand asserts that all encounters were consensual and refutes the allegations.

stories.title: David Bowie performed here, Carlos Sainz raced go-karts: Madrid's iconic La Ermita mall demolished for 529 homes in €77 million makeover
stories.summary: The once-thriving La Ermita shopping centre in Madrid has met its end as plans to demolish it progress. In its place, a new development will rise, offering 529 homes, a blend of accessible and protected housing. This initiative aims to enhance local infrastructure, incorporating public spaces and green zones for the community.

stories.title: EC announces electoral roll revision in 6 states, UTs; final rolls on Jan 21
Australia launches A$28 million project to stop invasive cane toads from reaching Pilbara after 1935 introduction
stories.summary: A new project involving Curtin University and Rio Tinto seeks to establish a waterless barrier for cane toads. The initiative intends to protect Western Australia's Pilbara area from the ecologically damaging species. Researchers plan to modify water sources over a significant area to prevent the toads' survival. Traditional Owners have been engaged throughout the project to ensure cultural significance is respected.

stories.title: Jimmy Buffett's $275 million family trust becomes a legal battleground
Did Russia rehearse satellite attack? Expert on close encounter with western spacecraft
stories.summary: A Russian military satellite's recent close encounter with a commercial satellite has sparked serious concerns about security in space. Experts are alarmed, suggesting this action may signal an escalation towards targeting satellites linked to military operations. US officials have warned that these provocative moves could jeopardize commercial satellite networks, further fueling the existing geopolitical tensions and prompting analysts to rigorously track Russian movements in the sky.

INDIA bloc stages mock arrest of CEC Gyanesh Kumar at Bengaluru protest: Watch
Woman's wedding falls apart, 11 strangers join her for a 'non-wedding' in Northern Ireland
stories.summary: After her fiance suffered a medical emergency and their wedding plans fell apart, Bridget Devaney invited 11 women she had never met to join her on a trip to Northern Ireland. The women, from the US, Canada and Wales, spent a week exploring popular attractions and celebrating her 'non-wedding'. What began as an online invitation turned into unexpected friendships and plans for future trips.

Kanye West's 6,713-acre Wyoming ranch returns to family that owned it for generations
stories.summary: In 2019, Kanye West acquired the Bighorn Mountain Ranch, visualizing it as an exclusive retreat. However, with shifting priorities, the Flitner family reacquired the property in 2025. Concerns over potential subdivision led them to prioritize agricultural preservation and landscape protection, ensuring that historic structures could be restored and serve as a lasting connection to the land for future generations.

'Respect seniors, end BJP-RSS hatred': Rijiju's seven-point advice to Rahul Gandhi
Centre proposes immediate suspension of licences for substandard drugs
stories.summary: The Health Ministry has introduced new regulations aimed at suspending manufacturing licenses for medicines that do not meet quality criteria. This swift action is intended to stop subpar drugs from reaching patients and to minimize their circulation during the regulatory review. Licenses can be suspended based on government analysts' findings that indicate deficiencies.

stories.title: Changing NEET-PG to rank-based system won’t fix structural problems, doctors say
stories.summary: Altering the merit-list approach for NEET-PG and NEET-SS without resolving core structural issues proves to be insufficient. In a recent meeting, stakeholders voiced concerns regarding excessive fees, low stipends, and compulsory bonds. The government primarily pointed to state authority on these matters, indicating a need for greater regulation. Attendees advocated for improved faculty hiring, fair stipends, and independent audits to enhance the quality of medical education.

stories.title: Noida airport among 10 new gateways proposed for drug imports
NDC draws line between general and specialist dental practice
Crude crashes below $100: Brent, WTI hit over two-month lows after midterm elections
stories.summary: Oil prices experienced a notable downturn, with Brent crude slipping below $95 and WTI declining beneath $90. This trend follows substantial losses from earlier sessions, influenced by the political shifts stemming from the US midterm elections. The election results could reshape President Donald Trump's stance towards the Iran conflict, opening doors for potential negotiations.

'Bye bye, Bo': Raja Krishnamoorthi takes a dig at Republican after Texas election defeat
US man who killed 2 children in house fire among 3 set to be executed on same day
10 SDRF personnel missing as boats capsize during Telangana rescue operation
TikTok Balance Exposed: Kai Cenat accidentally shows $23,232 on LIVE; sparks creator earnings debate
stories.summary: Kai Cenat accidentally revealed a $23,232.11 TikTok creator balance during a November 3 livestream with Detroit entertainer Looze Cannon. The 30-minute session reportedly generated another $7,000 to $7,300 through virtual gifts. Their TikTok LIVE battle saw Cenat receive over 200,000 gifts, while Cannon collected more than 1.4 million. The unexpected reveal sparked conversations about livestream earnings and the growing business of online entertainment.

Rare 1867 silver coin made for China trade sells for $4.75 million at Hong Kong auction; collection fetches nearly $32 million
stories.summary: A rare silver coin, crafted over 150 years ago, fetched an astonishing $4.758 million at a Hong Kong auction. This exceptional piece was part of the proposed Kwan Ping Trade Coinage aimed at solidifying trade currency standards in China. Hidden from public view since the mid-20th century, its mystery adds to its allure.

Mining heiress pledges A$120 million to 10 environmental groups, including A$25 M to Greenpeace
stories.summary: In a groundbreaking move, an Australian mining heiress and her spouse have gifted A$120 million to ten environmental organizations nationwide, marking one of the most significant private donations for conservation in Australian history. Among the beneficiaries, Greenpeace Australia Pacific will receive A$25 million, enabling it to enhance campaigns and engage in lengthy legal battles. This funding represents a transformative approach to how mining revenue supports environmental efforts.

stories.title: Florida shooting: 2 dead after gunfire reported at Citibank office complex
NJ homeowner wins $173,000 after court upholds award over a neglected oak tree that crushed her home
stories.summary: In a remarkable case in New Jersey, a homeowner secured $173,000 in damages after an oak tree, reported multiple times as hazardous, fell and damaged her property. The nearby utility company was found negligent in maintaining the tree. Following a favorable jury ruling, the appeals court affirmed the decision, underscoring the obligation of the utility company to address known risks.

stories.title: Two scrap collectors die in Srinagar fire, CM Omar Abdullah announces Rs 4L relief
Srinagar MP’s exit part of BJP’s ‘Op Lotus’ plan in J&K, says NC
Florida-based cruise ship company promised never-ending voyage, took tens of thousands of dollars from passengers, then abandoned them in Cambodia citing fuel costs
Pennsylvania approves zoning for a $1.4B data center project involving 194 families and 4,466 acres
stories.summary: In Salem Township, local officials have greenlighted a significant new zoning plan to establish a technology and energy campus. This ambitious $1.4 billion development will span 4,466 acres, affecting 194 families in the area. Alongside the main project, amenities such as a micro-hospital and recreational spaces are promised to enhance community welfare. However, property transfers will require further environmental assessments and reviews before finalization.

stories.title: Fremont Hindu temple responds to reports of 25 noise complaints, reveals names of Indian couple who apparently filed objection; says 'we attempted to arrange meetings'
Judge approves $650,000 settlement for 100 workers after alleged $1.3M retirement savings loss
stories.summary: In an important ruling, a federal judge in North Carolina approved a settlement totaling up to $650,000 for employees of Republic Mortgage. This decision follows allegations of mishandled retirement savings during the firm's closure, affecting around 100 workers who incurred notable financial losses. The settlement not only provides compensation but also includes the costs of legal fees and administrative tasks, concluding the 2024 case without the company acknowledging any misdeeds.

stories.title: Trump’s ‘Freedom In Space’ signals new contest for Moon; India’s challenge is safeguarding strategic autonomy
Midterm gamble, sliding stocks: Elon Musk's pricey election hangover continues
US job openings jump to 7.52 million as layoffs fall, but hiring remains slow
stories.summary: By September 2026, job vacancies in the United States climbed to an astonishing 7.52 million, demonstrating resilient hiring across various sectors, especially in public services. Interestingly, layoffs dropped while voluntary quits spiked, notably in the accommodation and food services industry. Recent revisions to employment statistics revealed higher job openings and hiring for August 2026. Expect the US Bureau of Labor Statistics to disclose October's numbers on December 1, 2026.

Mahadev betting app co-promoter Ravi Uppal arrested in UAE, India to extradite him
stories.summary: Uppal, 46, was taken into custody by authorities in Dubai on the basis of an Interpol Red Notice issued at the request of Indian investigating agencies, officials told PTI. The CBI and the ED are now coordinating efforts to secure his extradition to India. Investigators have also alleged that Uppal, like Chandrakar, secured a passport from Vanuatu, an island country in the South Pacific.

stories.title: UN report finds huge gap in adaptation finance ahead of COP31
stories.summary: Developing nations require approximately $305 billion annually by 2035 for climate change adaptation efforts. Rich countries' collective pledge could only reach $85-120 billion each year by 2035. While current financial contributions are around $28.2-31.7 billion, this is still inadequate. UN Environment Programme emphasizes the urgent need for increased adaptation financing and overcoming institutional barriers. Action on climate adaptation is essential to mitigate worsening impacts from extreme weather events.

stories.title: CBI successfully extradites sexual assault accused from UAE after Interpol Red Notice
'Normalise, recognise and formalise': Nadda accuses Congress of opposing SIR to legitimise outsiders, destabilise country
stories.summary: Union health minister JP Nadda accused the Congress party of opposing the Special Intensive Revision of voter lists. He alleged that their actions are aimed at protecting outsiders who support their political ambitions. Nadda criticized the Congress for undermining the credibility of the Election Commission when faced with electoral losses. He noted that the current electoral process includes Booth Level Officers facilitating voter registration door-to-door.
